Nvidia posts $96.2 billion quarter as AI demand more than doubles revenue
Revenue jumped 106% year over year, and the chipmaker is guiding for roughly $108 billion next quarter
Nvidia just reported $96.2 billion in quarterly revenue, a 106% increase from the same period a year ago. For context, that single quarter equals nearly half of what the company earned across its entire previous fiscal year.
The company isn’t easing off, either. Nvidia expects next quarter to land at approximately $108 billion, which suggests the appetite for AI computing still hasn’t been satisfied.
The numbers behind the quarter
The results cover the second quarter of Nvidia’s fiscal 2027, which closed on July 26, 2026. Revenue grew 18% from the prior quarter on top of the 106% annual gain.
The engine, once again, was the Data Center segment. It brought in $89.0 billion, up 117% from a year earlier.
Put plainly, the business that sells chips and systems for training and running AI models now makes up the overwhelming majority of the company. More than nine of every ten revenue dollars came from that one division this quarter.
Profitability held up as well. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share came in at $2.22, up 120% year over year, while gross margin stayed at 75%.
Guidance and the “inflection point” pitch
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, Nvidia guided revenue to approximately $108 billion, plus or minus 2%. Gross margin is expected to come in around 74%, give or take 50 basis points.

CEO Jensen Huang framed the moment in sweeping terms. He described the AI sector as having reached an inflection point, with AI capabilities becoming more productive and more valuable.
Huang also offered a longer-range view. He projected revenue growth of roughly 70% for fiscal 2028, a figure he characterized as supply-constrained.
That outlook sits well above where Wall Street had been. Analysts had previously expected growth of about 44% for that year.
How we got here
The latest quarter builds on an already enormous fiscal 2026. Nvidia posted total revenue of $215.9 billion for that year, up 65% from the year before.
Data Center accounted for around 90% of fiscal 2026 revenue.
What this means
The most important signal here may be the gap between Huang’s 70% outlook and the 44% analysts had penciled in. When a company’s own forecast runs that far ahead of the Street, estimates typically get revisited.
The supply-constrained label cuts both ways. On one hand, it implies demand is outrunning what Nvidia can deliver, which supports pricing power and those 75% margins. On the other, it means results depend heavily on manufacturing capacity and the supply chain behind it.
The margin guidance is a smaller detail with real weight. A move from 75% to around 74% is modest, but it is worth tracking over the next few quarters.
The next checkpoint is the third quarter. Hitting the $108 billion target, within the 2% range Nvidia gave, would reinforce the case that the inflection point Huang described is showing up in actual sales.

Why Nvidia at 13 Times Expected Earnings Still Isn’t Cheap
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA | NVDA Price Prediction) trades at $186.64. A forward multiple near 13 only looks cheap if Wall Street’s earnings forecasts hold up through the next phase of the AI expansion.
Nvidia makes the accelerators, networking gear and CUDA software at the center of AI data centers. Fiscal second-quarter revenue reached $96.22 billion, up 105.8%, and Data Center sales rose 117% to $89.02 billion. Still, the stock fell 21.4% over the past month during a broad chip selloff that Barron’s described as leaving chip stocks at fire-sale prices.
Demand Outruns Supply at 13x Forward Earnings
Bulls point to estimates that keep rising. The consensus for fiscal 2028 EPS is $15.9146 from 52 analysts, up from $12.8148 90 days ago, with zero downward revisions in the past month. Management expects revenue to grow about 70% in fiscal 2028 and calls that outlook supply-constrained, because customer demand is growing roughly 100%.
Vera Rubin raises revenue per gigawatt to $40 billion from $25 billion for Blackwell. Nvidia has also beaten EPS and revenue estimates in six straight quarters and has $99 billion left on its buyback authorization.
Forecasts Built on Financing Can Reset Quickly
A forward P/E rests on forecasts, and Nvidia’s forecasts depend on AI infrastructure spending continuing at a historic pace across Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle. If expected earnings fell 30% with the share price unchanged, the multiple would rise to about 18. A 40% cut would push it to about 21. The low-end fiscal 2028 estimate of $12.8484 already implies roughly 15 times earnings.
The balance sheet is also taking on more risk. Supply commitments rose to $279 billion, guarantee obligations reach $108.5 billion, and days sales outstanding stretched to 60 days from 45. Nvidia has invested nearly $50 billion in frontier AI labs, an arrangement CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged some call “circular financing.” Gross margin is expected to bottom at 71% to 72% in the fiscal fourth quarter, and the outlook includes no China data center compute revenue. Microsoft’s reported decision against extending an Oracle cloud arrangement built on older Nvidia chips shows how fast computing needs turn over.
Third-Quarter Results Will Settle the Debate
Execution remains strong, while the growing role of financing raises valuation risk. The fiscal third-quarter earnings report later this month tests revenue against guidance of $108.0 billion, gross margin against 74.0%, and whether management confirms its fiscal 2028 growth target.
Analysts See 75% Upside as Shares Lag the S&P 500
The average analyst target of $327.14 implies about 75% upside from $186.64. Targets are one data point and guarantee nothing. Of 62 analysts covering the stock:
- Strong Buy: 10
- Buy: 49
- Hold: 2
- Sell: 1
Nvidia is up 0.31% so far this year, and the S&P 500 has gained 7.83%. Over one year, the stock is down 0.53% against the index’s 9.69% gain. Its beta of 2.247 means the stock tends to move more than twice as much as the broader market.
Estimates Must Prove Durable Before Nvidia Looks Cheap
At $186.64, Nvidia’s valuation depends on whether estimates hold.
The multiple only looks low if the estimates behind it hold. Readers should look for three signals in the upcoming earnings report: revenue above guidance, gross margin tracking toward management’s floor, and days sales outstanding no longer rising. If all three appear and fiscal 2028 estimates keep rose, the case for owning the stock improves. If guidance falls, or more of the business depends on Nvidia’s own balance sheet, the bear case improves.
Upside surprises can move the stock fast. A strong report could quickly lift a stock that has dropped 8.8% in a week. Evaluating the stock before the report means relying on forecasts that can be cut far faster than the business can rebuild them.
At 13 times forecasts that depend on borrowed AI capital, one more quarter of results will show whether the stock is truly cheap.

Why Is Nvidia Stock Falling? Jensen Huang’s Exit Triggers Fresh Selling
Nvidia (NVDA) stock is facing renewed selling pressure after CEO Jensen Huang stepped down on November 12, with CFO Colette Kress appointed interim chief executive as the company searches for a successor. The leadership shake-up has raised concerns about Nvidia’s strategic direction and its role in financing parts of the AI infrastructure ecosystem. Wall Street’s caution has added to the pressure: Baird cut its price target from $500 to $200, citing leadership uncertainty, potential US export restrictions and slower AI infrastructure spending. Investors are now looking to Nvidia’s November 17 earnings report for clarity on demand and its forward outlook.
CoinPedia’s Nvidia Stock Price Prediction for 2026
Fundamental Analysis
Nvidia’s fundamental strength is increasingly concentrated in its Data Center business, which has become the primary driver of revenue and earnings. The company generated $215.9 billion in FY2026 revenue, while Q1 FY2027 revenue reached a record $81.6 billion. Data Center revenue accounted for $75.2 billion, rising 92% year over year, reflecting continued demand for accelerated computing, AI infrastructure and networking.
The valuation debate now centers on the durability of that growth at Nvidia’s scale. Management’s Q2 FY2027 revenue outlook of approximately $91 billion points to continued demand, but investors will increasingly focus on Blackwell and Rubin adoption, hyperscaler capital expenditure, gross margins and competition from custom AI accelerators.
For NVDA to reach a $6 trillion valuation, sustained earnings growth will be the critical variable. The company must continue expanding revenue and profitability fast enough to support a higher market capitalization without relying solely on multiple expansion.
Technical Analysis:
Nvidia stock could remain under pressure through November after falling below its $190–$200 support zone. The recent breakdown, accompanied by elevated selling volume, points to weakening short-term momentum. If NVDA fails to reclaim $200, the stock could test the $160–$175 range. A sustained recovery above $190–$200 would improve the outlook and open the way toward $215–$220. However, a stronger bullish reversal would require the stock to regain its short-term moving averages and attract fresh buying interest.
For 2026, CoinPedia projects NVDA to trade between $210 and $320, with an average target of $290. The bullish case depends on Nvidia converting continued AI infrastructure spending into earnings growth, while the technical setup will remain constructive above the $203-$209 support region. A failure to hold that zone would delay the upside thesis and increase the probability of a deeper consolidation.
NVDA Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Nvidia’s Upcoming Results
Nvidia is scheduled to release its Q3 FY2027 earnings on November 17, 2026, after the U.S. market closes. Wall Street expects revenue of approximately $109 billion, representing growth of around 91% year over year, while adjusted earnings are projected at $2.47 per share, compared with $1.30 a year earlier.
The results will put Nvidia’s AI growth story under fresh scrutiny. Investors will focus on data-center revenue, demand for Blackwell systems, gross margins and management’s forward guidance. Nvidia generated $89 billion in data-center revenue in the previous quarter, making continued AI infrastructure spending a key measure of business momentum.

What Does Nvidia Stock Price Depend On?
Nvidia’s valuation is primarily tied to the pace of AI infrastructure spending, its ability to convert demand into revenue and earnings, and its ability to maintain technological leadership. As its Data Center business has become the dominant revenue driver, changes in hyperscaler spending, product cycles, margins and investor expectations can have a significant impact on NVDA’s stock price.
AI & Data Center Spending: Capital expenditure by hyperscalers and enterprises remains the biggest demand driver for Nvidia’s GPUs, networking and accelerated-computing platforms.
Blackwell & Rubin Adoption: The pace of deployment of Nvidia’s latest and next-generation AI platforms will influence revenue growth and the strength of future product cycles.
Earnings & Profit Margins: Revenue growth, operating leverage and gross margins directly influence earnings expectations and the valuation investors are willing to assign to NVDA.
Hyperscaler Demand: Spending from major cloud providers and large AI developers can materially affect Nvidia’s order pipeline and Data Center growth.
AI Chip Competition: Custom AI accelerators and competing products could pressure Nvidia’s market share, pricing power and margins over time.
Export Restrictions: U.S. semiconductor export controls, particularly those affecting advanced AI chips, can restrict Nvidia’s addressable market and increase regulatory uncertainty.
Supply Chain & Manufacturing: Advanced-node production capacity, packaging availability and supply-chain execution remain important factors in Nvidia’s ability to meet AI chip demand.
Valuation & Investor Expectations: At Nvidia’s current scale, the stock increasingly depends on whether earnings growth can justify its valuation. Even strong results can trigger a sell-off if they fall short of elevated expectations.
Interest Rates & Market Liquidity: Higher interest rates can compress valuation multiples for high-growth technology stocks, while stronger liquidity and risk appetite can support expansion.
Technology Leadership: Nvidia’s CUDA ecosystem, accelerated-computing architecture, networking products and rapid product launches remain critical to defending its competitive position as the AI semiconductor market evolves.
Ultimately, NVDA’s stock price depends on three variables: how fast AI spending grows, how efficiently Nvidia converts that spending into earnings, and how much investors are willing to pay for that growth.
How CoinPedia Generated NVDA Stock Price Predictions
Nvidia operates at the center of the AI semiconductor market, making its long-term valuation closely linked to AI infrastructure spending, earnings growth, product adoption and technological execution. Rather than relying solely on historical price movements, CoinPedia’s NVDA stock price prediction combines fundamental performance, technical market structure, industry growth and broader market conditions to estimate Nvidia’s potential valuation across different time horizons.
Business Growth & Earnings Drivers
Our analysis focuses on the factors directly influencing Nvidia’s earnings trajectory, including Data Center demand, AI accelerator adoption, Blackwell and Rubin platform sales, networking growth, gross margins, operating leverage and hyperscaler capital expenditure. Nvidia’s ability to convert sustained AI demand into revenue and free cash flow remains central to its long-term valuation.
Competitive Position & AI Leadership
Nvidia’s valuation is assessed against its position within the global AI semiconductor industry. We evaluate its CUDA software ecosystem, accelerated-computing architecture, networking portfolio, product roadmap and competitive position against custom AI chips and rival accelerator platforms. Sustaining technological leadership remains critical to supporting premium valuation multiples.
Technical Market Structure

These signals help identify breakout levels, accumulation zones and potential price targets across different investment horizons.
AI Industry & Macroeconomic Environment
The forecast also incorporates broader variables including hyperscaler AI spending, semiconductor demand, interest-rate expectations, market liquidity, export restrictions, supply-chain conditions and investor sentiment toward high-growth technology stocks. These factors can influence both Nvidia’s earnings outlook and the valuation multiple investors assign to future growth.
Conclusion
Nvidia’s next major stock-price move will depend on whether its exceptional AI-driven growth can continue at increasingly larger revenue and earnings levels. The critical variables are Data Center demand, Blackwell and Rubin adoption, margins and hyperscaler spending, not simply the broader AI narrative.
With NVDA approaching its $236.54 record high, the technical setup adds another important catalyst. A sustained breakout could open the door to new price discovery, while failure to clear resistance would keep the stock vulnerable to another consolidation phase. If Nvidia continues delivering earnings growth at a pace capable of supporting higher valuations, the $6 trillion market-cap milestone becomes a measurable outcome of sustained execution rather than a purely speculative target.

Nvidia remains one of the strongest large-cap AI infrastructure plays, supported by Data Center growth, accelerated computing, networking and its CUDA ecosystem. However, the stock’s valuation reflects high growth expectations, making earnings execution, AI spending and margins critical to its future performance.

Yes. A sustained breakout above the $236.54 record high could put NVDA into price discovery, with $250 as the first major psychological level and $275-$300 as the next upside zone.
4. What factors could drive NVDA stock higher?
Continued hyperscaler AI spending, strong Blackwell and Rubin adoption, rising AI inference demand, Data Center growth, expanding networking revenue and sustained profit margins could support further upside in NVDA.
5. Can Nvidia become the first $6 trillion company?
Nvidia could reach a $6 trillion market capitalization if earnings continue expanding at a pace that supports a substantially higher valuation. The key requirement is sustained revenue and profit growth rather than multiple expansion alone.

content:
[11/15] The Eve of Nvidia's Earnings and the Reality of Demand as Shown by Japan's Supply Chain
Click here for Spotify / Apple Podcasts
On November 12, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang has stepped down as President, CEO, and Director, and that Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO. The earnings report for the period from August to October will be released early on the morning of November 18. Looking at the earnings of Japanese semiconductor-related companies since the end of October, ahead of Nvidia's results, we see record-high performance across inspection equipment, manufacturing equipment, substrates, electronic components, and memory. Nvidia's supply contracts have ballooned to $279 billion, and the company is directly investing capital into the production capacity of its partners. This report covers Nvidia's current situation and the focus of its earnings, the earnings content of various Japanese companies, the concentration of profits in memory, the funding burden of AI investment, market reactions and overseas perspectives, and explains the branching paths for future developments.
Changes in Nvidia's Management Structure and the Focus of Earnings
According to an 8-K filed by Nvidia with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 12, Mr. Huang stepped down as President, CEO, and Director on that date. Ms. Kress has become interim CEO and will continue to serve as CFO until a successor is found. The Board of Directors stated it will search for a successor both internally and externally and has appointed Harvey Jones as the company's first Chairman of the Board. The company did not provide a reason for the departure and explained that operations, commitments to customers, and the product roadmap will continue without interruption. Al Jazeera reported on November 13 that the company's stock fell more than 14% at one point on the 12th.
Results from May to July
- Revenue: $96.2 billion
- 106% increase year-over-year
- Data Center: $89.0 billion
- Gross Margin: 75.0%
- Adjusted Earnings Per Share: $2.22
Company Outlook for August to October
- Revenue: $108.0 billion
- Revenue range: +/- 2%
- Gross Margin: 74.0%
- Adjusted Operating Expenses: Approximately $9.0 billion
According to the earnings materials released on August 27, data center revenue increased by 117% year-over-year. The outlook for August to October assumes zero revenue from computing products for data centers in China. Finviz reported on November 11 that market expectations are for earnings per share of $2.49 and revenue of approximately $109 billion. Market expectations are slightly above the midpoint of the company's outlook, and the focus will be on where the final figures land within the range and the trend in gross margins.
CFO Comments Indicate Ties to the Supply Chain
The comments from the Chief Financial Officer, released by Nvidia alongside the earnings, contain figures that illustrate the company's relationships with its partners.
Changes in Lending Relationships
- Inventory: $25.8 billion → $31.6 billion
- Supply obligations: $119 billion → $279 billion
- Accounts receivable: $63.1 billion
- Days sales outstanding: 45 days → 60 days
The increase in inventory is in preparation for the launch of the next-generation Blackwell product. The increase in supply obligations is primarily due to memory procurement, with $92 billion to be paid over the remainder of fiscal year 2027. Regarding the lengthening of the accounts receivable collection period, the company explains that it is due to extended payment terms in multi-quarter contracts with large investment-grade customers.
The fact that supply obligations more than doubled in a single quarter means that Nvidia is securing future components and production capacity. From the perspective of Japanese suppliers, these are figures that underpin order and production plans. On the other hand, the lengthening of the accounts receivable collection period indicates a structure in which Nvidia is partially absorbing the financial burden of data center investments on the customer side.
https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_financials/2027/Q227/Q2FY27-CFO-Commentary.pdf
Advantest and Tokyo Electron: Record-High Performance for Equipment Manufacturers
Major companies in inspection and manufacturing equipment are both showing performance at record-high levels.
Advantest First Half
- Revenue: 845.2 billion yen
- Operating profit: 456.8 billion yen
- Profit before tax: 510.2 billion yen
- Net profit attributable to parent company: 368.1 billion yen
Advantest Full-Year Forecast
- Revenue: 1.714 trillion yen → 1.863 trillion yen
- Operating profit: 846 billion yen → 967 billion yen
- Net profit: 660 billion yen → 741.5 billion yen
According to the financial results summary released on October 28, first-half revenue increased by 60.5% year-on-year, and operating profit increased by 96.5%. Profit before tax includes approximately 57 billion yen in financial income, such as valuation gains on strategic investments. The test system business recorded revenue of 770.2 billion yen and segment profit of 455.6 billion yen, with growth in testers for DRAM and non-volatile memory in addition to SoC testers for AI. SoCs are semiconductors that integrate many functions into a single chip, and the increase in production volume and structural complexity of AI chips are boosting inspection demand. The overseas revenue ratio is 99.4%, and the average exchange rate for the first half was 160 yen to the dollar, which was weaker than the 146 yen of the previous year. The second half assumes a rate of 150 yen.
Media IR reported on October 29 that the company is expected to achieve its annual production capacity target of 10,000 SoC testers well ahead of schedule. The interim dividend is 49 yen, and the share buyback limit is a maximum of 280 billion yen.
Tokyo Electron's First Half
- Revenue: 1.6675 trillion yen
- Operating Profit: 506.8 billion yen
- Net Profit: 376.9 billion yen
Tokyo Electron's Full-Year Forecast
- Revenue: 3.7 trillion yen
- Operating Profit: 1.169 trillion yen
- Net Profit: 865 billion yen
In the financial results on October 30, first-half revenue increased by 41.3% year-on-year, and operating profit increased by 67.2%. According to Kabucho, the operating profit margin for the July-September quarter alone was 31.6%. The full-year forecast was provided for the first time this time, with operating profit expected to increase by 87.1% compared to the previous fiscal year. The second half assumes that operating profit will increase by about 30% compared to the first half. Demand for equipment is expanding in both inspection and manufacturing processes, confirming a structure where the increase in production volume of semiconductors for AI is boosting the performance of equipment manufacturers.
https://www.advantest.com/ja/news/2026/mpd9kn0000000ger-att/J_FR_FY2026_2Q.pdf
Ibiden and Murata Manufacturing: Investment in Increasing Production of Substrates and Components
Demand for AI servers is also boosting performance in substrates and electronic components.
Ibiden's Full-Year Forecast
- Revenue: 550 billion yen → 565 billion yen
- Operating Profit: 127 billion yen → 133 billion yen
- Net Profit: 84 billion yen → 89 billion yen
Ibiden announced its second upward revision for the current fiscal year on October 29. Taiwan's TechNews reported on October 30 that the revised net profit exceeded the market consensus of 87.7 billion yen compiled by Reuters. The company has also decided on an additional investment of approximately 151 billion yen to increase production of high-performance IC package substrates for AI servers and CPUs. Operations are scheduled to begin sequentially from fiscal year 2029. President Koji Kawashima expressed the view that semiconductor demand will remain strong until around 2030 and that substrates could become a bottleneck in semiconductor production.

Reliance Industries Q2 Results Highlights: Net profit jumps 34% on refining, digital gains; revenue hits record
Reliance Industries Q2 Results Highlights: The Oil and Gas business reported revenue of ₹6,020 crore, compared with ₹6,298 crore in the previous quarter and ₹6,058 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA stood at ₹4,901 crore, against ₹4,973 crore sequentially and ₹5,002 crore year-on-year. EBITDA margin was 81.4%, compared with 79% in the previous quarter and 82.6% in the corresponding quarter las
Consolidated revenue rose to ₹3.62 lakh crore from ₹3.40 lakh crore sequentially and ₹2.84 lakh crore year-on-year, marking the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and its strongest-ever quarterly performance. Consolidated EBITDA margin stood at 18.8%, compared with 17.3% in the previous quarter and 19.5% in the corresponding quarter last year.
Reliance Industries' Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C) business reported revenue of ₹2.32 lakh crore, compared with ₹2.02 lakh crore in the previous quarter and ₹1.61 lakh crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA rose to ₹25,203 crore from ₹17,010 crore sequentially and ₹15,008 crore year-on-year. EBITDA margin improved to 10.9% from 8.4% in the previous quarter and 9.3% a year earlier.
The Oil and Gas business reported revenue of ₹6,020 crore, compared with ₹6,298 crore in the previous quarter and ₹6,058 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA stood at ₹4,901 crore, against ₹4,973 crore sequentially and ₹5,002 crore year-on-year. EBITDA margin was 81.4%, compared with 79% in the previous quarter and 82.6% in the corresponding quarter last year.
Watch this space for all the highlights on Reliance Industries' Q2 results.
Thank you for joining our coverage of Reliance Industries Q2 Results
We will now wrap up the blog. Good night, folks!
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Retail Q2 Results: Gross revenue grows 6.4%
Reliance Retail Ventures (RRVL), the retail arm of Reliance Industries, reported a 6.4% year-on-year (YoY) increase in gross revenue to ₹91,716 crore in the September quarter, adjusted for the demerger of its Consumer Brands business. The company’s performance was impacted by the shift in the festive calendar to the December quarter. Read more here.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Jio Platforms Q2 profit jumps nearly 14%, broadband base crosses 30 million
Two days after its blockbuster stock market debut, Jio Platforms reported a net profit of ₹8,389 crore in the second quarter of FY27, up 13.7% from ₹7,379 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Gross revenue for the quarter stood at ₹47,485 crore, up 11.3% from ₹42,652 crore in the year-ago period and 3.3% from ₹45,961 crore in the previous quarter. Read more here
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance oil-to-chemicals profitability hits an all-time high
Reliance Industries (RIL) reported a record quarterly operating performance for its core oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business in the second quarter ended September 30, with segment EBITDA surging 67.9% year-on-year to an all-time high of ₹25,203 crore. Read more here
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Piyush Pandey, Research Analyst at Centrum Broking, on Jio Platforms Q2 results
“I would say Jio Platforms’ earnings are a broadly steady set of numbers. Revenue growth was primarily driven by higher customer additions and an increase in ARPU on a sequential basis. Overall, these look like in-line numbers.
So, we are building in revenue growth of close to 12%, EBITDA growth of around 13% and PAT growth of around 14-15% for the current financial year. In terms of EPS, I would say it will closely follow the PAT number. So, broadly, I would say we can expect 15% EPS growth for the full year, but it depends on the timing of the next tariff increase.”
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Deven Choksey, Managing Director of Drchoksey Finserv, on results
“I think indeed the Reliance Industries numbers are pretty handsome numbers. Frankly, I think I do recollect one of the interactions on the channel wherein I categorically stated that this quarter is possibly the best quarter that one has ever seen as far as the CRACKS margins are concerned, and particularly the diesel margins are concerned, because diesel exports to the European countries by Reliance have, actually, I think, worked in their favour significantly, as it looks like.
Of course, I need to see a lot of details before I make a qualified statement. But from the numbers that we had calculated and anticipated, I think this is clearly established. Another part, I think the company has been extremely agile in passing on the cost to their customers. When we were talking to the user industries in the petrochemicals, I think we were told that I think Reliance has been extremely quick in raising the prices based on the crude oil prices.
So, they have taken the advantage of lower inventory of crude, which they bought in, which came in transit, and I think took the advantage and created the higher delta for themselves. This is also getting reflected in the petrochemical or polyester chain margins that you are talking about. So, of course, we all want to see further details about whatever I have observed. But it appears to me that I think this is where we have made the difference, both in the refining segment as well as the petrochemical segments.
They are trying to optimise the cost in whichever format they are operating by way of rationalising the cost structures. In past, they continued with some amount of legacy effect, but in this quarter they have discarded some of the stores and formats, and that clearly gets reflected in the profit performance.
One important point I think I observed in the retail business is that somewhere around 3,500 own brands, in which I think they are operating the business, are giving them a significantly big handle in the form of getting the detailed margins. I think they can get it from the consumer company. So from that perspective, I find that the business, I think, remains absolutely strong and convincing going forward.
I think the success of JioMart is largely due to the quick commerce piece that they have added. I think we would like to see, in a different format, particularly in electronics, somewhere in this quarter, that is, the third quarter of the financial year, how exactly the numbers improve. In the second quarter, the numbers are in line with whatever I think we have been expecting, but the third quarter should be relatively better in my viewpoint. As far as I think the electronics format is concerned, the margins are apparently a little better compared to others.”
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: JioHotstar Entertainment watch-time grows over 15%
Entertainment watch-time on JioHotstar grew more than 15% year-on-year during the quarter, driven by strong performance across Hindi and regional markets. Shows such as ‘India Ke Top 1%’, ‘Khatron Ke Khiladi’, ‘Hustle Season 5’ and ‘Bhojpuri Bawaal’ contributed to JioStar’s position as India’s leading entertainment network.
‘Bigg Boss’ was launched across six languages during the quarter, with all editions collectively reaching more than 90 million viewers on JioHotstar in the first three weeks. This made it the biggest entertainment franchise on the platform. ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ was launched for the first time, with Saurav Ganguly as its host.
‘Resort’ became the most-watched show in JioHotstar’s history, supporting the platform’s Long-Running Series (LRS) strategy. The wider LRS slate also performed well, with ‘Heart Beat S3’ and ‘Court’ delivering strong early viewership as returning and new launches, respectively. ‘Thukra Ke Mera Pyaar S2’, a key Hindi LRS, recorded an increase in performance over the previous season, reinforcing the category’s role in driving platform growth.
‘Pritam & Pedro’, directed by Rajkumar Hirani, became the most successful short-running series in JioHotstar’s history.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: JioHotstar expands CTV reach
JioHotstar now has near-complete reach across the connected TV (CTV) universe, with an average CTV viewer consuming three times more content than a mobile viewer.
The streaming service was relaunched and rebranded as ‘JioHotstar’ in Singapore, the UK and Canada in September. Active subscriber volumes in these markets have grown by around 30% since the launch.
During the quarter, JioHotstar introduced ‘Pay Kisi Aur Se’ or ‘Ask Others to Pay’, an industry-first subscription payment solution that allows users to request friends or family members to complete purchases on their behalf. The solution, which aims to address payment and demographic gaps, drove a 10% increase in incremental payment initiations.
JioHotstar also extended CTV access to mobile phone plan users, allowing them to watch content on living-room devices for up to two hours every month. The move brought additional viewers to the CTV platform.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: JioStar Q2 revenue rises 10.%
JioStar reported revenue from operations of ₹6,806 crore in the second quarter of FY27, up 10.1% year-on-year, driven by growth in subscription revenue and digital entertainment advertising revenue. EBITDA from operations stood at ₹1,372 crore, with a margin of 22.1%.
During the quarter, JioStar relaunched and rebranded its digital destination as ‘JioHotstar’ in international markets, including Singapore, the UK and Canada. TV Entertainment continued to dominate the market, with the rollout of new shows across JioStar’s Hindi and regional channels.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: KGD6 produces 24 MMSCMD of gas
Reliance Industries reported average KGD6 production of 24.0 million standard cubic metres per day (MMSCMD) of gas and around 15,903 barrels per day of oil and condensate during the second quarter of FY27.
In the coal bed methane (CBM) business, the second phase of the multi-lateral well (MLW) campaign is underway to augment production. Drilling has been completed at 37 of the 40 wells planned under the campaign, of which 35 have been connected to the production system.
The current CBM production rate stands at 1.04 MMSCMD, with new wells under production making a significant contribution.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Oil and Gas Q2 EBITDA falls 2%
Reliance Industries’ oil and gas (exploration and production) segment reported a 0.6% year-on-year decline in revenue in the second quarter of FY27, mainly due to lower production and gas price realisation from KG-D6. The decline was partly offset by higher condensate prices and improved coal bed methane (CBM) gas prices and volumes.
The average price realised for KG-D6 gas stood at $8.88 per million British thermal units (MMBtu) in Q2 FY27, compared with $9.97 per MMBtu in the year-ago quarter. The average price realised for CBM gas increased to $13.24 per MMBtu from $9.53 per MMBtu.
EBITDA declined 2% YoY to ₹4,901 crore due to lower revenue and higher Government of India (GoI) levies. Favourable exchange-rate movements partly supported earnings.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Anant Ambani, Executive Director, Reliance Industries, on Q2 results
“Our O2C business has delivered its best-ever quarterly performance amid a highly volatile and challenging global environment. It is a sound testament to our operational resilience.
Our teams have exhibited excellent operational acumen along with financial astuteness. I feel honoured to be a part of this business that contributes to India’s energy stability and self-sufficiency in times of crisis. We will continue to build on our strengths, exercising operational discipline and delivering greater value.”
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Jio-bp Q2 fuel sales volume rises 4.2%
Reliance BP Mobility Ltd (RBML), which operates under the Jio-bp brand, runs a country-wide network of 2,304 retail outlets, supported by more than 5,900 electric vehicle (EV) charge points, 200 compressed biogas (CBG) and compressed natural gas (CNG) stations, and 184 convenience stores.
During the second quarter of FY27, Jio-bp maintained fuel supplies across the country amid renewed volatility in crude oil and product prices due to the Middle East disruption. The company kept its entire network fully stocked and retailed fuel at parity with the industry, ensuring uninterrupted service to customers. It continued to offer innovative products and industry-leading loyalty programmes, which have now been extended to CNG and CBG.
Jio-bp’s combined Motor Spirit (MS) and High-Speed Diesel (HSD) volumes grew 4.2% year-on-year to 1.83 million kilolitres (KL) in Q2 FY27, driven by continued momentum in petrol sales and its premium and loyalty-led retailing. Its market share increased to 5.46% in HSD and 3.86% in MS, with market effectiveness of 2.34 times and 1.72 times, respectively.
RBML’s aviation business is rebuilding aviation turbine fuel (ATF) volumes after regaining key airport allocations and re-engaging major airline customers. ATF volumes stood at 36.3 thousand kilolitres (TKL) in Q2 FY27, with a market share of 1.3%.
Under Jio-bp Pulse, electric vehicle charging volumes grew 60% YoY to 15.8 gigawatt-hours (GWh) in the quarter. The volumes were delivered through a fast-charging network of 5,943 charge points across more than 1,100 locations, with charger uptime of around 95%. Jio-bp Pulse now has partnerships with all major EV original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), expanding its participation across the electric mobility value chain.
Under its Clean N Green initiative, Jio-bp expanded its gaseous fuels network to 200 operational CBG and CNG stations. Combined volumes increased 121% YoY to 18.1 thousand metric tonnes (TMT), supported by third-party offtake agreements.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: O2C Q2 revenue jumps 44.2% to ₹2.32 lakh crore
Reliance Industries’ oil-to-chemicals (O2C) segment reported a 44.2% year-on-year increase in revenue to ₹2,31,601 crore ($24.2 billion) in the second quarter of FY27, driven by higher energy prices.
The Middle East conflict disrupted energy market supply chains, pushing crude oil prices up 40.6% and transportation fuel prices by 50-78% YoY. Revenue growth was also supported by a 25-35% increase in prices of most downstream chemical products.
Segment EBITDA surged 67.9% YoY to ₹25,203 crore ($2.6 billion), driven by unprecedented strength in transportation fuel cracks and improved downstream chemical margins. Fuel cracks increased 3-3.7 times year-on-year, reaching historic highs during the quarter. Polyester chain margins also recovered sharply to a three-year high, led by improvements in paraxylene (PX) and purified terephthalic acid (PTA) deltas.
Earnings growth was constrained by continued costs related to the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED) and under-recoveries in the Jio-bp business.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Isha Ambani, Executive Director, Reliance Retail Ventures, on results
“Our customers’ trust and continued engagement across our stores and digital platforms remain central to our growth. We are building a future-ready retail business by combining our extensive physical network with digital convenience, technology, and a deep understanding of Indian consumers.
The new model, with fast-growing Digital Commerce and B2B channels is working and funded by the profits of offline business. With continued investments in sustainable, profitable growth, we are well positioned to serve customers across India with quality, value, and choice this festive season.”
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Retail Fashion and Lifestyle Q2 LFL growth at 3%
Reliance Retail’s Fashion and Lifestyle business reported like-for-like (LFL) revenue growth of 3% year-on-year, despite the shift of major festivals to the third quarter. Apparel and Footwear stores sustained sales without the full-price festive weeks. The business launched over 250 new options every week, reinforcing its focus on fresh fashion across stores.
Own brands sustained their growth momentum, led by fresh womenswear collections and a sharper focus on evolving customer preferences. Their contribution increased by 710 basis points YoY. Digital commerce accounted for a higher share of Apparel and Footwear revenue, increasing 100 basis points year-on-year. AJIO’s catalogue grew 23% to 3.3 million options.
Tira and AJIO’s beauty category strengthened the premium beauty proposition, broadening customer reach and attracting consumers seeking premium beauty and personal care brands. Premium brands also reported growth across Eyewear, Luxury Menswear, Kidswear and Footwear. Reliance’s premium and luxury portfolio crossed 1,000 exclusive brand stores.
The company expanded its brand portfolio with the launch of Fabletics, a global active lifestyle brand, and signed an exclusive partnership with SKIMS, a global shapewear and lifestyle brand. AJIO Luxe added 22 brands, taking its portfolio to 1,040 brands.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Retail Consumer Electronics Business reports 8% LFL growth
Reliance Retail’s consumer electronics business reported like-for-like (LFL) growth of 8% year-on-year, driven by improved product availability, competitive pricing and targeted promotions.
The company is now India’s largest retailer of premium products, including mobile phones from leading brands such as Apple and Samsung. Lower margins are a strategic investment aimed at acquiring high-value customers with significant lifetime value. Omnichannel integration also expanded across Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets, improving customer experience.
ResQ delivered steady growth, completing 97% of services within 48 hours. The distribution business reported 20% YoY revenue growth, led by mobiles and laptops.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: JioMart Q2 revenue jumps 42%
JioMart reported a 42% year-on-year increase in revenue, driven by higher average order values and a 24% rise in units per order. The business is leveraging its network of over 5,000 stores across more than 1,000 cities to deepen its reach in smaller cities and towns. Free delivery encouraged customers to build larger baskets, contributing to higher average order values.
The share of digital commerce in B2C grocery revenue increased by 270 basis points YoY. The business also continued to scale quick delivery in consumer electronics while strengthening monetisation of its marketplace and seller services.
Improving dark-store productivity remains a key focus, with performance tracked by cohort to drive higher order density and reduce cost per order.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Retail grocery business reports 3% LFL growth
Reliance Retail’s grocery business delivered like-for-like (LFL) growth of 3% year-on-year while absorbing part of the input-cost inflation. The company strengthened regional customer engagement through festive-led in-store experiences around Jagannath Yatra, Ganesh Chaturthi and Janmashtami. Growth remained broad-based across Staples, Dairy, and Frozen and Bakery categories.
The company said margin recovery is expected to come from improved space productivity, optimised assortment, a focused vendor base and joint business planning with brands.
B2B revenue grew 10% YoY, supported by higher transaction volumes and average bill value. Beverages, Dairy, Frozen and Bakery, and Staples led the growth.
Targeted campaigns, including ‘METRO Ka Vaada, Fayda Sabse Zyada’ and ‘Mehangai Se Azaadi, Bachat Ki Azaadi, Vyapar Ki Tarakki’, also strengthened customer engagement.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Retail Q2 store count at 19,947
Reliance Retail opened 303 stores during the second quarter. After accounting for the closure of unproductive stores, the net reduction was 222, taking the total store count to 19,947. The company’s retail area stood at 77.5 million square feet.
The business recorded 7% year-on-year growth in transactions during the quarter, despite major festivals shifting to the third quarter, indicating continued customer engagement and growth.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Retail Q2 revenue up 6.4% to ₹91,716 crore
Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL) reported gross revenue of ₹91,716 crore for the second quarter, up 6.4% year-on-year, adjusted for the demerger of its Consumer Brands business. The business performance was impacted by the shift in the festive calendar to the third quarter.
EBITDA, before the one-time impairment charge, declined 8.6% YoY to ₹6,228 crore. The EBITDA margin stood at 7.8%, down 120 basis points, due to the planned investment phase in digital commerce, input-cost inflation absorbed for customers and the festive calendar shift.
Depreciation increased 18.1% YoY to ₹1,820 crore, driven by growth in the asset base. Finance costs rose 53.9% to ₹905 crore due to increased borrowings and higher interest rates.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Mukesh D Ambani, Chairman and Managing Director, on results
“This week marked a historic moment in Reliance’s value creation journey with Jio’s record-setting listing on Indian bourses. With over 22x subscription and strong listing appreciation, the issue has set multiple global benchmarks. JPL is now India’s second-largest company.
It demonstrates the depth of confidence investors place in Jio’s solid foundation and strong growth visibility. I am proud to witness the rejuvenation of “the equity cult” originally pioneered by our founder-chairman during the 1977Reliance IPO.
During 2Q FY27, our businesses delivered a strong performance despite a complex operating environment. Commodity markets remained volatile while geopolitical tensions continued to weigh on global supply chains. Against this backdrop, the domestic orientation of our portfolio, combined with operational discipline and versatility of our integrated businesses, helped Reliance navigate external volatility effectively.
Our O2C business delivered a particularly strong performance this quarter, led by tight fuel markets, improved downstream petrochemical deltas and firm domestic demand. Our ability to optimise feedstock sourcing and product placement along with operations across the value chain enabled us to improve
margin capture. This performance underscores the strength and resilience of our O2C business.
The Digital Services business continued its robust growth this quarter. Jio’s performance across mobility, home broadband and enterprise was strong, with healthy growth in earnings. Jio has built a proprietary technology stack and a growing portfolio of digital services, platforms and enterprise offerings that extend well beyond connectivity. The Jio IPO is a defining milestone. The faith placed in us by millions of our investors reinforces our commitment to building indigenous, world-class deep-tech solutions to deliver sustained value to customers and shareholders
Reliance Retail had a steady quarter, with growth sustained across all formats and channels. Consumer demand stayed healthy, supported by our extensive physical and digital presence and our continued focus on serving the diverse needs of Indian consumers. Our consumer products business kept its growth
momentum, with the FMCG brand portfolio gaining further ground among Indian consumers. Our disciplined capital allocation has helped create businesses that provide sustainable cash-flows and will remain significant contributors to India’s energy independence and technology evolution.”
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Consolidated profit jumps 34%
Reliance Industries Ltd reported a 33.8% year-on-year increase in consolidated profit after tax (PAT), including its share of profit or loss from associates and joint ventures, to ₹29,550 crore ($3.1 billion) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Depreciation increased 6.2% YoY to ₹15,315 crore ($1.6 billion), largely due to higher depreciation in the digital services business following the capitalisation of 5G assets. Finance costs rose 24.2% to ₹8,481 crore ($885 million), mainly due to higher liability balances and the capitalisation of 5G assets. Tax expenses increased 34.2% YoY to ₹9,363 crore ($977 million).
Capital expenditure (capex) for the quarter stood at ₹38,153 crore ($4 billion). The spending was largely driven by investments in O2C and new energy projects under implementation, along with the building and expansion of infrastructure and distribution reach for the consumer businesses.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: EBITDA rises 23.9% to ₹62,409 crore
Reliance Industries Ltd reported a 23.9% year-on-year increase in consolidated EBITDA to ₹62,409 crore ($6.5 billion) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Jio Platforms Ltd’s EBITDA increased 16.6% YoY, supported by revenue growth and a 250-basis-point expansion in margins. Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL), however, reported an 8.6% decline in EBITDA to ₹6,228 crore.
Its EBITDA margin fell 120 basis points YoY to 7.8%, reflecting planned investments in digital commerce, input-cost inflation absorbed for customers and the shift in the festive calendar to the third quarter.
The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) segment reported a 67.9% increase in EBITDA, driven by a sharp rise in transportation fuel cracks and downstream petrochemical margins. Fuel cracks increased 3-3.7 times amid a tight global refining environment. Polyester chain margins improved 33%, led by a 15% increase in the paraxylene (PX) delta and a 52% rise in the purified terephthalic acid (PTA) delta.
O2C earnings were constrained by higher crude oil premiums, elevated freight rates, costs related to the Special Additional Excise Duty (SAED) and under-recoveries in domestic fuel retail.
The oil and gas segment’s EBITDA declined 2% YoY due to lower KG-D6 gas revenue and higher government of India levies. This was partly offset by favourable exchange-rate movements.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Revenue jumps 27.8% to ₹3.62 lakh crore on O2C growth
Reliance Industries Ltd reported a 27.8% year-on-year increase in consolidated gross revenue to ₹3,62,268 crore ($37.8 billion) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Jio Platforms Ltd’s revenue grew 11.3% YoY, driven by continued subscriber additions, higher average revenue per user (ARPU) and healthy growth in digital services. Reliance Retail Ventures Ltd (RRVL) reported a 6.4% increase in revenue to ₹91,716 crore, with its performance impacted by the shift in the festive calendar to the third quarter.
The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) segment recorded a 44.2% rise in revenue, led by a sharp increase in crude oil and product prices. Crude prices rose 40.6% during the quarter, while transportation fuel prices increased 50-78% YoY. Prices of most downstream chemical products were up 25-35% year-on-year, driven by higher feedstock prices.
Revenue from the oil and gas segment remained stable year-on-year. Lower KGD6 gas production and price realisation were offset by higher condensate price realisation. Improved volumes and price realisation for coal bed methane (CBM) also supported revenue.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Industries O2C Q2 EBITDA jumps 67.9%
Reliance Industries’ oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business reported revenue of ₹2.32 lakh crore in the second quarter, up 44.2% year-on-year, driven by higher crude oil and product prices.
O2C EBITDA surged 67.9% YoY to an all-time high of ₹25,203 crore. Transportation fuel cracks rose 3–3.7 times year-on-year, reaching historic highs. The polyester chain margin touched a three-year high, led by an increase of 15% in paraxylene (PX) and 52% in purified terephthalic acid (PTA) deltas.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Reliance Retail Q2 gross revenue rises 6.4%
Reliance Retail reported gross revenue of ₹91,716 crore for the second quarter, up 6.4% year-on-year. The retail business performance was impacted by the shift in the festive calendar to the third quarter.
Retail EBITDA, before the one-time impairment charge, stood at ₹6,228 crore, with an EBITDA margin of 7.8%.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Consolidated EBITDA margin expands to 18.8% QoQ
Reliance Industries Ltd reported a consolidated EBITDA margin of 18.8% for the second quarter, compared with 17.3% in the previous quarter and 19.5% in the year-ago period.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Consolidated revenue rises 27.8%
Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) reported consolidated revenue of ₹3.62 lakh crore for the second quarter, compared with ₹3.40 lakh crore in the previous quarter and ₹2.84 lakh crore in the year-ago period.
The company delivered its strongest-ever quarterly performance, with consolidated revenue rising 27.8% YoY to ₹3.62 lakh crore, its highest-ever quarterly revenue.
Reliance Industries Q2 Results LIVE Updates: Consolidated profit rises to ₹29,550 Crore
Reliance Industries Ltd reported consolidated net profit of ₹29,550 crore for the second quarter, compared with ₹23,196 crore in the previous quarter and ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period.

title: Reliance Industries Q2 results: Profit may top Rs 21,000 crore as refining, Jio drive earnings- Moneycontrol.com
snippet: Analysts expect profit to top Rs 21,000 crore, driven by strong refining margins and Jio earnings. Retail performance, ARPU and O2C profitability will be closely watched.
content:
Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), India's most valuable company, is expected to report robust profit for the September quarter, supported by strong refining margins, higher telecom earnings, and steady retail performance.
The Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate is scheduled to announce its quarterly earnings on October 30.
Bloomberg consensus estimates suggest Reliance Industries will report a consolidated net profit of Rs 21,368 crore for the September quarter compared with Rs 20,946 crore in the preceding three months and Rs 22,092 crore in the year-earlier period. Analysts expect Reliance's oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business to be the principal earnings driver, benefiting from elevated refining cracks, while Jio's subscriber additions and improving average revenue per user (ARPU) are likely to support growth in digital services.
According to Bloomberg consensus estimates, Reliance Industries' O2C business is expected to generate revenue of Rs 1.62 lakh crore and EBITDA of Rs 16,434 crore in the fiscal second quarter.
The digital services business is projected to report revenue of Rs 41,213 crore and EBITDA of Rs 18,848 crore, while the retail segment is expected to generate revenue of Rs 91,966 crore and EBITDA of Rs 6,593 crore.
The oil and gas business is estimated to report revenue of Rs 5,699 crore and EBITDA of Rs 4,536 crore.
Prabhudas Lilladher expects Reliance's consolidated EBITDA to rise 3.4 percent sequentially to Rs 49,140 crore. Kotak Securities projects a 15 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated EBITDA, while Nuvama expects growth of 17 percent.
Reliance's O2C segment is expected to benefit from elevated refining margins amid tight global product supplies and geopolitical tensions in the Gulf.
According to Prabhudas Lilladher, Brent crude averaged $91.4 per barrel during Q2 FY27 after surging in September amid renewed US-Iran tensions. Refining cracks remained elevated, particularly for diesel and aviation turbine fuel.
Kotak Securities expects O2C EBITDA to rise 47 percent year-on-year, supported by strong earnings from Reliance's special economic zone refinery, which benefits from an exemption from the special additional excise duty, or windfall tax.
The brokerage also expects cheaper US ethane-based petrochemical feedstocks and a weaker rupee to support the segment's profitability.
Nuvama projects O2C EBITDA growth of 38 percent year-on-year, although higher freight costs and operational adjustments could partly offset the gains.
Reliance Jio is expected to maintain its earnings growth momentum, supported by subscriber additions and higher average revenue per user.
Yes Securities estimates Jio's ARPU at Rs 216.5 for the quarter, with its subscriber base reaching approximately 540.3 million.
Prabhudas Lilladher expects ARPU to increase around 1 percent sequentially to Rs 218, supported by the addition of approximately eight million subscribers during the quarter.
The brokerage projects a 3 percent sequential increase in Jio's EBITDA, while Nuvama expects digital services EBITDA to grow 16 percent year-on-year.
Reliance Retail is expected to deliver steady operating earnings, although analysts differ on the pace of revenue growth.
Yes Securities projects retail revenue of Rs 92,700 crore, representing growth of 2.4 percent year-on-year and 2.6 percent sequentially, with an EBITDA margin of around 7 percent.
Meanwhile, Kotak Securities expects retail revenue to grow 11.7 percent year-on-year but projects a 0.8 percent decline in segment EBITDA, reflecting pressure on operating margins.
Nuvama also expects retail EBITDA to decline approximately 1 percent year-on-year because of a higher comparison base.
Reliance's upstream oil and gas business could weigh on overall earnings growth, with analysts anticipating lower production.
Kotak Securities expects the segment's EBITDA to decline 7.2 percent year-on-year, while Nuvama projects a 6 percent fall.
Investors will also watch management's commentary on production trends, crude prices and gas realisations.
Apart from earnings, investors will focus on refining margins, the contribution from the O2C segment, Jio's ARPU and subscriber growth, and Reliance Retail's profitability. The company's capital expenditure, finance costs, and management commentary on the outlook for its major businesses will also signal earnings momentum in the coming quarters.

title: Reliance Industries m-cap tops Rs 17.5 lakh crore, shares surge nearly 12% after Q2 results; biggest gain in 6 yrs- Moneycontrol.com
snippet: Reliance Industries market cap crossed Rs 17 lakh crore as shares surged over 8%, marking their biggest intraday gain in at over years. The stock led Nifty gains after record Q2 earnings and bullish brokerage calls.
content:
Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) saw its market capitalisation cross Rs 17.5 lakh crore on Monday, as its shares surged to end nearly 12 percent higher following record Q2 FY27 earnings and bullish brokerage calls. The stock recorded its biggest single-day gain in over six years, since April 2020. It emerged as the top Nifty gainer and the biggest positive contributor to the benchmark index today.
Reliance Industries shares climbed to 11.6 percent to end the day's high of Rs 1,300, taking the Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate's market capitalisation to over Rs 17.59 lakh crore. The stock was also the most actively traded on both the NSE and BSE. The company added nearly Rs 2 lakh crore of m-cap today.
The sharp rally in RIL stock drove broad gains in the equity market. The rally in Reliance shares drove a broader market surge. At the end of the day, the Sensex was up 1,233 points, or 1.7 percent, at 75,693, while the Nifty gained 388 points to close at 23,441.
Reliance Industries reported its strongest-ever quarterly financial performance for the July-September quarter, with record revenue, EBITDA and net profit, supported by robust growth in its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, digital services and retail operations.
Consolidated revenue surged 28 percent year-on-year to an all-time high of Rs 3.62 lakh crore, while EBITDA increased 24 percent to a record Rs 62,409 crore. Net profit jumped 34 percent to Rs 29,550 crore, also a quarterly record.
The O2C business delivered its strongest-ever quarterly performance, with revenue rising 44.2 percent year-on-year to Rs 2.32 lakh crore and EBITDA surging 67.9 percent to Rs 25,203 crore. Transportation fuel cracks, a measure of refining margins, increased 3 to 3.7 times from a year earlier, reaching historic highs during the quarter.
Reliance's digital services business also reported growth, with Jio Platforms recording an 11.3 percent year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 47,485 crore. Its EBITDA rose 16.6 percent to Rs 21,879 crore, supported by subscriber additions, higher average revenue per user and expansion in digital services.
Goldman Sachs and Nomura maintained their Buy ratings on Reliance Industries following its record quarterly performance, citing strong refining earnings and steady telecom growth, even as retail earnings remained under pressure. Goldman Sachs set a target price of Rs 1,840 per share, implying 58 percent upside from Friday's closing price of Rs 1,164.90. The brokerage said Reliance's Q2 EBITDA exceeded its estimates by 9 percent, led by strong O2C performance.
Nomura also retained its Buy rating, with a target price of Rs 1,560 per share. The brokerage attributed the record earnings to multi-decade-high refining cracks and noted that consolidated EBITDA rose 19 percent sequentially, beating estimates by 9 percent.

title: Reliance Industries Shares Surge 11.6% as Oil and Jio Businesses Boost Earnings | Unique Times Magazine
snippet: Shares of Reliance Industries surged 11.6% on Monday, recording their strongest single-day performance in more than six years. The rally followed better-than-expected quarterly results, with the company reporting a 40.
content:
Reliance Industries Shares Surge 11.6% as Oil and Jio Businesses Boost Earnings
Shares of Reliance Industries surged 11.6% on Monday, recording their strongest single-day performance in more than six years. The rally followed better-than-expected quarterly results, with the company reporting a 40.6% increase in net profit to ₹25,548 crore for the September quarter. Stronger refining and petrochemical margins played a major role in driving the earnings growth.
The results highlighted the increasing contribution of Reliance’s oil-to-chemicals and telecom businesses. Its refining operations benefited from record crude processing and higher-value fuel exports, while Jio Platforms reported nearly 14% growth in quarterly profit. Jio also continued to attract subscribers and improve its profitability following its recent stock market debut.
However, Reliance’s retail business continues to face profitability challenges, while its shares had fallen more than 17% during 2026 before Monday’s rally. Analysts believe sustained growth will depend on a recovery in retail performance and stronger returns from its new energy investments. The latest results have nevertheless improved investor confidence in the company’s future earnings prospects.
