III.18 Liquidity turned into surplus during Q2:2024-25 with a pick-up in government spending after the elections, net forex purchases by the Reserve Bank and return of currency to the banking system. The build-up of GoI cash balances due to advance tax collections and GST payments tightened liquidity conditions between September 21-25, 2024. Additionally, net sales through open market operations (OMOs) under the negotiated dealing system - order matching (NDS-OM) absorbed durable liquidity amounting to ₹0.24 lakh crore during the quarter. Average daily net absorption under the LAF was ₹1.27 lakh crore during Q2. The Reserve Bank conducted five main and 44 fine-tuning VRRR auctions to absorb surplus liquidity. III.19 The liquidity surplus moderated in Q3:2024-25 with average net absorption under the LAF declining to ₹0.80 lakh crore from ₹1.27 lakh crore in the previous quarter. Except for a brief period, system liquidity remained in surplus during October-November on account of higher government spending, notwithstanding a significant increase in CiC due to festival related demand in October and capital outflows in November. Consequently, the Reserve Bank conducted five main and 23 fine-tuning VRRR operations during October 1-November 29, 2024 2 . System liquidity turned into deficit during the second half of December on account of advance tax payments and capital outflows. III.20 Liquidity conditions remained in deficit in Q4:2024-25 due to capital outflows and currency outgo, with average net injection of ₹1.56 lakh crore under the LAF. In order to ease the liquidity stress and the resultant pressure on the weighted average call rate (WACR), the Reserve Bank started conducting daily VRR auctions effective January 16, 2025 with reversal taking place on the next working day. During Q4:2024-25, the Reserve Bank conducted four main and 62 fine-tuning VRR auctions to inject liquidity. With a view to ease the persistently tight liquidity conditions, the Reserve Bank undertook a slew of measures in Q4, which included: (i) injection of ₹1.83 lakh crore through three term VRR auctions of varying maturities conducted in February 2025; (ii) OMO purchase auctions of Government of India securities for an aggregate amount of ₹2.45 lakh crore; and (iii) USD/INR Buy/Sell swap auction of US$ 5 billion for a tenor of six months on January 31, 2025 and US$ 10 billion for a tenor of three years each on February 28, 2025 and March 24, 2025 3 . In addition, the Reserve Bank purchased government securities amounting to ₹38,825 crore under the NDS-OM during the quarter that augmented durable liquidity. III.21 During 2024-25, average absorption under the standing deposit facility (SDF) at ₹0.94 lakh crore constituted 78 per cent of average daily total absorption (₹1.21 lakh crore) under the LAF, while the remaining 22 per cent was absorbed through VRRR auctions – both main and fine-tuning operations ( Chart III.3 ). Banks’ recourse to the MSF remained low, with average daily borrowing amounting to ₹0.07 lakh crore during 2024-25 compared to ₹0.5 lakh crore in 2023-24. Buyback of G-secs, which is part of an active debt consolidation strategy, augmented systemic liquidity amounting to ₹0.5 lakh crore during 2024-25. III.22 The tightening of liquidity conditions in the latter half of Q3 and Q4 was mainly on account of capital outflows and forex operations of the Reserve Bank. The Reserve Bank’s intervention in the forex market is aimed at maintaining orderly market conditions by containing excessive volatility in the exchange rate without targeting any exchange rate level or band, thereby allowing monetary policy to primarily remain focused on domestic macroeconomic conditions and the outlook ( Box III.1 ). Box III.1 Liquidity Management Challenges from Forex Market Operations Divergent monetary policy trajectories across advanced economies, lingering geopolitical tensions and rising trade and policy uncertainties in recent years have rendered capital flows highly volatile. Since its integration with the global economy, India has experienced episodes of surges and sudden stops/reversal in capital flows, posing trade-offs for monetary policy ( Chart 1 ). The Reserve Bank intervenes in the forex market to modulate excessive exchange rate volatility and maintain orderly market conditions, thereby allowing monetary policy to primarily remain focused on domestic macroeconomic conditions. The Reserve Bank’s spot interventions in the forex market entail changes in domestic liquidity conditions, which may necessitate sterilisation of such interventions, given the monetary policy stance. Sterilisations are typically carried out through open market operations (OMOs) – sale/purchase of government securities to modulate the domestic liquidity impact of purchase/sale of foreign currency assets by the Reserve Bank. This is reflected in an offsetting change in net domestic assets (NDA) vis-à-vis any change in net foreign assets (NFA) in the Reserve Bank’s balance sheet 4 . A change in NDA, in turn, may cause further change in NFA as sterilisation operations through OMOs may affect domestic yields resulting in further capital in/out flows. This contrasting movement between NDA and NFA dampens the impact of sterilised intervention. Therefore, the Reserve Bank carefully adjusts changes in NFA and NDA ( Chart 2 ), keeping in mind the prevailing liquidity conditions and the stance of monetary policy, while preventing excessive volatility in the exchange rate. The endogenous relationship between NDA and NFA is modelled using a central bank liquidity management reaction function (ΔNDA = α + βΔNFA + μ i X i ), and a net capital flows equation (ΔNFA = a + bΔNDA + θ i Y i ), where β and b are the sterilisation and offset coefficients, respectively. X i [nominal GDP: quarterly data interpolated to monthly, money multiplier (MUL) and domestic spread (DS: spread between the weighted average call rate and policy repo rate)] and Y i [nominal GDP, MUL, international spread (IS: spread between the weighted average call rate and effective Fed Funds rate) and real effective exchange rate (REER)] are control variables in the equations for NDA and NFA, respectively (Raj et al., 2018). Appropriate instrument variables are used to tackle endogeneity – IS and REER for NFA and DS for NDA. The model is estimated based on monthly data from January 2010 to September 2024 using a two-stage least squares (2SLS) framework ( Table 1 ). In this framework (Ouyang and Rajan, 2008), the efficacy of the sterilised forex market interventions can be gauged by the sterilisation coefficient (to what extent the increase in liquidity resulting from the increase in NFA is sterilised by a corresponding decline in NDA), net of the offset coefficient (the extent of change in NDA that is partially neutralised by a sterilisation induced change in NFA). The estimated sterilisation coefficient of -0.78 implies that, on average, about 78 per cent of the increase in rupee liquidity resulting from an increase in NFA is absorbed through sterilisation operations. The high offset coefficient of -0.71, however, dampens the impact of sterilisation operations. III.23 During 2024-25, two-way fine-tuning operations were the key instrument to manage frictional liquidity. During this period, fine-tuning and main VRRR operations elicited average offer-cover ratios of 0.50 and 0.16, respectively. Banks were reluctant in parting with liquidity for longer tenors, as evident from the lower offer-cover ratios of main operations vis-à-vis fine-tuning operations. In contrast, the market was more responsive to fine-tuning and main VRR operations as reflected in much higher bid-cover ratios. III.24 Reflecting the liquidity dynamics, the WACR – the operating target of monetary policy – remained broadly within the LAF corridor during 2024-25. 5 It, however, moderated after the introduction of daily VRR operations and the reduction in the policy repo rate by 25 bps on February 7, 2025. The WACR, on an average, remained 6 bps above the policy repo rate in 2024-25 as against 13 bps in 2023-24 ( Chart III.4 ). III.25 Overnight rates in the collateralised segment moved in tandem with the WACR ( Table III.2 ). In the short-term money market, average yield on 3-month treasury bills (T-bills) softened by 26 bps in September 2024 from June 2024 on account of lower short-term borrowing requirements of the government, as reflected in the cancellation of T-bill auctions in the second half of September. Yields declined further in March 2025. Similarly, yields on 3-month commercial papers (CPs) of NBFCs and certificates of deposit (CDs) softened from March 2024, taking cues from domestic developments such as the transition of systemic liquidity to surplus and moderation in the wedge between deposit and credit growth. The decline in short-term rates prompted banks to increase CD issuances to meet rising credit demand amidst sluggish deposit growth. G-sec yields also remained benign throughout the year (see Section 5 of Chapter II). Overall, monetary policy changes impact short-term interest rates more than long-term rates in the Indian context (Patra et al., 2024) 6 . Monetary Policy Transmission III.26 The transmission of policy repo rate changes to banks’ deposit and lending rates continued during 2024-25 albeit at a slower pace. The weighted average lending rates (WALRs) on fresh and outstanding rupee loans of SCBs declined by 2 bps and 8 bps, respectively, during 2024-25. In case of deposits, weighted average domestic term deposit rates (WADTDRs) on fresh and outstanding deposits increased by 3 bps and 14 bps, respectively, in 2024-25, with a rising proportion of deposits getting renewed at higher rates. The pace and extent of monetary transmission to lending and deposit rates of SCBs has strengthened in recent years, reflecting the Reserve Bank’s sustained efforts to impart transparency and flexibility to the interest rate structure. 7 III.27 During the tightening cycle (May 2022-January 2025), banks revised their repo-linked lending rates upwards by 250 bps and 1-year marginal cost of funds-based lending rate (MCLR) by 178 bps, resulting in an increase in the WALR on fresh rupee loans and on outstanding loans. The WADTDRs on fresh term deposits and outstanding term deposits also increased during this period ( Table III.3 ). The increase in term deposit rates on fresh deposits was mainly driven by bulk deposit rates, although retail deposit rates also exhibited significant transmission, especially in H1:2024-25. III.28 In response to the 25 bps cut in policy repo rate during the February policy meeting, banks have reduced their repo linked external benchmark lending rate (EBLR) by a similar magnitude. The MCLR, having a longer reset period and being linked to the cost of funds, may undergo adjustments with some lag. Consequently, the WALR on outstanding rupee loans declined by 10 bps during the easing cycle (February-March 2025). In case of fresh loans, however, it has increased by 3 bps. III.29 Across bank-groups, increase in the WADTDR on outstanding deposits and WALR on fresh rupee loans were higher for public sector banks (PSBs) relative to private banks (PVBs) during May 2022-January 2025 ( Chart III.5 ). The transmission to WALR on outstanding rupee loans, however, was lower for PSBs reflecting a comparatively higher share of internal benchmark-based lending rates, viz., MCLR and others. Transmission was highest in case of foreign banks, facilitated by their low-cost deposits and a higher proportion of EBLR-linked loans 8 . During February-March 2025, WALR on outstanding rupee loans declined across all bank-groups. Agenda for 2025-26 III.36 The Department would support the conduct and formulation of monetary policy by providing (i) high quality inputs on the assessment and outlook of inflation and growth; (ii) analysing and refining forecast of liquidity conditions; (iii) studying the monetary policy transmission process; and (iv) evaluating credit conditions and sectoral flows. Against this backdrop, the Department would focus on the following initiatives: Review of the monetary policy framework; Revisiting optimal level of system liquidity for effective monetary policy transmission; Spatial and cross-sectional analysis of National Sample Survey Organisation’s household consumption expenditure data; and Collection of credit deployment data from housing finance companies (HFCs) for improved assessment of sectoral credit by NBFCs. 4. Conclusion III.37 During 2024-25, headline inflation exhibited further moderation, though the path of disinflation was interrupted by volatile and elevated food inflation. System liquidity conditions transited from surplus during August-November 2024 to deficit in December-February. The Reserve Bank reduced the policy rate by 25 bps as growth-inflation dynamics opened up policy space for supporting growth and proactively conducted a suite of market operations to provide durable liquidity in the system. As a result, system liquidity returned to surplus by end-March 2025. Going forward, domestic economic activity is expected to strengthen from the lows of H1:2024-25. Headline inflation is expected to ease and move further towards the target in 2025-26. Monetary policy is committed towards achieving durable price stability, which is a necessary prerequisite for high growth on a sustained basis. Source: RBI. | Box III.1 Liquidity Management Challenges from Forex Market Operations Divergent monetary policy trajectories across advanced economies, lingering geopolitical tensions and rising trade and policy uncertainties in recent years have rendered capital flows highly volatile. Since its integration with the global economy, India has experienced episodes of surges and sudden stops/reversal in capital flows, posing trade-offs for monetary policy ( Chart 1 ). The Reserve Bank intervenes in the forex market to modulate excessive exchange rate volatility and maintain orderly market conditions, thereby allowing monetary policy to primarily remain focused on domestic macroeconomic conditions. The Reserve Bank’s spot interventions in the forex market entail changes in domestic liquidity conditions, which may necessitate sterilisation of such interventions, given the monetary policy stance. Sterilisations are typically carried out through open market operations (OMOs) – sale/purchase of government securities to modulate the domestic liquidity impact of purchase/sale of foreign currency assets by the Reserve Bank. This is reflected in an offsetting change in net domestic assets (NDA) vis-à-vis any change in net foreign assets (NFA) in the Reserve Bank’s balance sheet 4 . A change in NDA, in turn, may cause further change in NFA as sterilisation operations through OMOs may affect domestic yields resulting in further capital in/out flows. This contrasting movement between NDA and NFA dampens the impact of sterilised intervention. Therefore, the Reserve Bank carefully adjusts changes in NFA and NDA ( Chart 2 ), keeping in mind the prevailing liquidity conditions and the stance of monetary policy, while preventing excessive volatility in the exchange rate. The endogenous relationship between NDA and NFA is modelled using a central bank liquidity management reaction function (ΔNDA = α + βΔNFA + μ i X i ), and a net capital flows equation (ΔNFA = a + bΔNDA + θ i Y i ), where β and b are the sterilisation and offset coefficients, respectively. X i [nominal GDP: quarterly data interpolated to monthly, money multiplier (MUL) and domestic spread (DS: spread between the weighted average call rate and policy repo rate)] and Y i [nominal GDP, MUL, international spread (IS: spread between the weighted average call rate and effective Fed Funds rate) and real effective exchange rate (REER)] are control variables in the equations for NDA and NFA, respectively (Raj et al., 2018). Appropriate instrument variables are used to tackle endogeneity – IS and REER for NFA and DS for NDA. The model is estimated based on monthly data from January 2010 to September 2024 using a two-stage least squares (2SLS) framework ( Table 1 ). In this framework (Ouyang and Rajan, 2008), the efficacy of the sterilised forex market interventions can be gauged by the sterilisation coefficient (to what extent the increase in liquidity resulting from the increase in NFA is sterilised by a corresponding decline in NDA), net of the offset coefficient (the extent of change in NDA that is partially neutralised by a sterilisation induced change in NFA). The estimated sterilisation coefficient of -0.78 implies that, on average, about 78 per cent of the increase in rupee liquidity resulting from an increase in NFA is absorbed through sterilisation operations. The high offset coefficient of -0.71, however, dampens the impact of sterilisation operations. title: RBI MPC Key Takeaways 2026: Repo rate hiked to 5.50%, FY27 GDP growth forecast raised to 7.1%
snippet: Oct 7, 2026 · RBI Monetary Policy 2026 Takeaways: The Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, the first increase since February 2023. The GDP growth forecast for FY27 was raised from 6.7% to 7.1%, highlighting resilient economic activity.
content:
Listen to this article in summarized format
The RBI also raised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1% from 6.7% and its inflation projection to 5.2% from 5.1%, while shifting its policy stance to calibrated tightening.
The MPC voted unanimously to increase the repo rate, while the decision to change the policy stance to calibrated tightening was taken by a majority of 4-2.
Also read: RBI Policy Meeting 2026 Live: Malhotra & co hikes repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50% as war creeps into Indian retail inflation; more rate cuts off the table in near term
Here are the key takeaways from the RBI MPC meeting:
1. Repo rate raised by 25 bps to 5.50%
The MPC unanimously voted to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, the first increase since February 2023. The Standing Deposit Facility rate now stands at 5.25%, while the Marginal Standing Facility rate and the bank rate have been adjusted to 5.75%.
The rate hike comes amid renewed inflationary pressures from rising international crude oil prices, higher food prices and an uneven monsoon. The RBI also flagged the challenging global environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainty and volatility in financial markets.
“The MPC noted that the global context, on account of geopolitical developments, remains challenging. Nonetheless, the Indian economy has been strong, and the economic momentum remains broad based,” Malhotra said.
2. FY27 GDP growth forecast raised to 7.1%
The RBI raised its real GDP growth projection for FY27 to 7.1% from 6.7%, an upward revision of 40 basis points, reflecting the resilience of domestic economic activity.
The central bank projected growth at 7.2% for the second quarter, 6.9% for the third quarter and 6.8% for the fourth quarter of FY27. Real GDP growth for the first quarter of FY28 is projected at 7.1%.
The RBI said high-frequency indicators for the second quarter pointed to sustained economic momentum, supported by steady services activity, manufacturing resilience, domestic demand and investment. Both manufacturing and services purchasing managers’ indices remained in expansionary territory.
However, global economic uncertainty, supply-chain disruptions, elevated commodity prices and geopolitical tensions could weigh on the outlook. A weak southwest monsoon and strong El Niño conditions could also affect the upcoming rabi season and rural demand.
Also read: RBI Inflation FY2026-27: Malhotra & Co raises inflation forecast to 5.2% for FY27
3. FY27 inflation forecast raised to 5.2%
The RBI raised its CPI inflation forecast for FY27 to 5.2% from 5.1%, reflecting persistent price pressures from food and fuel.
Retail inflation rose to 4.8% in August from 4.5% in July, driven largely by higher food and fuel inflation. The central bank also flagged a broadening of price pressures across food commodities and early signs of inflation becoming more generalised.
The RBI projected CPI inflation at 4.9% for the second quarter, 6% for the December quarter and 5.7% for the fourth quarter of FY27. Inflation for the first quarter of FY28 is projected at 5.6%, with risks evenly balanced. Core inflation for FY27 is projected at 4.4%.
The central bank highlighted the risks posed by volatile international oil prices, deficient and uneven monsoon rainfall and El Niño conditions, which could affect agricultural output and food prices.
4. MPC shifts stance to calibrated tightening; rate cuts off the table
The MPC changed its policy stance to calibrated tightening by a majority of 4-2, signalling a sharper focus on containing inflationary pressures.
The central bank said inflation and its outlook were no longer as benign as they had been in the previous year. While there was some evidence of elevated inflation expectations and a generalisation of price pressures, the RBI noted limited signs of supply-side pressures becoming embedded in pricing behaviour.
The governor underscored that rate cuts were no longer an option in the near term.
“Given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near term, and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook,” Malhotra said.
The duration and extent of any rate-hike cycle, he added, would depend on actual growth and inflation developments, underlying inflation, the broadening of price pressures and the second-round effects of supply shocks.
5. Liquidity remains in surplus; RBI to align call rate with policy rate
System liquidity increased substantially over the previous two months following measures undertaken to attract capital inflows. The average daily surplus liquidity, measured by the net position under the liquidity adjustment facility, stood at ₹5.9 lakh crore since the previous MPC meeting.
Subsequent liquidity-absorption measures and quarterly advance-tax outflows moderated the surplus somewhat in September. The weighted average call rate largely traded in the lower half of the policy corridor, while short-term money-market rates moderated significantly.
The RBI said it would continue using an appropriate mix of liquidity-management tools to align the weighted average call rate with the policy repo rate.
6. RBI announces measures on account aggregation and financial markets
The RBI announced two additional measures alongside its monetary policy decisions.
First, it will allow interoperability among non-banking financial company account aggregators, enabling users to aggregate financial information across different account aggregators by onboarding with just one.
Second, the central bank will facilitate SEBI-regulated depositories in including bank deposit account information in consolidated account statements. This will allow individuals to access information on bank deposits alongside their securities, equity and debt holdings in a consolidated statement. The measures are to be implemented by the end of 2026.
The RBI will also constitute a technical consultative committee for financial markets to provide a forum for structured engagement with market participants and other stakeholders on policy and operational matters.

title: RBI New Repo Rate 2026: MPC Meeting Hikes Repo Rate By 40 Bps, GDP Forecast Raised
snippet: Oct 7, 2026 · RBI New Repo Rate 2026: The RBI MPC Meeting announced a 40 bps repo rate hike in its Monetary Policy 2026 review and raised the GDP forecast. Check key takeaways, inflation outlook and policy updates.
content:
Cheaper loans just got harder to expect. Today, October 7, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised policy repo rate for the first time in 4 years. It now stands at 5.50%, up by 25 basis points.
The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to banks. A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point, so 25 of them make a quarter of one per cent. This is the first hike since February 2023.
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra announced the decision. All members of the MPC, the panel that sets interest rates, voted for the hike. The committee also changed its stance to “calibrated tightening”.
Here are seven key takeaways investors need to watch now –
1. Repo rate rises to 5.50%
The MPC unanimously voted to increase the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50%.
The policy stance also changed to “calibrated tightening”, with a 4-2 majority.
2. RBI Governor rules out rate cut in near-term
The RBI has indicated that the policy options going forward are largely between another rate hike and a pause.
Inflation risks have increased due to higher crude oil prices, food prices and global uncertainties. The West Asia conflict has added another layer of risk.
Governor Sanjay Malhotra also warned that global inflation could rise sharply and trigger tighter monetary policy across economies.
He added, “The RBI’s October hike acknowledges that cyclical inflation risks are no longer benign.”
3. FY27 GDP growth forecast raised to 7.1%
Despite the rate hike, the RBI has raised its real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth forecast for financial year 2026-27 (FY27) to 7.1% from 6.7% earlier.
The second-quarter growth forecast was raised to 7.2% from 6.4%, while the third-quarter forecast was increased to 6.9% from 6.5%. The fourth-quarter estimate remains at 6.8%.
However, the first-quarter FY28 forecast was trimmed to 7.1% from 7.3%.
4. FY27 inflation forecast moves higher
The RBI has raised its Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation forecast for FY27 to 5.2% from 5% earlier. Inflation is now projected at 4.9% in the second quarter, 6% in the third quarter and 5.7% in the fourth quarter.
Core inflation, which excludes food and fuel, is projected at around 4.4%.
In August, CPI inflation rose to 4.8% from 4.5% in July. The RBI said food and fuel prices were major contributors, while core inflation also showed signs of broadening.
5. Oil, Yield and West Asia remain key risks
The RBI has pointed to geopolitical tension, elevated international commodity prices, trade frictions and tighter global financial conditions.
Crude oil is particularly important for India because higher oil prices can increase transport and input costs while also putting pressure on inflation and the rupee.
“The central bank has also projected inflation at 4.9% for the second quarter, 6% for the December quarter, Q4 at 5.7% and 5.6% for the June quarter of FY28, with risks evenly balanced,” Malhotra added. He also pointed out the hardening US Yield is a key factor to watch going forward.
6. RBI sees resilient growth despite risks
The central bank believes domestic economic activity can remain resilient despite global headwinds. At the same time, it wants to prevent temporary price pressures from becoming persistent.
7. NBFC aggregators and financial infrastructure
The policy also included developments around the financial system, including interoperability of Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) aggregators.
The RBI has enabled interoperability among Non-Banking Financial Company Account Aggregators (NBFC-AAs), allowing customers registered with one Account Aggregator to securely share their financial information with regulated entities through another Account Aggregator.

title: RBI Hikes Repo Rate to 5.5%, Raises FY27 Retail Inflation Forecast to 5.2%
snippet: Oct 7, 2026 · The Reserve Bank of India has announced a 25 basis point hike in the repo rate to 5.5 per cent and raised its retail inflation forecast for the current fiscal year (FY27) to 5.2 per cent ...
content:
The Reserve Bank of India has announced a 25 basis point hike in the repo rate to 5.5 per cent and raised its retail inflation forecast for the current fiscal year (FY27) to 5.2 per cent, signalling a 'calibrated tightening' amidst growing price pressures.
Key Points
- The RBI has raised its retail inflation projection for FY27 to 5.2 per cent, up from an earlier estimate of 5 per cent.
- The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) unanimously decided to hike the key interest rate (repo) by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent.
- The central bank's stance has shifted from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening' due to the non-benign inflation outlook.
- Price pressures are increasingly visible across food components and oil, exacerbated by deficient southwest monsoon and El Nino conditions.
- Core inflation for the current fiscal ending March 2027 is projected at 4.4 per cent, with overall CPI inflation for Q3 FY27 expected at 6.0 per cent.
The Reserve Bank of India on Wednesday marginally raised the forecast for retail inflation for the current fiscal to 5.2 per cent from its earlier estimate of 5 per cent and said price pressures are increasingly becoming visible across a range of commodities.
The near-term outlook on inflation points towards continued pressures from supply side on account of the deficient southwest monsoon, El Nino conditions and high volatility in international oil prices, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said while announcing the central bank's October bi-monthly monetary policy.
Rising Price Pressures and Core Inflation
"Price pressures are increasingly becoming visible across a range of commodities within the food component, apart from oil," he said.
In addition, the early signs of inflation becoming generalised are also evident from the increase in core inflation and higher inflation across a larger segment of the consumer price index (CPI) basket, he said.
Considering all factors, he said CPI inflation for 2026-27 is projected to be 5.2 per cent with Q2 at 4.9 per cent; Q3 at 6.0 per cent; and Q4 at 5.7 per cent.
Inflation for Q1:2027-28 is projected at 5.6 per cent, with risks being evenly balanced.
Core inflation has been projected at 4.4 per cent for the current fiscal ending March 2027.
Food and Fuel Drive Inflation
CPI-based retail inflation rose to 4.8 per cent in August 2026 from 4.5 per cent in July.
This was largely driven by higher inflation in food and fuel components.
"Food price increases have become more broad-based along with notable spikes in certain items such as sugar and onion," Malhotra said, and added fuel inflation inched up in August, mostly due to unfavourable base effects.
Core inflation, excluding precious metals, increased to 2.9 per cent in August.
MPC's Stance Shift
The Governor also said that the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) observed that in light of available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year.
In this milieu, recalibrating the policy rate is imperative, he said as the MPC unanimously decided to hike the key interest rate (repo) by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent.
The MPC also changed its stance to 'calibrated tightening' from 'neutral'.

What is driving inflation, according to the RBI?
The RBI noted that headline inflation rose to 4.4 per cent in June 2026, mainly because of higher food and fuel prices.
Key observations include:

- Fuel inflation rose following higher international energy prices.

Global risks highlighted by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra
The RBI flagged several global developments that continue to pose risks to the economy, including:
- Ongoing conflict in West Asia.
- Volatile crude oil prices.
- Persistent global inflation.
- Uncertainty surrounding global trade policy.
- Stronger US dollar and elevated US bond yields.

Domestic economy remains resilient
According to the RBI, India's economy continues to perform well despite external challenges.
Key positives highlighted by the MPC include:
- Strong private consumption.
- Resilient investment activity.
- Healthy manufacturing and services sectors.
- Robust exports.
- Stable employment conditions.
- Continued government infrastructure spending.
- Strong credit growth.
El Niño and monsoon remain key concerns
The central bank cautioned that deficient and uneven south-west monsoon conditions associated with El Niño could affect agriculture and rural demand.
However, it said government initiatives such as crop diversification, climate-resilient farming and water conservation are expected to help reduce the impact.
What's next for RBI monetary policy?
The MPC said the outlook remains uncertain because of:
- Inflation risks.
- El Niño and monsoon conditions.
- Geopolitical tensions.
- Global trade uncertainty.
The minutes of the August MPC meeting will be released on 19 August 2026, while the next RBI MPC meeting is scheduled to take place from 5 to 7 October 2026.

title: AI buildout hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts
snippet: Microsoft and Google both reported capital expenditures that fell short of analysts' estimates. Amy Hood, Microsoft's CFO, said on the company's earnings call that third-party providers of AI chips ...
content:
The past few quarters of hyperscaler earnings have been marked by ever-increasing capital expenditure forecasts as tech giants race to build out artificial intelligence infrastructure to meet what they describe as insatiable demand.
At least for the moment, Microsoft and Alphabet are telling a slightly different story.
In their earnings reports Wednesday, both companies shared capex figures that came up shy of analysts' estimates. Microsoft reduced its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, and Alphabet held its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion.
The numbers suggest a slowdown is nowhere in sight, but they do represent another potential point of concern for the AI buildout. Shares of neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN all dropped after the reports, as did Oracle, which is one of the biggest spenders on AI infrastructure.
Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on the software company's earnings call that third-party providers of graphics processing units had delays that will push out some available capacity until the first half of 2027. She didn't provide names, but Microsoft relies on CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius, among others.
Anat Ashkenazi, Alphabet's finance chief, told analysts that outside computing power "came online only at the very end of Q3." Alphabet shares tumbled about 10% in extended trading as the company missed on earnings and revenue and reported negative free cash flow of more than $9 billion.
Plenty of Alphabet shareholders remain faithful.
"We are pleased with what we see and what we heard, and trust management's approach to their AI spending," Chris Ballard, managing director of Check Capital Management, wrote in an email to CNBC.
Investors will get a final read on hyperscaler capex for the quarter when Amazon reports results after the close Thursday. In Meta's earnings report last week, the company said it expects full-year capex of $135 billion to $145 billion, raising the bottom of the range from $130 billion. Like with Alphabet, Meta shares sank as the company reported negative free cash flow.
Delays from emerging neocloud partners have occurred before at Microsoft, but they're more critical now as Anthropic gets set to go public. Anthropic counts on infrastructure from Amazon, Google and Microsoft for much of its computing needs, alongside capacity from SpaceX, Lambda and Nscale, which filed to go public in September but hasn't updated its prospectus in weeks.
At times this year, Anthropic's Claude assistant has been unavailable due to climbing demand. Rival OpenAI, which has said an initial public offering in 2027 is likely, is also in constant need of more capacity.
One big challenge for the market is that the neoclouds require billions of dollars in outside capital to fuel their buildouts but don't have investment-grade credit ratings. With interest rates rising and concerns about their debt loads mounting, lenders are pulling out of the market.
Last week, analysts at Gartner shared with CNBC the firm's prediction that, by 2030, 80% of neocloud companies will either be absorbed or completely cease operations. Nvidia-backed neocloud Firmus, based in Australia, withdrew plans to go public earlier this month, despite boasting large usage commitments from Meta and OpenAI.
None of that is to suggest the AI buildout is over, or even close to plateauing.
Microsoft's Hood said Wednesday that she sees capital spending accelerating in the first half of 2027 thanks to higher component costs and the delayed deliveries. As a group, hyperscaler capex is expected to top $1 trillion next year and, according to some estimates, continue rising from there.
Despite the third-quarter capex shortfall, investors cheered Microsoft's report on Wednesday as the company beat earnings and revenue estimates, driven by 48% sales growth in its Azure cloud business.
"We view the quarter as further validation of Microsoft's AI-led growth opportunity," Cantor analysts led by Thomas Blakey wrote in a Wednesday note to clients. They recommend buying Microsoft stock, and they pushed up their one-year price target to $630 from $608.

title: Microsoft shares retreat despite strong Azure growth as AI spending looms
snippet: Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT) shares gave back early gains on Thursday despite a stronger-than-expected quarterly performance, as investors weighed accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) demand ...
content:
Microsoft Corp (NASDAQ:MSFT) shares gave back early gains on Thursday despite a stronger-than-expected quarterly performance, as investors weighed accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) demand against the prospect of sharply higher infrastructure spending in the second half of its fiscal year.
The shares opened higher before turning lower, trading around 1.4% below their opening level.
Bank of America reiterated its Buy rating on Microsoft and raised its price target to $630 from $600, citing strong Azure growth and expanding opportunities to monetize AI across its cloud and software businesses.
Revenue rose 19% year over year in constant currency to $92.3 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, beating expectations for growth of about 17%, according to the bank.
Azure, Microsoft's cloud computing business, delivered 48% growth in constant currency, roughly three percentage points above expectations. Guidance for growth of 49% to 50% in the current quarter also exceeded the consensus forecast of about 45%.
Bank of America said improvements in GPU and CPU efficiency were helping Microsoft generate more revenue from its existing infrastructure, partly offsetting delays in third-party capacity deliveries.
However, those delays are expected to push some capital spending into the second half of the fiscal year. Bank of America forecasts fiscal 2027 capital expenditure of $222 billion, up 53% year over year, with spending reaching $125 billion in the second half, compared with $96 billion in the first.
Wedbush also highlighted the spending outlook, noting that Microsoft spent $45.2 billion on capital expenditure, including leases, in the latest quarter and projected spending of about $50 billion in the current quarter.
Jefferies maintained its Buy rating and $650 price target, pointing to improving profitability alongside the strong cloud performance.
Operating margin reached 49.8%, above the 48.4% to 48.7% implied by guidance, while Microsoft 365 commercial cloud growth accelerated to 18% in constant currency from 15% in the previous quarter.
Commercial bookings growth, however, fell 11% in constant currency following 11% growth in the prior quarter, against a tougher year-ago comparison. Remaining performance obligations stood at $677 billion, up 73% year over year.
AI adoption provided further encouragement. Bank of America said daily Copilot users increased nearly 50% quarter over quarter, while customers actively consuming Copilot credits rose more than 75%. Revenue from Microsoft's Foundry platform more than tripled year over year.
The results highlighted Microsoft's ability to turn AI demand into growth across infrastructure and software. But with capital spending expected to accelerate sharply, investors will be watching whether revenue gains can keep pace with the rising cost of building out AI capacity.

title: Microsoft and Alphabet Just Reported Earnings, Putting the AI Boom to the Test | The Motley Fool
snippet: Azure revenue grew 48%, while Google Cloud revenue more than doubled. Alphabet burned $9.1 billion in free cash flow, while Microsoft generated $18.6 billion. Microsoft has more room to fund its ...
content:
Two tech behemoths -- Alphabet (GOOG -0.96%) (GOOGL -0.98%) and Microsoft (MSFT +0.17%) -- reported earnings today. Both showed strong cloud growth, but the market is treating them very differently. Microsoft shares popped after hours while Alphabet stock sank. Why?
I think a big part of the answer is how each plans to pay for the massive outlays both have planned.
Cloud growth accelerated at both companies
Microsoft beat Wall Street's targets with sales up 19%, reaching $92.3 billion. GAAP -- generally accepted accounting principles -- earnings per share (EPS) came in at $4.92. Adjusted EPS was $4.89, above the roughly $4.72 the Street expected. Azure, its cloud platform, grew 48%, reaching $33.17 billion in revenue.
Alphabet's cloud growth was even stronger than Microsoft's: 103% growth for the unit, earning $11.1 billion in operating income on $30.7 billion in sales. Overall, sales jumped 25%, reaching $127.6 billion, slightly missing estimates, while GAAP EPS actually fell from $2.87 to $2.12. Search and YouTube ads also underperformed.
Alphabet's cash flow is the real problem
Some of Alphabet's EPS drop can be explained by an $8.7 billion net loss on equity securities, but even if you remove this -- worth $0.55 per share -- the earnings still came in well below what Wall Street was looking for.
While it's not a great look, I think the real issue the market is reacting to is the company's cash picture. Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital expenditures (capex), up from $24.0 billion a year ago. Operating cash flow -- the cash the actual business generated -- was $42.3 billion. That left free cash flow (FCF) -- the money left after paying for its capex investments -- at negative $9.1 billion. That's worse than the negative $5.9 billion the company reported last quarter.
During the quarter, Alphabet raised $28.7 billion through senior unsecured notes and $12.4 billion from selling stock. Long-term debt has grown from $46.5 billion at the end of 2025 to $125.1 billion.
Alphabet said its capex guidance for 2026 holds -- $195 billion to $205 billion -- but said it expects capex in 2027 to "increase significantly."
Microsoft is still paying its own way
Microsoft, on the other hand, is still FCF positive, though like Alphabet, that figure is moving in the wrong direction. The company reported FCF of $18.63 billion, down 27% year over year, after $39.37 billion in cash capital spending. Its broader capex figure, which includes finance leases, was $45.2 billion.
CFO Amy Hood said on July's earnings call that the company expects to stay free-cash-flow positive for its current fiscal year, though capex is expected to expand. On that call, she also said demand for its cloud services was running ahead of supply.
The bottom line
Microsoft at this point has a much healthier cushion in its quarterly cash flow -- more room to keep spending while it waits for those investments to pay off. Alphabet is increasingly asking lenders and shareholders to help cover the bill.
Obviously, the growth is hard to argue with, but I still think the jury is out on whether this bet will pay off for both companies. Costs are climbing, and I'm concerned the math won't pencil out long term.

title: Microsoft’s Neocloud Pullback Isn’t a Crack in AI Demand
snippet: Microsoft's pullback from Nebius, IREN and Nscale projects sparked a neocloud sell-off, but Azure growth, backlog data and ...
content:
Reports that Microsoft is pulling back from Nebius, IREN and Nscale projects triggered sharp sell-offs in neocloud stocks on Nov. 5.
Microsoft's moves appear tied to supplier execution problems, such as permit fines and cabling issues, rather than weakening AI demand.
Azure growth of 48% and a $677 billion backlog suggest strong demand, though rising CapEx and falling free cash flow raise cost concerns.
On Nov. 5, Bloomberg reported that Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ: MSFT) is stepping away from risky projects with Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS), IREN (NASDAQ: IREN) and Nscale and debating new neocloud deals. The Financial Times added that Microsoft passed on an option to more than double its Nscale contract in Texas.
Those reports, coming on the heels of the U.S. midterm elections, sent neocloud stocks tumbling. By the end of the day, NBIS was down about 14%, IREN dropped 17%, and CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) dropped 10%.
Many investors interpreted the news as the first crack in AI demand. The fundamentals tell a different story. Days earlier, Microsoft reported 48% Azure growth and said demand still exceeds supply.
Some investors pointed out a less-than-expected capital expenditure (CapEx) number. However, that fell short because third-party suppliers delivered late, not because Microsoft spent less by choice.
That context reframes the neocloud news. Bloomberg cited a $1 million fine for unpermitted generators at a New Jersey site being built for Nebius. It also flagged cabling problems at an IREN site in Texas. Microsoft is demanding better execution and building more of its own capacity.
Microsoft Is Rationing Trust, Not Spending
Microsoft's recent moves share a common thread. Each one targets a specific supplier problem. None of them points to weaker demand.
For example, a source familiar with the Nscale decision told Reuters that Microsoft made that decision several months ago. The existing Texas contract remains in place. Microsoft declined an expansion option, but it didn't cancel live capacity.
The same pattern shows up elsewhere. Microsoft exited an Nscale project in England after grid delays pushed power into the 2030s. Bloomberg also reported that Microsoft is winding down a 2023 Oracle deal. The reason given was older NVIDIA chips that no longer meet Microsoft's specifications.
Both of those examples provide nuance to the delays with IREN. On its earnings call, the company communicated that Microsoft requested network design changes that pushed some deliveries into early 2027. The company said it faces no financial penalties for those changes, and that its vertically integrated business model put it in a position to manage the changes in ways that other neoclouds would not be able to do.
Microsoft's Azure Growth Shows AI Demand Remains Strong
The numbers from Microsoft's fiscal first quarter support that reading. Azure revenue grew 48% to $33.2 billion, surpassing management's guidance of 44% to 45%. Microsoft expects Azure growth to accelerate to 49% to 50% in the current quarter.
Microsoft's commercial backlog tells a similar story. Remaining performance obligations rose 73% to $677 billion. That represents contracted future revenue that Microsoft has yet to recognize. A company with that backlog cannot afford unreliable suppliers.
Investors have seen this movie before. In early 2025, reports that Microsoft was canceling data center leases sparked fears of an AI slowdown. Microsoft's capital spending kept climbing anyway.
The Bearish Counterpoint: "Build, Don't Rent" Has a Price
There is a tradeoff investors should not ignore. Renting capacity from neoclouds spreads costs over the life of a contract. Building it means paying more up front. If Microsoft owns more capacity, more of the cost lands on its own balance sheet.
That cost is already visible. Free cash flow fell about 27% to $18.6 billion last quarter. Operating cash flow rose 29% to $58 billion over the same period. The gap reflects how much cash Microsoft is pouring into data centers.
Spending is set to rise from here. CFO Amy Hood guided for CapEx above $50 billion in the December quarter. She also expects spending to accelerate in the second half of the fiscal year. That includes third-party capacity that slipped from earlier quarters.
The mix of that spending matters too. Hood said roughly 75% of CapEx now goes to short-lived assets such as GPUs and CPUs. Those chips lose value far faster than buildings do. Owning more of them puts more pressure on future margins.
Investors should ask whether "build, don't rent" means even heavier CapEx ahead. Microsoft hasn't said how much neocloud capacity it plans to replace with its own. That answer will shape free cash flow for years.
What This Means for Neocloud and Microsoft Investors
For neocloud stocks, the sell-off may not be pure overreaction. Microsoft is a major customer for Nebius, IREN, and Nscale. If it concentrates on fewer suppliers, the risk to those business models is real. Execution now matters as much as headline contract values.
IREN's backlog grew 22% to $20.3 billion last quarter. But the company still needs about $6 billion in financing for its fiscal 2027 spending plan. Delivery delays make that harder.
For MSFT shareholders, the picture is more favorable. Demand remains ahead of supply, and Microsoft is using its leverage to secure better capacity. The open question is cost, not demand.
Key dates will test the thesis. Nebius reports earnings on Nov. 12. IREN is targeting January 2027 to bring more than $4 billion in contracted annual recurring revenue online, although additional supplier delays could push that milestone into February. Microsoft's fiscal second-quarter report in late January will show whether CapEx topped $50 billion as promised.

title: Infosys Q2 FY27 Profit Rises 6.2%; Cuts Growth Guidance | Sarkaritel.com
snippet: Infosys Q2 FY27 profit rises 6.2% to ₹7,823 crore as revenue reaches ₹49,244 crore; FY27 growth guidance cut to 1.
content:
Infosys reported a consolidated net profit of ₹7,823 crore in Q2 FY27, up 6.2% year-on-year, while revenue from operations rose 11% to ₹49,244 crore. The IT major lowered its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%–2% in constant currency, from the earlier 1.5%–3%, while maintaining its operating margin guidance at 20%–22%.
Key Highlights
- Net profit rose 6.2% year-on-year to ₹7,823 crore in Q2 FY27.
- Revenue from operations increased 11% year-on-year to ₹49,244 crore.
- FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 1%–2%, from 1.5%–3%.
- Infosys declared an interim dividend of ₹26 per share.
New Delhi, Oct 24: IT services major Infosys reported a consolidated net profit of ₹7,823 crore for Q2 FY27, compared with ₹7,364 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year, marking a 6.2% year-on-year increase. Sequentially, profit was nearly flat against ₹7,769 crore in Q1 FY27. Revenue from operations rose 2.14% quarter-on-quarter to ₹49,244 crore and increased 11% from ₹44,490 crore in Q2 FY26.
The Bengaluru-headquartered company revised its FY27 revenue growth guidance downward to 1%–2% in constant currency, compared with its earlier forecast of 1.5%–3%. Infosys retained its operating margin guidance at 20%–22%. The company attributed business momentum in part to stronger demand from energy and utilities clients and increased enterprise spending on artificial intelligence services.
CEO and Managing Director Salil Parekh said Infosys secured large deals worth $5.2 billion, including a mega deal exceeding $2 billion. He also said AI-related revenue accounted for 10.5% and grew 29% quarter-on-quarter, reflecting increased client adoption and demand for AI-led transformation services.
Infosys declared an interim dividend of ₹26 per share, with November 3, 2026, set as the record date and November 11, 2026, as the payout date, according to the supplied announcement. The company’s total employee headcount stood at 332,542 as of September 30, 2026, compared with 328,062 in the previous quarter. Last-twelve-month voluntary attrition eased to 12.7% from 13% in Q1 FY27 and 14.3% a year earlier. Women accounted for 39.8% of the workforce.
Infosys delivered year-on-year profit and revenue growth in Q2 FY27, supported by demand for technology transformation and AI services. However, its decision to lower FY27 revenue growth guidance signals a more cautious outlook. Investors will be watching deal conversion, AI revenue momentum, margins and future demand trends for signs of sustained growth.

"We are advising some of the largest global enterprise on their AI strategy and continue to invest in deep domain and technology capabilities to bring new ideas and an integrated ecosystem to help businesses unlock AI value at scale," he added.

Infosys collaborated with Mondelez International to drive its supply chain transformation through AI-enabled decision-making, data standardization, and intelligent enterprise workflows. Sanjay Gurbaxani, Global Vice President, Digital Supply Chain, Mondelez International, said, "From digitally connected supply chain to standardizing data and enabling more informed decision-making, the opportunity lies in bringing together people, processes, data, and technology to deliver meaningful business outcomes. As AI evolves towards agentic AI, the potential extends beyond generating insights to enable more autonomous, responsive, and intelligent workflows. The real value comes from embedding intelligence into everyday business decisions, rethinking established processes, and scaling solutions across the enterprise. With Infosys we are building a compelling solution where technology, aligned with business priorities, can become a catalyst for operational excellence and long-term impact."

Tom Britt, Chief Information Officer, Crocs, Inc. said, "As our organization reimagines its IT landscape, we sought a collaborator who could combine deep domain expertise with a commitment to innovation and operational excellence. By leveraging Infosys' proven delivery frameworks and advanced automation capabilities, we will optimize operations, reduce costs and scale responsibly—while driving continuous improvement and building a foundation for sustainable growth and digital resilience that positions Crocs, Inc. for the future."

Satheeskaran Navaratnam, Chief Digital Officer & VP Transformation & Governance IT, Knorr-Bremse, said, "At Knorr-Bremse, we are building a future-ready technology foundation that supports innovation and long-term value creation. By working with Infosys, we aim to make our technology estate as optimized and reliable as the systems we build for our customers, ensuring that every layer of our infrastructure is equipped to support the pace of change our business demands."
Infosys expanded collaboration with Metsä Group to drive AI-led transformation of its IT landscape. Kristiina Lammila, Chief Information Officer of Metsä Group, said, "This engagement marks a new chapter in Metsä's long-standing collaboration with Infosys, as we simplify and transform our IT sourcing model to meet the efficiency demands of today's business environment. We are confident in our joint ability to deliver on these targets and accelerate the transformation of Metsä's IT, powered by AI."

Kenji Kitazato, Head - ICT Strategy Department, NTN Corporation, said, "This migration to SAP Commerce Cloud powered by Infosys has streamlined our IT operations, improved agility, and laid a strong foundation for future digital growth. This transformation enables us to utilize this new foundation and further promote the use of digital technology."
Infosys collaborated with Telia to drive AI-powered transformation across its network and cybersecurity operations. Hein Müskens, Group CIO, Telia, said, "Infosys' proven expertise in AI, automation, and telecom transformation made them the ideal partner for this initiative. Leveraging Infosys Topaz and deep industry knowledge, we look forward to accelerating the modernization of our network and cybersecurity operations, enhancing efficiency and agility, and strengthening our foundation for future innovation."

Jaap van Riel, CTO, KnitWell Group, said, "Our relationship with our customers truly comes to life in our stores. Once we identified the opportunity, Infosys was quick to develop a solution and approach. From there, we engineered and built Engage together, and we've seen great results."

Lyndon Subroyen, Global Head of Digital and Technology for Investec Group, said, "Our partnership with Infosys Finacle and Microsoft Azure marks a step change in our digital transformation journey. Digital is no longer a layer that supports the business, it is integral to how we grow, deepen client relationships, and improve our efficiency."

title: What Infosys (INFY) Said on Its Q2 Earnings Call
snippet: Infosys (NYSE:INFY) reported 1.5% year-over-year revenue growth in constant currency for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, while raising its emphasis on artificial intelligence services and ...
content:
Key Points  
    -       Interested in Infosys Ltd.? Here are five stocks we like better.  
-       AI momentum and large deals strengthened Infosys' future growth prospects: AI revenue rose 29% sequentially to 10.5% of total revenue, while the company signed 19 large contracts worth $5.2 billion, including a new seven-year financial-services deal exceeding $2 billion.  
-       Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was cut to 1%–2% growth because of weaker volumes, slower discretionary spending, lower pricing increases and intensified competition, particularly in retail and high-tech. Operating-margin guidance was maintained at 20%–22%.  
-       Second-quarter operating margin held at 21%, while free cash flow reached $928 million and the company maintained a debt-free balance sheet. Infosys also declared a 26-rupee interim dividend and increased headcount by about 4,400 employees.  
Infosys (NYSE:INFY) reported 1.5% year-over-year revenue growth in constant currency for the second quarter of fiscal 2027, while raising its emphasis on artificial intelligence services and large-deal execution amid cautious client spending and heightened pricing competition.  
        Revenue totaled $5.145 billion, up 1.2% sequentially in constant currency terms. CEO and Managing Director Salil Parekh said AI revenue grew 29% sequentially and represented 10.5% of total revenue, compared with 8.2% in the previous quarter. The company said its AI work is increasingly tied to enterprise-scale transformation programs, modernization projects and operational efficiency initiatives.  
        → Bloom Energy Just Reported—Its Biggest Order Is Still Waiting on a Pipeline  
            "As enterprises adopt AI at scale, another quarter of strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of a differentiated market positioning and client confidence," Parekh said. He added that AI is now part of almost every large transaction Infosys is pursuing, including programs focused on customer service, quality improvement, growth, cost optimization and technology modernization.  
            Large deals provide future growth visibility  
        Infosys signed 19 large deals with total contract value of $5.2 billion during the quarter, its second-highest quarterly TCV over the past five years, according to CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka. About 62% of the bookings were net new.  
        → Chefs' Warehouse Has Rallied 76%—Can the Stock Keep Climbing?  
             The company highlighted two mega deals. One was a net-new, seven-year financial-services contract valued at more than $2 billion. Transition on the contract is expected to begin in the second half of the fourth quarter, and management expects it to contribute more than 1 percentage point of company revenue growth in fiscal 2028. Infosys also renewed an existing financial-services contract valued at $1 billion.  
            Parekh said the net-new mega deal involves business transformation using AI to improve technology and operations work. He said the contract includes some employee transfers but no asset transfers, and the company does not expect a material margin impact from the transition this year.  
          → Why Western Digital's AI Storage Boom Defies the Chip Sell-Off  
       For the first half, Infosys recorded $8.8 billion in large-deal wins, up 28% year over year, with 62% of bookings classified as net new. Financial services accounted for more than $3.5 billion of second-quarter deal signings.  
       Management said the large-deal pipeline remains healthy and includes additional mega-deal opportunities. Parekh said the company expects its organic business to be "in a good shape" next year, citing AI momentum, the signed mega deal and the deal pipeline.  
       Guidance reduced as volume and pricing lag expectations  
       Infosys revised its fiscal 2027 constant-currency revenue growth forecast to 1% to 2%, reflecting softer-than-expected first-half performance and its updated assessment of the remainder of the year. The company maintained its operating-margin guidance of 20% to 22%.  
       Sanghrajka said quarterly growth came in below expectations because of softer volumes, lower-than-anticipated pricing increases and slower discretionary spending, particularly in retail and high-tech. He said competitive intensity has increased in recent quarters, limiting the pricing expansion Infosys had expected at the beginning of the year.  
          Management said the lower end of its guidance assumes a further deterioration in macroeconomic conditions and pricing, while the upper end assumes improvement. The second half also includes seasonal headwinds from fewer working days.  
       Infosys said its growth outlook has also been affected by lower revenue from offshoring and by a large European manufacturing deal that it did not pursue because the economics did not meet its return expectations. Management said those two factors combined represented an estimated 1.8% to 2% impact on growth for the year.  
       Financial services and energy, utilities, resources and services are expected to grow faster than the company average, according to Sanghrajka. Manufacturing faces near-term pressure, including lower revenue from a large client, while retail and high-tech were affected by lower third-party revenues and weaker spending among certain customers.  
       Margins hold at 21% as AI productivity reshapes commercial discussions  
       Second-quarter operating margin was 21%, down 10 basis points sequentially. Sanghrajka cited a 70-basis-point headwind from changes in post-sales customer support and a 20-basis-point impact from additional acquisition consolidation. These were partly offset by currency, Project Maximus efficiency measures and higher working days.  
          For the second half, Infosys expects margin pressure from compensation increases, acquisition-related amortization, seasonally softer revenue, large-deal ramp-ups and continued sharing of AI-driven productivity benefits with clients. Project Maximus initiatives are expected to partly offset those pressures.  
       Management said clients across industries are increasingly seeking to share in productivity gains from AI, creating pricing pressure in both existing and new contracts. Parekh said the intensity of client productivity expectations has remained broadly similar since the start of the fiscal year, but the trend is reaching more parts of the company's portfolio as AI adoption expands.  
       Infosys said it remains selective about contracts where expected productivity commitments exceed its economic-return thresholds. Parekh said the company is focused on realizing measurable productivity benefits rather than relying on assumptions about gains that may emerge years into a multi-year contract.  
          Cash flow, hiring and dividend  
       Free cash flow totaled $928 million, equal to 113% of net profit. Infosys ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents and no debt. Earnings per share rose 8.7% year over year to 19.32 Indian rupees.  
       The board declared an interim dividend of 26 rupees per share, up 13% from a year earlier. Attrition declined to 12.7% from 13% in the prior quarter, while net headcount increased by about 4,400 employees. Infosys hired roughly 13,000 freshers in the first half and said it remains on track to hire approximately 20,000 for the full fiscal year.  
       Management also said compensation increases for most employees will begin in October, with a second phase scheduled for January.  
       About Infosys (NYSE:INFY)  
       Infosys Ltd. is a digital services and consulting company, which engages in the provision of end-to-end business solutions. It operates through the following segments: Financial Services, Retail, Communication, Energy, Utilities, Resources, and Services, Manufacturing, Hi-Tech, Life Sciences, and All Other. The company was founded by Dinesh Krishnan Swamy, Senapathy Gopalakrishnan, Narayana Ramarao Nagavara Murthy, Raghavan N. S., Ashok Arora, Nandan M. Nilekani, and S. D. Shibulal on July 2, 1981 and is headquartered in Bangalore, India.

title: Infosys Q2 Results: PAT Jumps 6% YoY To Rs 7,823 Crore, Cuts FY27 Revenue Guidance - Full Earnings Report
snippet: The company has lowered its FY27 guidance to 1% to 2% in revenue from earlier 1.5% to 3% forecast. Meanwhile, operating margins guidance is between 20-22%.
content:
Infosys Q2 Results: PAT Jumps 6% YoY To Rs 7,823 Crore, Cuts FY27 Revenue Guidance - Full Earnings Report
Tech giant, Infosys has declared its Q2 results on October 23, 2026. The company bagged a consolidated net profit of Rs 7,823 crore in Q2FY27, registering a growth of 6.2% YoY. Meanwhile, revenue from operations surged by 10.7% YoY. However, Infosys has lowered its revenue guidance for FY27.
Infosys had posted a net profit of Rs 7,364 crore in September 2025 quarter.
Compared to the preceding quarter, Infosys reported 0.7% growth from Rs 7,769 crore in June 2026 quarter.
On the top-line front, Infosys posted revenue from operations at Rs 49,244 crore in Q2FY27, registering a growth of 10.7% from Rs 44,490 crore revenue in Q2FY26. The revenue surged by 2.1% from Rs 48,211 crore in Q1FY27.
EBIT margin stood flat at 21% on year-on-year basis, but slipped 1 basis points from 21.1% margins in Q1FY27. EBITDA came in at Rs 10,330 crore, recording a growth of 10.4% YoY and 1.6% QoQ.
During the quarter under review, Infosys delivered $5,145 million in Q2 revenues, year on year growth of 1.5% and sequential growth of 1.2% in constant currency. Operating margin was stable at 21.0%. EPS growth was 8.7% year on year in rupee terms. TCV of large deal wins was $5.2 billion, with 62% net new.
Meanwhile, H1 revenues grew at 1.9% year on year in constant currency. Operating margin for H1 was at 21.0%.
"We had strong large deals of $5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over $2 billion, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex transformation programs. Our AI revenue was at 10.5% and grew 29% quarter-on-quarter. As enterprises move to AI adoption at scale, the strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of our differentiated market positioning and client confidence," said Salil Parekh, CEO and MD.
He added, "We are advising some of the largest global enterprise on their AI strategy and continue to invest in deep domain and technology capabilities to bring new ideas and an integrated ecosystem to help businesses unlock AI value at scale."
The company has lowered its FY27 guidance to 1% to 2% in revenue from earlier 1.5% to 3% forecast. Meanwhile, operating margins guidance is between 20-22%.
"We delivered operating margins of 21.0% in Q2 amidst heightened volatility. Focus on cost and operational efficiency measures while making the required investments, have led to stable margins," said
Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO. "Free cash flow of $928 million, representing 113.3% of net profit, underscores the financial strength of the business," he added.
Infosys has declared an interim dividend of Rs 26 per share for FY27.

Bengaluru-based IT services major Infosys reported net profit of Rs 7,823 crore for the quarter ending September 30, 2026, a 6.2 percent growth year-on-year. The company's revenue from operations grew to Rs 49,244 crore for Q2 FY27, an 11 percent increase over the corresponding quarter in FY26.
While Infosys does not disclose its AI revenues separately, the company reported a 29 percent sequential growth quarter-on-quarter, as per the press statement issued by the company. As of date, Infosys' AI revenue stood at 10.5 percent of total revenue, said CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO at Infosys.
"We had strong large deals of $5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over $2 billion, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex transformation programs. Our AI revenue was at 10.5 percent and grew 29 percent quarter-on-quarter. As enterprises move to AI adoption at scale, the strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of our differentiated market positioning and client confidence,” said CEO and Managing Director of Infosys Salil Parekh in the statement.

title: Infosys Share Price: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold After Q2 Results? Here’s What Brokerage has to Say
snippet: The IT stock reported over USD 5 billion in Q2 FY27 deal wins but reduced FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1-2% due to weak ...
content:
The article outlines the global brokerage outlook on the company, which provides consulting, technology, outsourcing, and next-generation digital services to enable clients to execute strategies for their digital transformation.
With a market capitalization of Rs 4,60,919 crore, Infosys Ltd’s share was last trading at Rs 1,136 per share, down by 1.62 percent from its previous close. The stock of the company gave a negative return of 25 percent over the last year.
Brokerage Outlook on the Share
UBS on Infosys
UBS has maintained a Buy rating on Infosys with a target price of Rs 1,415, indicating 23 percent upside. However, the brokerage flagged weaker-than-expected Q2 FY27 performance and a further cut in the company's FY27 revenue growth guidance.
Revenue Growth Misses Estimates
Infosys reported revenue growth of 1.2 percent QoQ in constant currency terms in Q2 FY27, below UBS estimates of 1.5 percent and the consensus estimate of 1.8 percent. The brokerage also noted that the reported EPS of Rs 19.3 fell short of its estimate of Rs 19.5.
Margin Performance Remains Under Pressure
The company's EBIT margin declined 10 basis points QoQ to 21 percent, missing UBS estimates of 21.3 percent and the consensus estimate of 21.2 percent. The margin performance added to concerns around profitability as the company navigates a challenging demand environment.
FY27 Guidance Cut
Infosys revised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1 to 2 percent YoY in constant currency terms, while retaining its EBIT margin guidance of 20 to 22 percent. The guidance cut signals continued caution around demand and near-term growth prospects.
Nomura on Infosys
Nomura has maintained a Buy rating on Infosys with a target price of Rs 1,300. While the brokerage noted a modest miss in Q2 FY27, it highlighted strong deal wins and attractive valuations as key factors supporting its positive stance on the stock.
Modest Miss in Q2 FY27
Infosys reported a modest miss against expectations in Q2 FY27, according to Nomura. However, the brokerage believes the quarterly performance needs to be viewed alongside the company's strong deal wins, which could support future revenue growth despite the current demand challenges.
Guidance Cut Slightly Higher Than Expected
Nomura noted that the reduction in FY27 revenue growth guidance was slightly higher than anticipated. The company retained its EBIT margin guidance of 20 to 22 percent, indicating that management continues to expect margins to remain within the stated range despite uncertain revenue growth.
Attractive Valuations
Nomura highlighted that Infosys was trading at 14.2 times its estimated FY28 earnings per share of Rs 81. The brokerage maintained its Buy rating and Rs 1,300 target price, with the valuation offering support to its investment view despite near-term growth concerns.
HSBC on Infosys
HSBC has maintained a Hold rating on Infosys with a target price of Rs 1,110. The brokerage noted that the company lowered its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1 to 2 percent, placing it at the lower end of the peer range, while highlighting a large deal win as a positive.
Revenue Guidance at the Lower End
Infosys revised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1 to 2 percent, which HSBC noted was at the lower end of the peer range. This reflects the challenges facing the company as client spending remains cautious and demand conditions continue to be subdued.
USD 2 Billion Mega Deal
HSBC highlighted the USD 2 billion mega deal as a positive development for Infosys. The deal is expected to contribute around 1 percent to revenue growth in FY28, potentially supporting the company's growth outlook as it works through near-term demand challenges.
Wage Hikes Could Pressure Margins
HSBC expects margins to come under pressure in the second half of FY27 due to wage hikes. While the large deal win provides some support to the growth outlook, the brokerage maintained its Hold rating and Rs 1,110 target price amid concerns around growth and profitability.
Goldman Sachs on Infosys
Goldman Sachs has maintained a Neutral rating on Infosys with a target price of Rs 1,000. The brokerage viewed Q2 FY27 results as largely in line with expectations but flagged the second consecutive guidance cut, weak demand and continued pricing pressure as key concerns.
Second Consecutive Guidance Cut
Infosys reduced its FY27 revenue growth guidance for the second consecutive quarter. Goldman Sachs noted that the midpoint of the revised guidance implies slightly negative organic revenue growth for FY27, highlighting the challenges facing the company in converting current demand into revenue growth.
Strong Deal Wins Provide Some Support
Goldman Sachs highlighted strong deal wins during Q2 FY27, including a mega deal that could partly offset revenue headwinds in FY28 following the exit of a manufacturing client. However, the brokerage noted that client-specific ramp-downs, subdued volume growth and changing spending priorities continue to weigh on demand.
Pricing Pressure and Margin Concerns
Infosys continues to operate in a challenging environment marked by elevated competition and pricing pressure, according to Goldman Sachs. The brokerage also noted that clients are demanding higher productivity through AI, although management views the resulting productivity-related deflation as a one-time exercise.
Citi on Infosys
Citi has maintained a Neutral rating on Infosys with a target price of Rs 1,105. The brokerage noted that Q2 FY27 revenue and EBIT were largely in line with expectations, while total contract value (TCV) of deals exceeded USD 5 billion, providing a positive signal for future business momentum.
Organic Growth Outlook Weakens
Citi highlighted that the midpoint of Infosys' FY27 organic revenue guidance now implies a 0.2 percent YoY decline. This compares with expected growth of 0.6 percent after Q1 FY27 and 2.3 percent at the start of FY27, reflecting a weaker growth outlook.
Strong Deal Pipeline
Infosys' trailing 12-month deal TCV increased 41 percent YoY, while Q2 FY27 deal TCV exceeded USD 5 billion. Citi viewed this as a positive indicator of business momentum, although cautious client spending continues to create uncertainty around the pace of revenue conversion.
Mega Deal Could Offset Client Loss
Citi noted that the new mega deal could address some concerns about Infosys entering FY28 at a disadvantage following the loss of a European manufacturing client. However, the brokerage retained its Neutral rating, with FY27 and FY28 earnings estimates revised marginally by 0 to 1 percent.
About the Company
Infosys Limited is a Bengaluru-based IT services company that provides digital services, business consulting and technology solutions to clients worldwide. Founded in 1981, the company operates across 59 countries, serving more than 2,000 active clients with a workforce of over 300,000 employees.
Financial Highlight: Revenue increased to Rs 49,244 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 44,490 crore in Q2 FY26, registering an 11 percent growth YoY. EBIDT rose to Rs 11,689 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 10,535 crore in Q2 FY26, up 11 percent YoY. Net profit increased to Rs 7,838 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 7,375 crore in Q2 FY26, up 6 percent YoY. EPS increased to Rs 19.28 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 17.73 in Q2 FY26, up 9 percent YoY.

Amazon stock rises as AWS growth meets $220 billion AI spend
Published on 11/10/2026 at 16:20 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWS
AWS growth meets heavier AI spending
- AWS revenue accelerated sharply in the third quarter, while operating income and the operating margin reached new highs.
- Amazon's holiday-quarter forecast puts retail demand, advertising and infrastructure execution at the center of the next investor test.
- Free cash flow remains under pressure as artificial intelligence investment drives higher capital spending.
Amazon stock traded at 243.30 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:08 CET on Tuesday, November 10, 1.63 percent above the Xetra close of Monday, November 9. The quote was 4.31 percent above the 233.25 euros recorded in the previous report on Friday, November 6.
That move adds a fresh market signal to an investment debate that remains centered on AWS acceleration and the cost of building artificial intelligence capacity.
What has changed since our last report
Amazon.com Inc. released its third-quarter results on Thursday, October 29, according to the company's official results release. AWS revenue rose 39.3 percent year over year to 46.0 billion US dollars, while AWS operating income reached 17.8 billion US dollars from 11.4 billion US dollars a year earlier.
Group operating income increased 61 percent to 28.1 billion US dollars, lifting the operating margin to a record 13.9 percent. Net income fell to 20.7 billion US dollars, mainly because the year-earlier quarter benefited from a substantial pre-tax gain related to Amazon's Anthropic investment.
AI spending keeps cash in focus
Amazon's operating cash flow rose 29 percent to 168.3 billion US dollars on a trailing-twelve-month basis. Free cash flow, however, swung to an outflow of 42.4 billion US dollars from an inflow of 14.8 billion US dollars a year earlier as property and equipment purchases increased, primarily for artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The company continues to expect cash capital expenditures of approximately 220 billion US dollars for 2026. Chief Executive Andy Jassy said AWS growth should exceed 40 percent in both 2027 and 2028, raising the potential payoff from the spending while also increasing the execution burden.
Holiday quarter sets next test
Amazon expects fourth-quarter net sales of 240.0 billion to 247.0 billion US dollars and operating income of 28.5 billion to 33.5 billion US dollars. Advertising revenue is expected to grow in the high teens, leaving seasonal retail demand and delivery capacity as additional variables for the next earnings assessment.

title: Amazon Q3 2026 10-Q Analysis: AWS Margins and Capex Surge
