content:
Loading blog posts...
November 3, 2026 • 3 min read
Amazon’s quarterly earnings reports are massive, complex documents that often conceal the real operational drivers beneath retail volume, cloud infrastructure, and non-operating accounting adjustments. The goal here is to dig into the income statement from Amazon's latest 10-Q filing to see how the core business is performing, unpack where profitability is concentrating, and evaluate what the numbers reveal about the company's aggressive technological and capital investments.
During the third quarter of 2026, Amazon generated $201.9 billion in net sales, representing a 12% year-over-year increase from $180.2 billion. While consolidated top-line growth remained steady, core profitability surged. Operating income—the profit remaining after covering direct production costs and regular operational expenses—jumped 61% from $17.4 billion to $28.1 billion, lifting Amazon's quarterly operating margin to 13.9%.
The primary engine behind this operating leverage is Amazon Web Services (AWS), which provides cloud infrastructure, compute power, and data storage. AWS net sales climbed 39% year-over-year to $46.0 billion, contributing roughly 23% of company-wide revenue. More importantly, AWS produced $17.8 billion in operating profit, delivering an exceptional 38.7% operating margin and accounting for more than 63% of Amazon's total quarterly operating earnings. Higher-margin Advertising services also advanced to $19.6 billion (up 11%), while core commerce units such as Online stores ($68.5 billion) and Third-party seller services ($46.5 billion) provided steady volume.
Despite the $10.7 billion surge in operating income, Amazon's quarterly net income dipped slightly from $21.2 billion in Q3 2025 to $20.7 billion in Q3 2026. This divergence illustrates how non-operating accounting marks can disconnect reported net earnings from operating performance.
Under U.S. GAAP, observable transaction prices for private equity holdings require companies to adjust their carrying values through non-operating income. In Q3 2025, Amazon recorded a $7.2 billion upward valuation adjustment, driven by observable valuation gains in its nonvoting preferred stock in artificial intelligence safety startup Anthropic, PBC. In Q3 2026, that quarterly adjustment dropped to just $39 million, alongside higher net interest expense of $504 million following extensive corporate debt issuances. Over the full nine-month period, cumulative Anthropic valuation gains totaled an astonishing $62.9 billion, demonstrating how strategic venture-scale generative AI holdings can induce substantial volatility in headline net income.
Beneath expanding profit margins lies an unprecedented acceleration in capital deployment. Cash purchases of property and equipment escalated to $77.3 billion in the quarter alone, bringing trailing twelve-month capital expenditures (net of proceeds) to $210.7 billion. This intensive spending pushed trailing twelve-month free cash flow—cash generated from operations minus net capital expenditures—deep into negative territory at $(42.4 billion), down from positive $14.8 billion over the prior period. Furthermore, management reaffirmed that full-year 2026 cash capital expenditures are expected to reach approximately $220 billion.
This spending spree reflects an intensifying cloud and artificial intelligence infrastructure race against hyperscale rivals like Microsoft Azure and Alphabet's Google Cloud. Amazon is channeling immense capital into proprietary AI chips, expanded data centers, and dedicated energy contracts to satisfy surging enterprise cloud demand. While AWS's accelerating 39% growth and robust margins provide strong operational justification, sustained negative free cash flow leaves little margin for error if cloud demand moderates or monetization timelines lengthen.

title: Bank Stocks Are Trading at 14.3x PE Despite 19.4% Credit Growth; Are Gold Loans and Credit Cards Changing the Valuation Story?
snippet: The key question is whether strong credit growth and improving asset quality can offset funding pressures and justify current valuations as gold loans in focus.
content:
India's banking space is seeing credit growth, but the valuation of the banking stocks suggest that the market remains wary of its capacity to sustain earnings. The P/E of the banking sector was at 14.33x as of October 19, 2026, IIFL Capital reported in a note which comprised of 41 listed stocks with a combined market capitalisation of around Rs 54.06 lakh crore.
Bank credit grew 19.4% on a yearly basis to reach Rs.229.95 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, compared to 17.8% increase in deposits to Rs.283.96 lakh crore. As such, the credit to deposit ratio stands at around 81%, indicating that banks are lending significantly higher amount than what they mobilize in terms of deposits. The question remains regarding the sustainability of earnings without having to erode the earnings margin or asset quality.
Loan Books Are Growing, but the Underlying Picture Is Different
The latest Q2 FY27 results of ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Federal Bank and Punjab National Bank provide a useful comparison. While all four banks reported double-digit advances growth, the composition of lending and dependence on different funding sources varied considerably.
| Bank | Advances (Rs lakh crore) | Advances (Rs lakh crore) | Deposits growth YoY | 
| ICICI Bank | 18.32 | 30.0% | 27.1% | 
| Axis Bank | 13.7 | 23.0% | 21.0% | 
| Federal Bank | 2.98 | 22.0% | 19.0% | 
| Punjab National Bank | 13.41 | 14.7% | 9.9% | 
The headline growth numbers, however, need some adjustments. ICICI Bank's advances growth drops from 30% to 24.1% after stripping out the loan growth from international branches against FCNR(B) deposits. Axis Bank's comparable growth falls from 23% to 19% while PNB's advances from domestic operations grew only 12.5% against global growth of 14.7%. So higher lending growth does not necessarily mean proportionately higher domestic credit demand.
The mix of the loan book is important in understanding the scope of profitability. At ICICI Bank retail and rural lending grew 14.8% to Rs 9.46 lakh crore, while business banking jumped 33.8% to Rs 3.89 lakh crore and domestic corporate lending grew 30.6% to Rs 3.55 lakh crore. Axis Bank's retail book grew 16% to Rs 7.40 lakh crore, constituting roughly 54% of advances, while SME and corporate loans grew 25% and 34% respectively. PNB's retail, agriculture and MSME portfolio grew 13.6% to Rs 7.22 lakh crore, representing 57.4% of domestic advances.
Gold Loans Are Surging While Credit Card Lending Slows
One of the more noticeable developments within retail lending is the rapid expansion of gold-backed loans, even as credit-card advances have contracted at some large private banks.
ICICI Bank's jewel loan portfolio grew by Rs 24,691 crore to Rs 55,794 crore in one year compared to Rs 31,103 crore while credit card advances dropped by Rs 5,709 crore in the same period. Federal Bank's gold loan portfolio grew by an additional Rs 11,978 crore to Rs 44,242 crore and constitutes approximately 27% of its internally classified retail banking portfolio. Gold loans provide collateral security and attractive yield, Federal Bank reports a gold-loan yield of 10.4% and a loan-to-value ratio of approximately 61%. Rapid growth makes earnings increasingly sensitive to the valuation of the collateral, underwriting standards and the ability to realise loans if gold prices fall.
The credit-card business is not a happy hunting ground. Axis Bank has added about 10.9 lakh new cards in Q2 FY27, but its outstanding advances on credit cards have fallen 3% to Rs 45,422 crore versus a year ago. And this is a key point. There is no guarantee that a rise in cards issued will immediately result in a proportionate increase in the amount of money lent on credit cards.
The case for credit cards is that they carry higher yield as well as higher fees, but they are also completely unsecured exposures at the bank, where the potential for loss is higher. The difference in performance between Federal Bank and ICICI Bank and Axis Bank also suggests a nuanced view of the credit-card situation. Here, the emphasis needs to be on the situation on the lending front for individual banks, rather than an overarching sector view.
Deposit Competition Is Putting Bank Margins to the Test
Funding costs continue to be another factor that determines whether expanding loan books result in increased earnings. ICICI Bank's net interest margin decreased despite an increase in their cost of deposits just from 4.41% to 4.50%. Axis Bank, on the other hand recorded a NIM of 3.36%, compared to 3.47% if the impact of FCNR(B) deposits were excluded. Federal Bank improved its margin helped by a fall in deposit costs from 5.61% to 5.21%. PNB's domestic NIM improved to 2.74% from 2.72% a year earlier. The differences in margins also translate into considerable variation in asset-level profitability and returns to shareholders.
| Bank | Q2 FY27 NIM | ROA | ROE | Gross NPA | Net NPA | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ICICI Bank | 4.18% | 2.26% | 16.60% | 1.20% | 0.30% | 
| Axis Bank | 3.36% | 1.38% | 13.30% | 1.16% | 0.35% | 
| Federal Bank | 3.32% | 1.32% | 13.57% | 1.32% | 0.17% | 
| PNB | 2.58% | 1.05% | 17.32% | 2.55% | 0.25% | 
Strong Profit Growth Is Supported by Improving Asset Quality
Funding costs continue to play a role in translating growing loan books into higher earnings. ICICI Bank's net interest margin fell from 4.36 % in Q1 FY27 to 4.18 % in Q2 FY27, even though its cost of deposits increased only marginally from 4.41 % to 4.50 %. Axis Bank reported a NIM of 3.36 %, which would have been 3.47 %, excluding the impact of FCNR (B) deposits. Federal Bank improved its margin from 3.06 % a year ago to 3.32 %, helped by a decrease in deposit costs from 5.61 % to 5.21 %. PNB's domestic NIM improved to 2.74 % from 2.72 % a year earlier.
Despite financing worries, quarterly profits were healthy. ICICI Bank's net profit grew 20.1% to Rs 14,843 crore, boosted by 17.7% growth in net interest income to Rs 25,339 crore. Axis Bank's jumped 38% to Rs 7,003 crore, but its core operating profit grew more slowly 11%. Federal Bank's profit grew 45% to Rs 1,386 crore while PNB reported 12.8% growth to Rs 5,532 crore. These differences justify the market's assessment of core operating income, provisioning requirements and recurrent returns.
Gross NPA: ICICI Bank's gross NPA ratio fell from 1.58% to 1.20%, and that of Axis Bank improved to 1.16%. Federal Bank lowered its gross NPA ratio from 1.83% to 1.32%, while PNB reported a 90-basis point improvement to 2.55%. But given the expansion in their loan books, current NPA ratios may understate possible credit losses in recently originated loans and normalized credit costs and future slippages are important for assessing sustainable earnings.
Are Current Valuations Justified by Returns on Equity?
PNB is trading near its reported book value but has recorded a higher quarterly ROE than the three private banks. However, its ROA (1.05%) versus ICICI Bank (2.26%) suggests that it is generating significantly lower profits from its assets. On the other hand, ICICI Bank's higher valuation suggests that it has better operating profitability and quality of assets, but it needs to maintain its ROE and earnings growth to justify its ~2.75x book valuation.
A simple residual-income valuation illustrates the sensitivity of bank valuations to profitability assumptions. Assuming a 12% cost of equity and sustainable 7% annual book-value growth, the theoretical justified P/B multiples change as follows.
| Sustainable ROE | Illustrative justified P/B | 
|---|---|
| 13% | 1.20x | 
| 16% | 1.80x | 
| 18% | 2.20x | 
Their analysis shows that a relatively small increase in sustainable ROE can have a big impact on the price investors should be willing to pay for book value. A bank that is expanding advances by 20% but realizing inadequate returns on the incremental capital could well deserve a lower multiple than a less aggressive competitor with superior profitability and risk management.
Future Outlook: Can Loan Growth Translate Into Shareholder Value?
The outlook for FY27 and FY28 will depend increasingly on the quality of credit expansion. Gold loans can support secured lending growth and margins, while credit-card portfolios could provide higher fee and interest income if asset quality remains controlled. However, deposit mobilisation, higher funding requirements and potential credit losses could offset these benefits. The sector's 14.33x P/E is consequently not sufficient evidence of undervaluation on its own. The more important question is which banks can convert expanding loan books into sustainable returns above their cost of equity, without taking disproportionate credit or funding risks.

title: ICICI Bank extends rally, soars 10% in 4 days; market cap nears ₹11 trn
snippet: ICICI Bank's share price extended its up move, hitting a new high of ₹1,526.35, gaining 2 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s ...
content:
ICICI Bank extends rally, soars 10% in 4 days; market cap nears ₹11 trn
ICICI Bank's market cap touched ₹10.96 trillion on the BSE in intraday trade on Friday, BSE data shows.
Listen to This Article
ICICI Bank share price movement
ICICI Bank's share price extended its up move, hitting a new high of ₹1,526.35, gaining 2 per cent on the BSE in Friday’s intraday deals. In the past two trading days, the stock price of the private sector lender rallied 7 per cent, while it soared 10 per cent in the past four trading days. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was up 0.56 per cent at 79,757 at 11:04 AM.
 
A sharp rally in ICICI Bank's stock price lifted the bank's market capitalisation (market cap) toward a record ₹11 trillion. In Friday’s intraday deals, ICICI Bank’s market cap touched ₹10.96 trillion, BSE data shows.
 
Currently, HDFC Bank with a market cap of ₹11.89 trillion stands at the number one position in the banking sector ranking, followed by ICICI Bank. In the overall ranking of BSE listed companies, ICICI Bank stood at the fifth position, data shows. 
What’s driving ICICI Bank share price?
Banking and financial services stocks were among the biggest movers on Dalal Street on Thursday, helped by multiple factors, including the ease in bond yields following an oil price plunge, easing inflationary fears, and steady buying by foreign investors over the last few sessions.
Also Read
According to stock exchanges' provisional data, on November 5, 2026, foreign institutional investors (FIIs)/foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) made a net investment of ₹14,975 crore in Indian equities. Meanwhile, till November 5, 2026, FPIs' net investments totalled ₹22,693 crore in Indian equities, NSDL data shows.
Foreign investors’ net inflow on Thursday was their biggest daily purchase in nearly six years. Earlier, on February 24, 2021, they purchased a net amount of ₹28,739 crore which included a large promoter-driven block deal.
 
Meanwhile, ICICI Bank has held the tide and offers a clean play on best-in-class return on asset (ROA). With an upward turning rate cycle, strong improvement in business growth over the past few quarters and support from lower credit costs, return metrics remain strong, analysts at Elara Capital said in the Q2 result update.
 
The brokerage firm believes ICICI Bank has demonstrated strong execution across cycles, supported by healthy growth across segments and controlled asset quality. While margins moderated in Q3 and may remain under pressure in Q4, analysts expect net interest margin (NIM) to improve through the rate-hike cycle, aided by deployment into higher-yielding retail assets. Consistent delivery on key operating metrics positions the bank to sustain earnings momentum.
“We remain confident in the strength of the bank’s underlying franchise and view it as our preferred pick among large private sector peers. We stay constructive on its earnings trajectory. We recommend Buy with a SOTP -based target price of ₹1,720, including ₹219 from subsidiary valuation,” analysts at Elara Capital said.
 
Analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services believe that ICICI Bank is well poised to deliver 2.34 per cent/2.38 per cent RoA over FY27/FY28. Asset quality is among the best in the industry, while a healthy contingency buffer at ₹13,100 crore (0.7 per cent of loans) provides comfort. The brokerage firm raised earnings by 3 per cent for FY28E estimating RoA/RoE of 2.4 per cent/17.6 per cent. ICICI Bank remains a top 'Buy' in the sector with a target price of ₹1,750 (2.5x Mar’28E adjusted book value), the brokerage firm said.
ICICI Bank is better positioned, given lower exposure to riskier sectors and a manageable share of SME/unsecured retail loans. The bank is among the strongest deposit franchises and should thus benefit from deposit polarization, while valuations look attractive, analysts at Jefferies said. In the base case, the brokerage firm has a target price of ₹1,750 and in the upside scenario, the stock’s target price is ₹1,860 per share.
 
ICICI Bank delivered 18 per cent YoY growth in net interest income (NII), higher than Axis at 12 per cent and HDFC Bank at 10 per cent. While core net interest margins (NIMs) fell by 10bps quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) due to a rise in the share of corporate loans and FCNR-B. The brokerage firm said it expects the normalization of the asset mix (from bank balances to loans) and benefits from rate hikes (one-third of loans reprice every month) to aid margins going forward.  ICICI Bank sees a lower impact from cuts in bancassurance fees due to lower contribution to total income. Bank's liquidity coverage ratio (LCR) is at 124 per cent, compared with 113 per cent for HDFC Bank and 119 per cent for Axis Bank, analysts at Jefferies said. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

title: Anup Bagchi takes charge at HDFC Bank: Can he close the gap with ICICI Bank? - CNBC TV18
snippet: HDFC Bank’s incoming CEO Anup Bagchi inherits a powerful franchise but faces a tough investor test: revive deposit momentum, ease margin pressures and improve returns to close the performance gap with ...
content:
Anup Bagchi takes charge at HDFC Bank: Can he close the gap with ICICI Bank?
- Edited bySheersh Kapoor
- Published OnOct 27, 2026 | 05:14 IST
- Last Updated OnOct 27, 2026 | 05:14 IST
Anup Bagchi’s experience at ICICI Bank gives him a valuable perspective on the competitive landscape. He has seen the rival institution from a senior leadership position and subsequently led ICICI Prudential Life, giving him experience across banking and insurance.
When Anup Bagchi takes charge as MD and CEO of HDFC Bank on October 27, he will inherit one of India’s strongest banking franchises. But the challenge is not simply to sustain the bank’s size or keep its balance sheet growing. It is to show that this scale can translate into stronger earnings, better returns and a more compelling proposition for shareholders.
That is where the comparison with ICICI Bank becomes particularly relevant.
Over the past few years, ICICI Bank has emerged as a formidable competitor, delivering stronger earnings momentum and higher net interest margins. Its stock has also outperformed HDFC Bank, reflecting the market’s greater willingness to reward its operating performance. HDFC Bank, meanwhile, has faced questions over its deposit franchise, margin pressures and ability to generate adequate returns following its merger with HDFC Ltd.
Bagchi’s appointment adds an interesting dimension to this contest. He knows the ICICI ecosystem from the inside, having served as an executive director at ICICI Bank before becoming managing director and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance (now ICICI Life Insurance) in 2023. He now takes the helm at HDFC Bank at a time when investors are looking for measurable improvement rather than assurances about its long-term potential.
The question is whether he can accelerate that improvement and narrow the performance gap with a rival that has increasingly set the benchmark.
The earnings gap is becoming harder to ignore
HDFC Bank remains the larger franchise, with substantially higher absolute earnings. But the latest quarterly results underline the difference in momentum between the two banks.
In the September quarter of FY27, HDFC Bank reported net profit of ₹19,510 crore, up 4.7% year-on-year. Its net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned on loans and investments and interest paid on deposits and borrowings, rose 9.7% to ₹34,620 crore.
ICICI Bank, by comparison, reported net profit of ₹14,843 crore, up 20.1% year-on-year, while NII increased 17.7% to ₹25,339 crore.
The distinction is important. HDFC Bank continues to generate more profit in absolute terms, but ICICI Bank’s faster growth points to stronger earnings momentum. For investors, the direction of travel can matter as much as the size of the business.
The margin comparison reinforces that point. HDFC Bank reported a net interest margin (NIM) of 3.16% in Q2 FY27, compared with 4.18% at ICICI Bank. NIM measures the return a bank earns on its interest-bearing assets after accounting for its interest costs, relative to its relevant asset base.
The two banks have different balance-sheet structures and business mixes, so their margin figures should not be interpreted in isolation. Even so, the gap highlights the pressure on HDFC Bank to improve the economics of its lending and funding operations.
For Bagchi, the task is not simply to grow the loan book. It is to ensure that incremental growth generates adequate income and shareholder returns.
Deposits: The problem beneath the headline growth
One of the biggest challenges facing HDFC Bank is the composition and cost of its deposit base.
In Q2 FY27, total deposits rose 18.8% year-on-year to ₹33.27 lakh crore, while gross advances increased 16.3% to ₹32.20 lakh crore. On the surface, both sides of the balance sheet are expanding at a healthy pace, with deposits growing faster than advances.
But the composition of that deposit growth matters.
CASA, or current account and savings account deposits, is generally a lower-cost source of funding than term deposits. In the September quarter, HDFC Bank’s CASA deposits grew 10.8% year-on-year, significantly slower than the 22.8% growth in term deposits. CASA accounted for 31.6% of total deposits.
When a bank relies more heavily on term deposits, it may have to pay more to attract and retain funding. If deposit costs rise faster than the yields on loans and investments, the pressure eventually shows up in margins.
This is particularly important for HDFC Bank because its balance sheet expanded substantially following the merger with HDFC Ltd in July 2023. The enlarged franchise created significant opportunities to cross-sell products, deepen customer relationships and expand lending. But it also increased the importance of mobilising deposits at a competitive cost to fund the larger balance sheet.
The merger changed the scale of the institution. The next phase is about improving the efficiency with which that scale is funded and deployed.
ICICI Bank provides a useful competitive reference point. Its average CASA ratio was reported at 35.8% in Q2 FY27, above HDFC Bank’s 31.6%, although the banks’ CASA measures and deposit movements need to be compared on a consistent basis. The difference nevertheless illustrates why the composition of liabilities is an important competitive variable.
Bagchi will need to strengthen HDFC Bank’s ability to attract primary banking relationships, grow savings and current account balances, and deepen engagement with existing customers. The objective is not simply to raise the CASA ratio as a headline metric, but to improve the overall cost and stability of funding while maintaining competitive deposit growth.
That is easier said than done. Banks compete aggressively for deposits, and customers are increasingly sensitive to the returns available on term deposits. Rebuilding a low-cost deposit franchise requires sustained customer acquisition and engagement, not a quick balance-sheet adjustment.
Can HDFC Bank arrest the pressure on margins?
The deposit mix feeds directly into another key challenge: net interest margin.
HDFC Bank’s NIM fell to 3.16% in Q2 FY27 from 3.26% in the previous quarter. The decline comes as the bank continues to balance lending growth, funding costs and the composition of its assets and liabilities.
A lower margin does not automatically mean that a bank is performing poorly. Margins can be influenced by the interest-rate cycle, changes in the mix of loans and deposits, liquidity conditions and the timing of repricing. But sustained pressure can constrain earnings growth, particularly when the balance sheet is expanding.
For Bagchi, the challenge is to improve the relationship between funding costs and the returns earned on assets. That may involve better deposit mobilisation, sharper pricing discipline, a more favourable business mix and greater efficiency in deploying capital.
ICICI Bank’s reported 4.18% NIM offers a useful reference point, but not a target that HDFC Bank can simply be expected to match. The two banks have different portfolios, funding structures and accounting considerations. The more relevant question is whether HDFC Bank can stabilise its margins and improve them over time while continuing to grow its franchise.
There is also a broader question around earnings quality. In Q2 FY27, HDFC Bank’s NII rose 9.7%, but net profit increased by just 4.7%. Changes in non-interest income, operating expenses and provisions can all affect how much core banking income translates into bottom-line growth.
Investors will therefore be watching more than NIM alone. They will want to see whether stronger core income translates into more consistent profit growth and whether the bank can improve returns without taking on undue credit risk.
Asset quality is holding up. The focus now shifts to returns
HDFC Bank enters Bagchi’s tenure with asset quality that remains broadly stable. Its gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio stood at 1.11% in Q2 FY27, while the net NPA ratio was 0.37%.
That provides an important foundation. A bank seeking to accelerate growth cannot afford to do so at the expense of underwriting standards or future credit costs.
The challenge is to sustain this asset-quality performance while improving profitability. A larger balance sheet is valuable only if it generates adequate returns after funding costs, operating expenses, credit provisions and the capital required to support growth.
For investors, the distinction between growth and value creation is central to the HDFC Bank story. The bank has expanded substantially, particularly following the merger. But the market needs evidence that the enlarged institution can generate stronger returns on its assets and capital.
Return on assets, return on equity, the cost-to-income ratio and the trajectory of margins will be important indicators. So will the bank’s ability to grow loans and deposits without creating an imbalance between funding needs and lending opportunities.
Bagchi’s early performance will be judged on how these metrics move together, rather than on any one quarterly number.
The stock market has been less forgiving
The operational challenges have translated into a broader investor-confidence test.
HDFC Bank’s shares have underperformed ICICI Bank over the recent period, reflecting differing market assessments of their earnings momentum, profitability and execution. Recent market comparisons have shown HDFC Bank substantially weaker year-to-date, while ICICI Bank has delivered a positive return over the same period.
The precise performance depends on the cut-off date, and a like-for-like comparison should use the same dates and account for corporate actions. But the broader point is clear: HDFC Bank’s scale has not, by itself, been enough to secure the market’s confidence.
The merger was a landmark strategic move, combining HDFC Bank’s lending and distribution capabilities with HDFC Ltd’s housing-finance franchise. It also brought a larger balance sheet and a different funding profile. The market’s concern now is less about the logic of the combination and more about how effectively the bank can convert that scale into sustainable financial performance.
Investors will want greater visibility on deposit growth, margin recovery, earnings momentum and returns. They will also be watching execution and leadership continuity as the bank transitions to a new CEO and navigates changes across its senior management team.
For Bagchi, rebuilding confidence will require a sustained run of results that demonstrate progress. A strong statement of intent may set the direction, but only the numbers can establish whether the strategy is working.
Bagchi’s ICICI experience: An advantage, but not a ready-made playbook
Bagchi’s experience at ICICI Bank gives him a valuable perspective on the competitive landscape. He has seen the rival institution from a senior leadership position and subsequently led ICICI Prudential Life, giving him experience across banking and insurance.
That background could help him identify opportunities in customer engagement, product distribution, cross-selling and operational execution. But the HDFC Bank mandate comes with its own institutional realities.
HDFC Bank is a different franchise, with a different balance-sheet structure and a distinct set of post-merger priorities. Its task is not to become ICICI Bank, but to strengthen its own competitive position and deliver returns commensurate with its scale and market standing.
The first phase of Bagchi’s tenure will also be shaped by the need to understand the organisation, engage with stakeholders and establish his priorities. Investors are unlikely to expect every structural issue to be resolved immediately. They will, however, look for a clear set of priorities and evidence that the bank is making progress against them.
The most important early signals may be the trajectory of CASA deposits, the cost of funds, NIM, core earnings growth and returns. Consistency across these measures would do more to improve confidence than an aggressive growth target that comes at the expense of profitability.
The real test: Turning scale into superior performance
HDFC Bank does not need to prove that it can grow. Its balance sheet and market position already establish its scale. The harder task is to show that it can grow profitably, fund that growth efficiently and deliver more consistent returns to shareholders.
That means rebuilding low-cost deposit momentum, managing funding costs, stabilising margins and improving the conversion of core income into profit. It also means sustaining asset quality and giving investors clearer evidence of progress on returns and execution.
ICICI Bank has raised the competitive bar. Its recent earnings growth, stronger margins and stock-market performance have given investors reasons to favour its shares. HDFC Bank must now demonstrate why its own franchise can deliver a compelling outcome.
Bagchi’s experience gives him a strong understanding of the industry and of the competitor he must measure himself against. But his success will ultimately depend on the results he delivers at HDFC Bank.

title: ICICI Bank Q2 profit rises 20.1% to ₹14,843 crore; NIM falls to 4.18%
snippet: ICICI Bank's Q2 profit rose 20.1% to ₹14,843 crore as net interest income grew 17.7%. Loan growth reached 30%, while net interest margin fell to 4.18%.
content:
ICICI Bank reported a 20.1 per cent year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹14,843 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by strong growth in net interest income (NII). The bank posted a profit after tax (PAT) of ₹12,359 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year. However, PAT remained largely flat sequentially.
Net interest income rises 17.7 per cent
The bank’s net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, rose 17.7 per cent to ₹R25,338.7 crore during the reporting quarter, compared with ₹21,529.5 crore a year earlier. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, NII increased 3.9 per cent to ₹24,384.4 crore.
Loan book expands 30 per cent
ICICI Bank’s loan book expanded 30 per cent year-on-year to ₹18.3 lakh crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with ₹14.08 lakh crore in the same period last year. Advances grew 12 per cent sequentially. Excluding the leverage provided on FCNR(B) loans, the bank’s lending grew 24.1 per cent year-on-year and 7.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter.
Deposits grow on FCNR(B) inflows
Deposits rose 27.1 per cent to ₹20.4 lakh crore in the quarter under review, up from ₹16 lakh crore in the year-ago period. Sequentially, deposits rose 11.8 per cent to ₹18 lakh crore from ₹16 lakh crore in the previous quarter.
FCNR(B) inflows contributed significantly to deposit growth. Excluding these NRI inflows, total deposits grew 17 per cent year-on-year and 3.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter as of September 30, 2026.
Net interest margin contracts
Despite strong profitability and business growth, the bank’s margins came under pressure. Net interest margin (NIM) fell to 4.18 per cent in the reporting quarter, down from 4.30 per cent in the year-ago period, a contraction of 12 basis points. The Q2 NIM was also 18 basis points lower than the 4.36 per cent recorded in the previous quarter. Excluding the benefit of interest income from a tax refund, the bank’s NIM stood at 4.28 per cent in the preceding quarter. On this adjusted basis, NIM fell by about 10 basis points in Q2.
Addressing the margin contraction, ICICI Bank Executive Director Sandeep Batra said the decline was largely attributable to the cost of FCNR(B) inflows. “Talking of the decline from 4.28 per cent to 4.18 per cent, it is largely a function of FCNR(B), which results in a higher deposit base and a lower CASA ratio,” Batra said during the media call.

snippet: Oct 17, 2026 · ICICI Bank, the country’s second-largest private sector lender, on Saturday reported a 20.1 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to ₹14,843 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), supported by strong growth in net interest income (NII) and lower provisions. content:
ICICI Bank Q2 net rises 20% to ₹14,843 crore as provisions fall
Net interest income grew 17.7 per cent to ₹25,339 crore, while provisions declined and the gross NPA ratio improved to 1.20 per cent
Listen to This Article
ICICI Bank, the country’s second-largest private sector lender, on Saturday reported a 20.1 per cent year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to ₹14,843 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27), supported by strong growth in net interest income (NII) and lower provisions.
 
NII, the difference between interest earned and interest expended, increased 17.7 per cent year-on-year to ₹25,339 crore.
 
The growth came alongside a 30 per cent increase in the bank’s total loan portfolio to ₹18.32 trillion as of September 30, 2026.
 
Excluding loans provided by its international branches against Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank), or FCNR(B), deposits, the loan portfolio grew 24.1 per cent.
 
NIM moderates to 4.18%
The bank’s net interest margin (NIM) moderated to 4.18 per cent in Q2FY27, compared with 4.30 per cent in the year-ago quarter and 4.36 per cent in the April-June quarter.
Also Read
The bank said the benefit from interest on tax refunds was negligible during the September quarter, compared with 8 basis points in the preceding quarter.
 
Excluding this benefit, NIM in Q1FY27 stood at 4.28 per cent.
 
Core operating profit, excluding treasury income, rose 21.8 per cent year-on-year to ₹20,805 crore.
 
Non-interest income, excluding treasury income, increased 12.5 per cent to ₹8,277 crore, while fee income rose 20.1 per cent to ₹7,795 crore.
Fees from retail, rural and business banking customers accounted for about 75 per cent of total fee income.
 
Operating expenses increased 8.5 per cent year-on-year to ₹12,811 crore.
 
The bank reported a treasury loss of ₹230 crore in Q2FY27, compared with a gain of ₹220 crore in the year-ago quarter, primarily reflecting market movements.
 
Provisions declined 6.9 per cent year-on-year to ₹851 crore from ₹914 crore.
 
Sequentially, provisions fell 32.5 per cent from ₹1,260 crore in Q1FY27.
 
The bank’s gross non-performing assets (GNPA) ratio improved to 1.20 per cent as of September 30, 2026, from 1.38 per cent in the June quarter and 1.58 per cent a year earlier.
The net NPA ratio declined to 0.30 per cent from 0.35 per cent in the preceding quarter and 0.39 per cent a year earlier.
 
Gross NPA additions stood at ₹4,833 crore in Q2FY27, compared with ₹5,034 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.
 
The bank wrote off gross NPAs worth ₹1,592 crore during the quarter.
 
Its provisioning coverage ratio on non-performing loans stood at 75 per cent as of September 30, 2026.
 
ICICI Bank continued to hold contingency provisions of ₹13,100 crore.
 
It also retained an additional standard asset provision of ₹1,283 crore made in Q3FY26 on the Reserve Bank of India’s direction in respect of its agricultural priority sector portfolio, pending completion of a review.
The bank’s total advances grew 30 per cent year-on-year and 12.3 per cent sequentially to ₹18.32 trillion as of September 30, 2026.
 
Excluding loans extended by international branches against FCNR(B) deposits, advances grew 24.1 per cent year-on-year and 7.3 per cent sequentially.
 
The retail and rural loan portfolio grew 14.8 per cent year-on-year, accounting for 51.6 per cent of the total loan portfolio.
 
The business banking portfolio expanded 33.8 per cent, while the domestic corporate portfolio grew 30.6 per cent.
 
Total period-end deposits rose 27.1 per cent year-on-year and 11.8 per cent sequentially to ₹20.50 trillion.
 
Excluding FCNR(B) deposits, deposit growth stood at 17 per cent year-on-year and 3.1 per cent sequentially.
The bank added 145 branches during the first half of FY27, taking its branch network to 7,656 as of September 30, 2026.
 
On a consolidated basis, ICICI Bank reported a net profit of ₹16,333 crore for Q2FY27, compared with ₹13,357 crore in the year-ago quarter, an increase of 22.3 per cent.
 
Consolidated assets grew 22.6 per cent year-on-year to ₹32.93 trillion as of September 30, 2026.

The Board of Directors of ICICI Bank Limited (NSE: ICICIBANK, BSE: 532174, NYSE: IBN) at its meeting held at Mumbai today, approved the standalone and consolidated accounts of the Bank for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1-2027). The statutory auditors have conducted a limited review and have issued an unmodified report on the standalone and consolidated financial statements for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Profit & loss account
Profit before tax excluding treasury increased by 20.9% to ₹ 18,975 crore (US$ 2.0 billion) in Q1-2027 compared to ₹ 15,690 crore (US$ 1.7 billion) in the quarter ended June 30, 2025 (Q1-2026)
Core operating profit increased by 15.6% year-on-year to ₹ 20,235 crore (US$ 2.1 billion) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 17,505 crore (US$ 1.8 billion) in Q1-2026
Core operating profit excluding dividend from subsidiaries increased by 18.3% year-on-year to ₹ 19,125 crore (US$ 2.0 billion) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 16,169 crore (US$ 1.7 billion) in Q1-2026
Net interest income (NII) increased by 12.7% year-on-year to ₹ 24,384 crore (US$ 2.6 billion) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 21,635 crore (US$ 2.3 billion) in Q1-2026
Net interest margin was 4.36% in Q1-2027 compared to 4.32% in Q4-2026 and 4.34% in Q1-2026
Non-interest income, excluding treasury, increased by 16.0% year-on-year to ₹ 8,425 crore (US$ 890 million) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 7,264 crore (US$ 767 million) in Q1-2026
Fee income increased by 23.5% year-on-year to ₹ 7,286 crore (US$ 770 million) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 5,900 crore (US$ 623 million) in Q1-2026. Fees from retail, rural and business banking customers constituted about 72% of total fees in Q1-2027
Operating expenses increased by 10.4% year-on-year to ₹ 12,574 crore (US$ 1.3 billion) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 11,394 crore (US$ 1.2 billion) in Q1-2026
There was a treasury gain of ₹ 151 crore (US$ 16 million) in Q1-2027 as compared to loss of ₹ 106 crore (US$ 11 million) in Q4-2026 and gain of ₹ 1,241 crore (US$ 131 million) in Q1-2026
Provisions (excluding provision for tax) was ₹ 1,260 crore (US$ 133 million) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 1,815 crore (US$ 192 million) in Q1-2026. At June 30, 2026, the Bank continued to hold contingency provision of ₹ 13,100 crore (US$ 1.4 billion), and additional standard asset provision of ₹ 1,283 crore (US$ 136 million) made in Q3-2026 as directed by RBI in respect of the agricultural priority sector portfolio.
Profit before tax increased by 13.0% year-on-year to ₹ 19,126 crore (US$ 2.0 billion) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 16,931 crore (US$ 1.8 billion) in Q1-2026
Profit after tax increased by 15.9% year-on-year to ₹ 14,805 crore (US$ 1.6 billion) in Q1-2027 compared to ₹ 12,768 crore (US$ 1.3 billion) in Q1-2026
Credit growth
Total advances increased by 19.6% year-on-year and 5.0% sequentially to ₹ 16,31,260 crore (US$ 172.3 billion) at June 30, 2026. The retail loan portfolio grew by 12.0% year-on-year and 2.7% sequentially, and comprised 49.2% of the total loan portfolio at June 30, 2026. Including non-fund outstanding, the retail portfolio was 41.1% of the total portfolio at June 30, 2026. The business banking portfolio grew by 28.2% year-on-year and 6.9% sequentially at June 30, 2026. The rural portfolio grew by 35.4% year-on-year and 6.2% sequentially at June 30, 2026. The domestic corporate portfolio grew by 18.5% year-on-year and 6.9% sequentially at June 30, 2026. The domestic advances grew by 18.8% year-on-year and 4.6% sequentially at June 30, 2026.
Deposit growth
Total period-end deposits increased by 14.0% year-on-year and 2.2% sequentially to ₹ 18,33,586 crore (US$ 193.7 billion) at June 30, 2026. Average deposits increased by 14.0% year-on-year and 6.1% sequentially to ₹ 17,48,028 crore (US$ 184.7 billion) in Q1-2027. Average current and savings account deposits increased by 12.1% year-on-year and 4.7% sequentially in Q1-2027.
With the addition of 97 branches during Q1-2027, the Bank had a network of 7,608 branches and 12,190 ATMs & cash recycling machines at June 30, 2026.
Asset quality
The gross NPA ratio was 1.38% at June 30, 2026 compared to 1.40% at March 31, 2026 and 1.67% at June 30, 2025. The net NPA ratio was 0.35% at June 30, 2026 compared to 0.33% at March 31, 2026 and 0.41% at June 30, 2025. The gross NPA additions were ₹ 5,552 crore (US$ 587 million) in Q1-2027 compared to ₹ 6,245 crore (US$ 660 million) in Q1-2026. Recoveries and upgrades of NPAs, excluding write-offs and sale, were ₹ 2,845 crore (US$ 301 million) in Q1-2027 compared to ₹ 3,211 crore (US$ 339 million) in Q1-2026. The net additions to gross NPAs, excluding write-offs and sale, were ₹ 2,707 crore (US$ 286 million) in Q1-2027 compared to ₹ 3,034 crore (US$ 321 million) in Q1-2026. The Bank has written-off gross NPAs amounting to ₹ 1,673 crore (US$ 177 million) in Q1-2027. The provisioning coverage ratio on non-performing loans was 74.7% at June 30, 2026.
Excluding NPAs, the total fund based outstanding to all borrowers under resolution as per the various extant regulations/guidelines declined to ₹ 1,363 crore (US$ 144 million) at June 30, 2026 from ₹ 1,496 crore (US$ 158 million) at March 31, 2026 and ₹ 1,788 crore (US$ 189 million) at June 30, 2025.
The loan and non-fund based outstanding to performing corporate borrowers rated BB and below was ₹ 3,485 crore (US$ 368 million) at June 30, 2026 compared to ₹ 3,519 crore (US$ 372 million) at March 31, 2026 and ₹ 2,995 crore (US$ 316 million) at June 30, 2025.
At June 30, 2026, the Bank holds total provisions, other than specific provisions on fund-based outstanding to borrowers classified as non-performing, amounting to ₹ 22,963 crore (US$ 2.4 billion) or 1.4% of loans. These provisions include the contingency provisions of ₹ 13,100 crore (US$ 1.4 billion) as well as general provision on standard assets, provisions held for non-fund based outstanding to borrowers classified as non-performing, loan and non-fund based outstanding to standard borrowers under resolution and the BB and below portfolio. The Bank also continued to hold additional standard asset provision of ₹ 1,283 crore (US$ 136 million) made in Q3-2026 as directed by RBI in respect of the agricultural priority sector portfolio.
Capital adequacy
The Bank’s total capital adequacy ratio at June 30, 2026 was 16.84% and CET-1 ratio was 16.19% compared to the minimum regulatory requirements of 11.70% and 8.20% respectively.
Consolidated results
The consolidated profit after tax increased to ₹ 15,440 crore (US$ 1.6 billion) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 13,558 crore (US$ 1.4 billion) in Q1-2026
Consolidated assets grew by 12.5% year-on-year to ₹ 30,02,407 crore (US$ 317.2 billion) at June 30, 2026 from ₹ 26,68,636 crore (US$ 281.9 billion) at June 30, 2025.

The annualised premium equivalent of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance (ICICI Life) increased to ₹ 2,136 crore (US$ 226 million) in Q1-2027 from ₹ 1,864 crore (US$ 197 million) in Q1-2026. title: ICICI Bank Ltd (IBN) (Q2 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Strong Deposit Growth and Asset ...
snippet: Oct 19, 2026 · ICICI Bank Ltd (IBN) delivered 23.4% profit before tax growth and improved net NPA to 0.30%, though net interest margin slipped to 4.18% with further moderation expected in Q3 before...
content:
Q: How should one look at margins for the next one or two quarters? Has the impact of heavy FCNR (B) sourcing played out fully this quarter, or do you expect more compression before recovery? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) explained that the full impact of the FCNR (B) deposits raised in Q2 and the higher proportion of the overseas book will be reflected in the Q3 averages, leading to further margin moderation, partly offset by the rate hike. From Q4, margins are expected to recover healthily as these factors reverse, even assuming no further rate hikes. He noted the bank raised a large quantum of fixed-rate funding that will support growth, and the optical decline over a quarter or two is not a concern.
Q: On corporate growth, is it just temporary parking of FCNR funds, or do you see corporate growth remaining high? Retail growth looks softer than usual while corporate is very strong how do you see the mix going forward? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) said retail growth has been steadily picking up over the last few quarters, from single digits to close to 15%, with mortgages and personal loans back to mid-teen levels. Corporate growth partly reflects a low base from last year, but is not temporary FCNR parking it is a response to client demand and pricing, driven by working capital needs, a shift from bond and foreign currency markets, and some investment activity. The franchise is open on both retail and corporate fronts, and the bank will take whatever meets its risk-reward threshold.
Q: On provisions, credit costs have been lower than the new normal in the last two quarters. When does the agri provision of around INR13 billion get reversed, and was there a big corporate recovery this quarter as well? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) said corporate NPL formation is negligible, business banking is low, and retail is stable, with personal loans and cards seeing lower formation over the past four to six quarters. This quarter included one chunky corporate recovery and higher general provisioning due to loan book expansion, particularly loans against FCNR deposits, which is more of a one-off. Adjusted for these, credit cost is expected to remain up to 50 basis points. On the agriculture standard asset provisioning, the remediation review process is underway, and an update is expected over the next two quarters.
Q: On the FCNR strategy, relative to peers the amount raised is very high as a proportion of the balance sheet. Is there a strategic change are you now prioritizing NII over NIM? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) said the bank solves for sustainable earnings growth, not NII over NIM. The FCNR opportunity was a one-off, and the bank did not weigh it against short-term margin impact but rather the strength it gives for business growth going forward. Of the roughly USD18 billion raised, about USD10 billion was lent to customers, about USD3.6 billion lent by partner banks, and upwards of USD4 billion where customers put in their own money. The deposits are cost-effective with no regulatory preemption and support growth, making it a big opportunity.
Q: On overseas margins, the base has widened and the incremental FCNR-linked book would be at a much lower margin. How is the overseas margin moving up, and to what level can it settle? Can you quantify the FCNR impact on margins this quarter? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) said overseas margins are also supported by higher dollar interest rates, which increase spreads on float deposits. He declined to project overseas margins separately or give a pro forma FCNR impact number, saying it can be calculated in many ways and would be theoretical. On an overall basis, the full impact of the higher term deposit denominator, lower CASA ratio, and larger overseas book (earning about 1% margin versus 4%-plus domestic) will be seen in Q3 averages, with a healthy pickup from Q4. Excess liquidity is expected to be deployed over the next two quarters.
Q: On the retail lending products, credit card growth has been subdued and the book declined slightly quarter-on-quarter. When will recovery come? And gold loan growth was much lower this quarter versus peers anything to read into that? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) said the bank is fully engaged in credit cards, launching new products and variants and shifting from a product lens to a customer lens to build primariness. The decline this quarter was mainly seasonal last year the book built up toward end-September, while this year that will happen in Q3 and underlying growth is okay, maybe marginally positive. On jewel loans, year-on-year growth is very strong, but sequential growth came off as processes and distribution were aligned with new RBI guidelines; volumes are expected to pick up over time.
Q: On fees, 20% fee income growth is much higher than peers. Is there any one-off on FCNR to call out this quarter? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) confirmed there were some processing fees charged for the leverage against FCNR deposits. However, the sequential increase in operating expenses was largely due to the cost of wholesale resources, bonds, and loans raised during the quarter to fund that leverage, so broadly the two even each other out.
Q: On the retail versus corporate debate, do the two businesses have similar RAROC thresholds, and could continued corporate growth dilute ROE? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) said it does not work that way. Corporate credit losses are much lower because the focus is on return of capital at the client level, a go/no-go decision, whereas granular portfolios are managed at a portfolio level with some tolerance for credit loss. Corporate also brings ancillary revenue such as transaction banking and collections, which factor into the overall return. He stated clearly that corporate is definitely not worse than retail, and healthy current account growth owes substantially to the corporate franchise.
Q: Savings deposit growth looks soft at around 5% year-on-year. Anything to read into that, and can you call out the LCR for September separately? A: Anindya Banerjee (Group CFO) said there is nothing to read into it. Institutional savings, particularly from government departments, have been trending down, while retail savings growth is okay. title: ICICI Bank Q2 Results: Consolidated Profit Climbs To ₹16,333 Crore As Operating Profit Increases 20.2% Year-On-Year
snippet: Oct 17, 2026 · The ICICI Bank Q2 results also showed growth in operating profit and total income. Consolidated net interest income (NII) increased 15.9% to ₹30,336 crore, while operating profit rose 20.2% to ₹24,010 crore.
content:
ICICI Bank Q2 FY27 Results: Consolidated Net Profit Rises 22.3% to ₹16,333 Crore And Net Interest Income Grows 15.9%
ICICI Bank’s consolidated Q2 FY27 profit after tax rose 22.3% year-on-year to ₹16,333 crore, while net interest income increased 15.9% to ₹30,336 crore.
ICICI Bank reported a 22.3% year-on-year increase in consolidated profit after tax (PAT) to ₹16,333. The figure was ₹13,357 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The ICICI Bank Q2 results also showed growth in operating profit and total income.
Consolidated net interest income (NII) increased 15.9% to ₹30,336 crore, while operating profit rose 20.2% to ₹24,010 crore. Total income grew 15.5% to ₹62,505 crore during the September quarter.
The ICICI Bank share price closed at ₹1,397 on 16 October 2026 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), gaining 0.55% during the session.
ICICI Bank Q2 Results (Consolidated): Key Highlights
Non-interest income increased 15% year-on-year to ₹32,169 crore. Fee income rose 19.3% to ₹10,328 crore, while premium income increased 16.1% to ₹21,393 crore. Other income declined 48.6% to ₹449 crore.
Operating expenses stood at ₹38,495 crore, up 12.7% year-on-year. Provisions were ₹895 crore, compared with ₹910 crore in Q2 FY26. Profit before tax (PBT) rose 21.3% to ₹23,115 crore, while tax expenses increased 20.7% to ₹5,803 crore.
How Did Consolidated Advances And Deposits Perform?
The balance sheet showed advances of ₹19,35,385 crore as of 30 September 2026, compared with ₹17,29,328 crore at the end of June 2026. Deposits stood at ₹20,91,539 crore, against ₹18,70,363 crore three months earlier. Total assets reached ₹32,92,953 crore at the end of September, compared with ₹30,02,407 crore at the end of June 2026.
The return on equity (ROE) stood at 16.9% for Q2 FY27, compared with 16.6% in Q1 FY27 and 16.1% in Q2 FY26. Weighted average earnings per share increased to ₹91 from ₹74.8 a year earlier. The capital adequacy ratio was 16.62% at 30 September 2026, compared with 16.75% a year earlier. The Common Equity Tier 1 ratio stood at 15.97%.

title: ICICI Bank Q2 results: Net profit rises 20.1% to Rs 14,843 crore, NII up 17.7%
snippet: Oct 17, 2026 · ICICI Bank on Saturday reported a 20.1% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 14,843 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, supported by strong net interest income growth ...
content:
ICICI Bank on Saturday reported a 20.1% year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 14,843 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, supported by strong net interest income growth, lower provisions and an improvement in asset quality.
The country’s second-largest private sector lender reported net interest income (NII) of Rs 25,339 crore for the September quarter, up 17.7% from Rs 21,529 crore in the corresponding period last year. The NII figure also exceeded the poll estimate of Rs 24,811 crore.
The bank’s loan portfolio grew 30% year-on-year during the quarter, while its net interest margin (NIM) contracted by 0.12 percentage points to 4.18%.
Loan and deposit growth
ICICI Bank said a significant part of its loan growth came from lending by international branches against deposits mobilised under the FCNR(B) concessional swap scheme. Excluding these loans, advances growth stood at 24.1%.
On the deposits front, overall growth was 27.1%. Excluding diaspora deposits, growth stood at 17%, according to the bank’s statement.
The figures indicate continued expansion in the bank’s lending and deposit businesses, although the adjusted growth rates provide a more limited view of underlying momentum after excluding the specified categories.
Provisions decline, asset quality improves
Provisions and contingencies declined to Rs 850.69 crore in the September quarter from Rs 914.11 crore in the year-ago period, supporting profitability.
The bank also reported an improvement in asset quality. Its gross non-performing assets (NPA) ratio fell to 1.20% at the end of September 2026, compared with 1.38% in the preceding quarter and 1.58% a year earlier.
The lower gross NPA ratio indicates a reduction in the proportion of gross advances classified as non-performing assets.
Capital adequacy strengthens
ICICI Bank’s overall capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.68% as of September 30, 2026, up from 15.76% a year earlier.
The ratio measures a bank’s capital in relation to its risk-weighted assets and is an indicator of its capacity to absorb potential losses.

title: ICICI Bank Q2 profit rises 20% to ₹14,843 crore, NII jumps 18%
snippet: Oct 17, 2026 · ICICI Bank reports a 20% YoY rise in Q2 profit to ₹14,843 crore, driven by an 18% jump in net interest income and improved asset quality. Discover key financial highlights, including advances growth and deposit surge.
content:
ICICI Bank Q2 profit rises 20% to ₹14,843 crore, NII jumps 18%
ADVERTISEMENT
ICICI Bank on Saturday reported a 20.1% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit to ₹14,843 crore for the September quarter of FY27, compared with ₹12,359 crore in the year-ago period, as net interest income rose and asset quality improved.
Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 17.7% YoY to ₹25,339 crore from ₹21,529 crore in Q2 FY26. However, net interest margin (NIM) narrowed to 4.18% from 4.36% in the preceding quarter and 4.30% a year earlier.
During the quarter under review, operating profit grew 18.9% YoY to ₹20,575 crore from ₹17,298 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Non-interest income, excluding treasury, increased 12.5% YoY to ₹8,277 crore. Fee income rose 20.1% to ₹7,795 crore, with fees from retail, rural and business banking customers accounting for around 75% of the total.
Operating expenses increased 8.5% YoY to ₹12,811 crore. The bank reported a treasury loss of ₹230 crore during the quarter, compared with a gain of ₹220 crore in the year-ago period, ICICI Bank said in its earnings report.
Asset quality improves, provisions decline
ICICI Bank’s asset quality improved during the September quarter, with the gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declining to 1.20% as of September 30, 2026, from 1.58% a year earlier and 1.38% in the June quarter.
The net NPA ratio eased to 0.30% from 0.39% in the year-ago period and 0.35% in the preceding quarter.
As per the release, provisions, excluding tax provisions, declined to ₹851 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹914 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The bank continued to hold contingency provisions of ₹13,100 crore as of September 30, 2026, along with additional standard asset provisions of ₹1,283 crore made in Q3 FY26 as directed by the Reserve Bank of India for its agricultural priority-sector portfolio.
Advances rise 30%, deposits grow 27%
ICICI Bank’s total advances increased 30% YoY and 12.3% sequentially to ₹18.32 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026. Excluding loans extended by its international branches against FCNR (B) deposits, advances grew 24.1% YoY and 7.3% quarter-on-quarter.
Total deposits rose 27.1% YoY and 11.8% sequentially to ₹20.50 lakh crore. Excluding FCNR (B) deposits, deposit growth stood at 17% YoY and 3.1% sequentially.
The bank’s consolidated assets grew 22.6% YoY to ₹32.93 lakh crore at the end of September 2026, compared with ₹26.86 lakh crore a year earlier.
Its capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.68%, while the Common Equity Tier 1 (CET-1) ratio was 16.01%, comfortably above the respective minimum regulatory requirements of 11.70% and 8.20%.
During the quarter, ICICI Bank also purchased an additional 2% stake in ICICI Life Insurance Limited for ₹1,470 crore.
Ahead of the results, ICICI Bank shares closed Friday’s session at ₹1,396.80 on the BSE, up 0.13%. The lender’s market capitalisation stood at around ₹10.02 lakh crore.

title: Brent Oil $95.84: Iran Mine Claims Before Sunday Open
snippet: Brent settled at $95.84 after a second weekly loss. Iran says three tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Saturday; the US disputes ...
content:
Updated 15 November 2026, 07:00 GMT. Brent crude futures go into the Sunday evening reopen at $95.84, Friday’s settlement, after a second straight weekly fall of about 2.5 percent (market reports based on Reuters data). The weekend added new risk: Iran said on Saturday that three oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, a claim the US military disputes. Verdict: the mine claims give Brent an upside risk at the open, but the supply surplus that drove two weekly losses has not changed. Reference levels for the week: $98 above, $91 below.
Key facts
- Last settlement: Brent $95.84 on Friday 13 November, up 2 cents; WTI $88.56, down 0.2 percent (Kitco, market reports).
- The week: down about 2.5 percent from the $98.32 settlement on 6 November, Brent’s second weekly loss in a row.
- The week’s low: Tuesday’s $91.49 settlement, the lowest since August.
- Saturday’s news: Iran’s navy and Revolutionary Guards said three tankers hit mines and caught fire in the strait after using routes Iran had not authorised. No vessel has been named (Manila Times, Oman Observer, citing Iranian state media).
- US position: the US military says it has cleared the strait’s main routes of mines and that the waterway is open to commercial shipping.
- Traffic: shipping through Hormuz is about 65 percent below pre-war levels, according to the latest UKMTO report.
What happened over the weekend
Brent does not trade on Saturday, so the weekend news has not yet been priced. Iran’s navy and the Revolutionary Guards said two tankers were hit in the south of the strait and a third to the east, and that ships using routes without Iran’s approval would be set on fire by naval mines. Tehran has told vessels they need its permission to cross during the conflict. The US military disputes the claims and says the main routes are clear.
The United Nations said on 14 November that 25 seafarers have been killed in and around Hormuz since the US-Israel war on Iran began in February (Al Jazeera). Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it was time to remove the Iranian threat once and for all, according to CBS News. Neither statement changed the supply picture on its own, but both make an early deal on Hormuz look less likely.
There was no confirmation from Saudi Arabia of damage from the Houthi attack claims of 12 November on the East-West pipeline and Yanbu. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two drones, and Aramco has made no statement. That pipeline carries about 4 million barrels a day of crude to the Red Sea, Saudi Arabia’s main route around Hormuz.
Why Brent fell for a second week
Reuters put the weekly decline down to signs of a growing supply surplus and to the US blockade of Iranian oil, which lowered fears of a renewed direct war. President Donald Trump said a deal with Iran was not needed and that the blockade stays. The International Energy Agency said the market is back in surplus as Gulf exports recover, and US government data showed crude and fuel stocks rising.
Thursday showed how fast the risk premium can come back. Brent jumped 3.3 percent to $95.82 on the Houthi claims and Iranian reports of tanker explosions, then held that level on Friday without adding to it. Our Saturday Brent page covers Friday’s session. Higher US interest-rate expectations are a further headwind: hot inflation data last week raised bets on a December Fed rate increase, and gold posted a steep weekly loss as Treasury yields rose (Kitco). Our gold page covers the rate outlook.
The week ahead: what can move Brent
Hormuz, from the open. If ship trackers or insurers confirm Saturday’s mine strikes, Brent could open higher and test $98. If the claims go unconfirmed, as several earlier ones have, the market is likely to fade them as it did on Friday.
US inventory data. The Energy Information Administration’s weekly petroleum report, normally out on Wednesday, is the next read on demand after recent builds.
OPEC+ on 29 November. The group kept December output targets unchanged on 1 November. The full ministerial meeting on 29 November will set policy for 2027, and Rystad Energy’s Jorge Leon called it the much more important test. Talk of restoring more halted output before that meeting would weigh on prices.
Brent price: bull, base and bear
| Scenario | Brent | What has to happen | Anchor | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Bear | $91 | The mine claims go unconfirmed, US stocks build again and supply-surplus talk returns. | Tuesday’s $91.49 settlement, the lowest since August; about 4.5 percent below $95.84. | 
| Base | $94-$97 | The weekend news adds a small premium that fades, and Brent trades around last week’s settlements. | Thursday’s $95.82 and Friday’s $95.84 settlements, and Friday’s $96.67 intraday high. | 
| Bull | $98 | Tanker damage is confirmed, traffic through Hormuz falls further or Saudi exports are hit. | The $98.32 settlement on 6 November; about 2.6 percent above $95.84. | 
The bear case sits below the current price. These are reference levels measured from Friday’s settlement, not forecasts.
What to watch
- Sunday evening: the futures reopen and price Saturday’s mine claims.
- Shipping data: any vessel names, insurer notices or UKMTO updates on the three tankers.
- Wednesday: the EIA weekly petroleum status report.
- $91.49 and $98.32: last week’s low settlement and the previous Friday’s settlement.
Monday update: our Brent page for Monday 16 November covers the reopen, Iran’s attack on a US base in Bahrain and the move back above $96.
Quick take: Brent settled at $95.84 on Friday after a second weekly loss. Iran’s Saturday claim that three tankers hit mines in Hormuz is the first thing the market will price when futures reopen on Sunday evening; the US says the routes are clear. Supply surplus points lower, tanker risk higher. $91 is the downside reference, $98 the upside.
FAQ
What is the Brent crude oil price today?
Brent futures do not trade until Sunday evening. The last settlement was $95.84 on Friday 13 November, up 2 cents.
Did oil go up or down this week?
Down. Brent fell about 2.5 percent from the $98.32 settlement on 6 November, its second straight weekly loss, according to Reuters data.
What happened in the Strait of Hormuz this weekend?
Iran said on Saturday 14 November that three oil tankers hit naval mines and caught fire after using routes it had not approved. The US military disputes the claims and says the main routes are clear of mines.
What is the WTI price?
WTI settled at $88.56 on Friday, down 0.2 percent.
Why has oil been falling?
Reuters cites a growing supply surplus, higher OPEC+ output, rising US inventories and the US blockade of Iranian oil, which lowered fears of a wider war.
When is the next OPEC+ meeting?
The full OPEC+ ministerial meeting is on 29 November and will set production policy for 2027. The group kept December targets unchanged on 1 November.

title: EIA Sees Brent Near $100 for the Rest of the Year as Crude Futures Ease Again
snippet: Oil Market Daily News Commentary - U.S. crude oil futures closed lower for a second straight session on Tuesday. The December NYMEX West Texas Intermediate contract settled at $86.04 a barrel, down 81 ...
content:
HOUSTON, Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oil Market Daily News Commentary - U.S. crude oil futures closed lower for a second straight session on Tuesday. The December NYMEX West Texas Intermediate contract settled at $86.04 a barrel, down 81 cents, or 0.93%, and the January ICE Brent contract settled at $91.49, down $1.08, or 1.17%. December WTI had settled at $104.12 on Oct. 30. Over the past two weeks, a producer, an oil sands company, a refiner, a gas processor and a tanker owner have each reported quarterly results from a different point along the oil and gas chain. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: APA Corporation (NASDAQ: APA), Suncor Energy Inc. (NYSE: SU), HF Sinclair Corporation (NYSE: DINO), Kinetik Holdings Inc. (NYSE: KNTK), and International Seaways, Inc. (NYSE: INSW).
What the federal outlook says
The U.S. Energy Information Administration released its November Short-Term Energy Outlook on Tuesday. The agency said crude oil prices rose for a third consecutive month in October as falling global inventories, attacks on oil tankers in the Persian Gulf, constrained shipping capacity and higher transportation costs tightened supply, and that it expects the Brent crude oil spot price will remain near $100 per barrel for the remainder of this year before gradually falling to an average of $77 per barrel in the fourth quarter of 2027. The EIA finalized its model inputs on Nov. 5, and the forecast does not specifically account for market events after that day.
At home, the outlook said U.S. commercial crude oil inventories fell to 410 million barrels at the end of October, the lowest end-of-October level since 2014, and forecast that U.S. crude oil production will reach a record 14.3 million barrels per day in 2027. The agency said it now assumes global petroleum product markets will face continued supply constraints through the end of 2027, conditions it said will support wider crack spreads next year. For natural gas, it forecast the Henry Hub spot price will average $2.87 per million British thermal units from November through March, 16% lower than it expected last month.
On the supply side, seven OPEC+ countries (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman) met virtually on Nov. 1 and decided to maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026, according to an OPEC press release. Their next meeting will be held on Nov. 29.
At the wellhead
APA Corporation (NASDAQ: APA) said in its third-quarter 2026 results, released Nov. 4, that U.S. oil production of 128,000 barrels per day came in 4,000 barrels above guidance through high uptime, earlier turn-in-lines and robust new well performance. The company reported net income attributable to common stock of $698 million, or $2.00 per diluted share, and increased its full-year 2026 free cash flow outlook to approximately $2.9 billion, reflecting stronger operating performance and higher commodity prices. In Egypt, APA said adjusted production was slightly lower than guidance primarily due to production sharing contract impacts associated with higher Brent prices.
"We are delivering another strong year, with our third-quarter results reflecting the quality of our assets and consistent execution across the business," said John J. Christmann IV, APA's CEO.
From oil sands to refined products
In Canada, Suncor Energy Inc. (NYSE: SU) reported in its third quarter 2026 results, released Nov. 3, record quarterly adjusted funds from operations of $6.7 billion and free funds flow of $5.2 billion (Suncor reports in Canadian dollars). The company said record bitumen transfers supported upstream production of 853,000 barrels per day, and that it achieved record third quarter refined product sales of 677,000 barrels per day. Subsequent to the quarter, Suncor increased its quarterly dividend by 10% to $0.66 per share and raised monthly share repurchases by 50% to $750 million.
"The third quarter was highlighted by record adjusted funds from operations and the ingenuity of our teams, who continue to find new ways to create value through our unparalleled integration, most recently by sustaining Edmonton refinery throughput during a turnaround," said Rich Kruger, Chief Executive Officer.
Oil stocks track crude, but not tick for tick, and reading the chart is one way to tell which producers, refiners and pipeline stocks are following it. Oil Market Daily's sister site, Stock Preachers, offers a free 27-page guide, Knowledge is Power, with 10 chapters in plain English on the two skills every trade comes down to: reading the news and reading the chart. Readers who sign up also receive The Roadmap every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
Inside the refinery
HF Sinclair Corporation (NYSE: DINO) reported in its 2026 third quarter results, released Oct. 28, net income attributable to HF Sinclair stockholders of $2,015 million, or $11.38 per diluted share, compared with $403 million, or $2.15 per diluted share, a year earlier. Its Refining segment reported Adjusted EBITDA of $2,582 million, up from $661 million, an increase the company said was driven principally by the tight supply of transportation fuels across the markets, elevated crack spreads and benefits from the small refinery RINs waivers granted by the EPA. Adjusted refinery gross margin was $54.22 per produced barrel sold, a 183% increase compared to $19.16 a year earlier.
HF Sinclair's Chief Executive Officer, Franklin Myers, commented, "Our third quarter performance reflects the strength and continued focus on safe, reliable execution of all our businesses."
Gas in the Permian
Kinetik Holdings Inc. (NYSE: KNTK), which describes itself as a Permian-to-Gulf Coast midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin, provides gathering, transportation, compression, processing and treating services for companies that produce natural gas, natural gas liquids, crude oil and water. In its third quarter 2026 results, released Nov. 4, the company reported record processed gas volumes of 1.94 Bcf/d. Kinetik also said it reached a final investment decision on phase 1 of the ECCC Pipeline expansion, which is expected to increase throughput capacity by roughly 50% to approximately 225 MMcf/d.
"Kinetik delivered another strong quarter with record processed gas volumes underscoring the strength and increasing scale of our business," said Jamie Welch, Kinetik's President & Chief Executive Officer.
On the water
On Nov. 4, the International Energy Agency, the International Energy Forum and OPEC held a technical workshop on maritime energy flows, shipping and insurance, requested by ministers at an Oct. 12 meeting in Riyadh where, according to OPEC, they expressed concern about elevated shipping and insurance costs.
A day later, International Seaways, Inc. (NYSE: INSW), a tanker company providing energy transportation services, reported third quarter 2026 results with record net income of $344 million, or $6.90 per diluted share, including a $53 million gain on the sale of a 2012-built Suezmax tanker, compared to $71 million, or $1.42 per diluted share, a year earlier. The company said the increase was primarily driven by higher TCE revenues from spot earnings that increased an average of approximately $38,300 per day across the fleet and higher profit-sharing results on applicable time charters by approximately $75 million. It declared a dividend of $5.05 per share, matching the record set in the previous quarter.
Lois K. Zabrocky, International Seaways President and CEO commented, "We delivered record quarterly net income, reflecting both exceptional tanker market conditions and the benefits of our long-term approach to fleet investment and capital allocation."
One barrel, five reports
Read side by side, the five reports cover U.S. oil output above guidance, record bitumen transfers, higher refining margins, a gas pipeline expansion decision and record tanker net income.
