title: Meta by the Numbers: 3.60 Billion Daily Users and $60.80 Billion in One Quarter
snippet: Dec 22, 2025 · Meta statistics: 3.60 billion daily users, $60.80 billion Q2 revenue, ARPP, ad pricing, Reality Labs losses and capex trends.
content:
Meta Platforms reported 3.60 billion daily active people on average for June 2026, an increase of 3% year-over-year. That count covers everyone who used Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, or WhatsApp on a given day. Meta statistics from the same filing show sales growing far faster: revenue was $60.80 billion, an increase of 28% year-over-year in the second quarter.
Meta now grows through pricing, engagement, and new revenue lines more than through new people. In the same quarter, average price per ad increased by 12% year-over-year, and capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $31.08 billion as the AI build-out accelerated. The figures below draw on Meta’s SEC filings and earnings calls, Pew Research Center survey data, and European Commission enforcement records.
Key Takeaways
- Meta’s second-quarter revenue increased by 28% year-over-year, while DAP increased 3% over the same period.
- Worldwide ARPP was $16.86 in the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 24% from the second quarter of 2025.
- Meta puts its DAP error margin at approximately 3% of worldwide DAP, or roughly 108 million people, nearly the 120 million people added between June 2025 and June 2026.
- Free cash flow was $784 million in the second quarter, down from free cash flow of $8.55 billion a year earlier.
- Family of Apps other revenue grew about 1.97 times between Q1 2025 and Q2 2026, driven primarily by WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions revenue.
- Reality Labs lost a combined $27.84 billion in operating income over the six quarters from Q1 2025 to Q2 2026.
Editor’s Choice
- Daily active people: 3.60 billion on average for June 2026.
- Second-quarter revenue: $60.80 billion, up 28% year-over-year.
- Full-year 2025 revenue: $200.97 billion.
- Instagram daily actives: Instagram reached 2 billion daily actives, and Facebook has reached more than 2 billion daily actives.
- Threads monthly actives: Threads crossed 500 million monthly actives.
- Advantage+ run-rate: over $75 billion in annual revenue run-rate.
- Headcount: Headcount was 75,472 as of June 30, 2026.
Meta Statistics on Daily Active People by Quarter
- Mark Zuckerberg told investors that 3.6 billion people were using at least one of Meta’s apps each day in the second quarter.
- DAP has added 250 million people since December 2024.
- According to Meta’s first-quarter earnings release, the March 2026 dip was driven by internet disruptions in Iran, as well as a restriction on access to WhatsApp in Russia.
- According to CFO Susan Li on the Q1 2026 earnings call, absent these impacts, growth in Family Daily Active People would have been positive quarter-over-quarter.
- Annual DAP growth slowed from 8% in September 2025 to 3% in June 2026.
- Meta ended 2025 with more than 3.5 billion people using at least one of its apps every day.
| Month | DAP (billions) | Year-over-year growth (%) | 
|---|---|---|
| December 2024 | 3.35 | 5 | 
| March 2025 | 3.43 | 6 | 
| June 2025 | 3.48 | 6 | 
| September 2025 | 3.54 | 8 | 
| December 2025 | 3.58 | 7 | 
| March 2026 | 3.56 | 4 | 
| June 2026 | 3.60 | 3 | 
Source: Meta quarterly earnings releases, December 2024 to June 2026
About This Data
- Compiled from 15 sources: 14 primary documents and 1 survey from Pew Research Center.
- The primary documents are Meta earnings releases, call transcripts, its Form 10-Q, Meta newsroom posts, and a European Commission decision.
- Sources were published between January 2025 and September 2026, and only primary or original-research data qualified.
- Figures are reviewed on a rolling basis and updated when Meta files new results.
Meta Revenue by Quarter
- Meta’s second-quarter 2026 earnings release shows revenue on a constant currency basis would have increased by 27% year-over-year.
- Advertising brought in $59,363 million of second-quarter revenue.
- Net income was $15.85 billion, with diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $6.18 for the quarter.
- Second-quarter operating margin was 31%, compared with 43% in Q2 2025.
- First-quarter 2026 revenue grew 33% year-over-year.
- Meta guided third quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $61-64 billion.
Recent Developments
- September 24, 2026: At Connect 2026, Meta introduced new glasses, a pair of glasses that weighs about 100 grams.
- September 15, 2026: Meta launched Meta One with more than 50 features on Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Meta AI.
- July 2026: Meta entered into an exclusivity agreement to co-develop a data center campus in El Paso, Texas, through a venture in which it would hold a 20% membership interest.
- July 29, 2026: Meta reported that second-quarter total costs and expenses were $42.03 billion, an increase of 55% year-over-year.
- Q2 2026: More than 1 million businesses used Meta Business Agents each week after their global launch on WhatsApp and Messenger.
- May 2026: Meta issued an aggregate of $25.00 billion of fixed-rate senior unsecured notes in six series.
How Many People Use Each Meta App
- Facebook and WhatsApp each had more than 2 billion daily active users at the end of 2025, with Instagram just shy of that.
- WhatsApp peaked at 30 million messages sent per second during the World Cup Final.
- Meta AI saw a 60% increase in the number of people interacting with the assistant each day after Meta rebuilt it around Muse Spark, as covered in our Meta AI usage statistics.
- On Facebook, video time spent increased 9% globally year over year and over 10% within the US & Canada.
- The optimizations Meta made in Q4 drove a 20% lift in Threads time spent.
| App | Latest reported users | Metric | Period | 
|---|---|---|---|
|  | More than 2 billion | Daily actives | Q2 2026 | 
|  | 2 billion | Daily actives | Q2 2026 | 
|  | More than 2 billion | Daily actives | Q4 2025 | 
| Threads | Crossed 500 million | Monthly actives | Q2 2026 | 
Source: Meta Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 earnings call transcripts
Meta Annual Revenue and Net Income
- Income from operations reached $83,276 million in 2025, up 20%.
- Diluted earnings per share was $23.49 in 2025, against $23.86 in 2024, even as revenue climbed.
- The third quarter 2025 provision for income taxes includes a one-time, non-cash income tax charge of $15.93 billion.
- Net income rose 59% in 2024.
- Meta’s operating margin was 41% in 2025, compared with 42% in 2024.
- Annual revenue grew about 49% between 2023 and 2025.
Meta Revenue by Region
- In the second quarter of 2026, revenue increased by 32% in United States & Canada, 24% in Europe, 19% in Asia-Pacific, and 36% in Rest of World, measured by user geography.
- United States and Canada customers generated about 39.2% of Q2 2026 revenue.
- Meta’s reporting Europe includes Russia and Turkey.
- Its Rest of World includes Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East.
- Asia-Pacific customers accounted for about 26.4% of Q2 2026 revenue, ahead of Europe.
Meta Ad Impressions and Price per Ad Growth
- For full-year 2025, ad impressions increased by 12% year-over-year.
- Average price per ad increased by 9% year-over-year for the full year 2025.
- On WhatsApp, hundreds of millions of people now view ads in Status daily.
- 9 million small businesses are now using at least one of Meta’s AI ad creative tools.
- Advertisers comparing platforms can set these figures against our Facebook advertising statistics.
View the data
Why it matters: Meta’s second-quarter ad impressions increased by 14% year-over-year while average price per ad increased by 12%, so volume and pricing rose together. Across our 50+ platform statistics pages, engagement depth matters more than raw user growth, and Meta’s ad data fits that pattern.
Meta AI Ad Tools and Revenue Run-Rates
- The annual revenue run-rate of Meta’s value optimization suite is now over $20 billion, more than doubling year-over-year.
- Partnership ads revenue run-rate more than doubled year-over-year in Q1 to $10 billion.
- The combined revenue run-rate of video generation tools hit $10 billion in Q4 2025.
- Paid messaging within WhatsApp crossed a $2 billion annual run-rate in Q4 2025.
| Product | Annual revenue run-rate | Period | 
|---|---|---|
| Advantage+ end-to-end solutions | Over $75 billion | Q2 2026 | 
| Value optimization suite | Over $20 billion | Q1 2026 | 
| Partnership ads | $10 billion | Q1 2026 | 
| Video generation tools | $10 billion | Q4 2025 | 
| WhatsApp paid messaging | Crossed $2 billion | Q4 2025 | 
Source: Meta earnings call transcripts, Q4 2025 to Q2 2026
Meta Non-Advertising Revenue
- For the first time, quarterly Family of Apps other revenue reached $1 billion and grew 73% year-over-year in Q2 2026.
- Family of Apps other revenue totaled $2.58 billion in 2025, against $1.72 billion in 2024.
- Meta One plans start at $2.99 a month for single products, $7.99 a month for individual bundles, and $14.99 a month for creator and business bundles.
Other revenue made up about 1.7% of second-quarter revenue. It is still small, but it is the one line that does not depend on advertisers.
Reality Labs Operating Losses
- Reality Labs posted operating losses of $19.19 billion in 2025 and $17.73 billion in 2024.
- During the six months ended June 30, 2026, the RL segment reduced overall operating profit by approximately $8.65 billion, and Meta expects full-year 2026 RL operating losses to remain similar to 2025.
- Q2 revenue was $431 million, up 16% year-over-year due to strong growth in AI glasses revenue, partially offset by lower Quest headset sales.
- Zuckerberg said sales of Meta’s glasses more than tripled in 2025, a shift our virtual reality statistics track across the wider headset market.
Meta Employee Headcount
- Employee compensation for the three months ended June 30, 2026 also includes $1.18 billion of severance expenses related to the May 2026 headcount reduction of approximately 8,000 employees.
- Meta said the majority of these employees will no longer be reflected in its headcount by the end of the third quarter of 2026.
- Meta ended Q2 with over 75,000 employees, down 3% from Q1.
- Headcount was 74,067 as of December 31, 2024, an increase of 10% year-over-year.
- Longer-run workforce history sits in our Meta employee count data.
Meta Capital Expenditures
- Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $72.22 billion for full-year 2025.
- Meta expects 2026 capital expenditures to be in the range of $130-145 billion.
- Meta now expects full-year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $165-169 billion.
- Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $90.26 billion as of June 30, 2026, against long-term debt of $83.66 billion.
Key finding: Meta’s second-quarter capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $31.08 billion, and its cash flow from operating activities was $31.86 billion. Nearly all the cash the business generated in the quarter went back into servers, networks and data centers for AI.
Meta App Usage Among U.S. Adults
- Pew Research Center surveyed 5,022 U.S. adults from Feb. 5 to June 18, 2025.
- Facebook use peaks among 30- to 49-year-olds, at 80%.
- Eight-in-ten adults ages 18 to 29 say they use Instagram, compared with 19% of adults ages 65 and older.
- More than half of women report using Instagram (55%), compared with under half of men (44%).
- Instagram use is up from 40% in 2021, and WhatsApp use is up from 23% in 2021.
Meta Regulatory Fines and Legal Charges
- The European Commission fined Meta €200 million for breaching the Digital Markets Act.
- On the same day, the Commission fined Apple €500 million.
- Meta’s second-quarter results include $2.40 billion of charges related to legal proceedings, which our privacy fines tracker sets alongside other platform penalties.
| Item | Amount | Period | 
|---|---|---|
| European Commission DMA fine | €200 million | April 2025 | 
| Charges related to legal proceedings | $2.40 billion | Q2 2026 | 
| Severance for May 2026 headcount reduction | $1.18 billion | Q2 2026 | 
| One-time non-cash income tax charge | $15.93 billion | Q3 2025 | 
Source: European Commission 2025, Meta earnings releases and Form 10-Q 2025 to 2026
How Many Users Does Meta Have?
Meta had 3.60 billion daily active people on average during June 2026, its most recent reported count. At the app level, Facebook has reached more than 2 billion daily active users, and Instagram has reached 2 billion daily active users. The app totals overlap, since one person can use several apps.
Is Facebook Losing Users in 2026?
Meta’s family-level data shows only a brief dip. DAU was 3.56 billion on average for March 2026, before DAP was 3.60 billion on average for June 2026. Meta said the March count declined slightly from December due to internet disruptions in Iran and a restriction on access to WhatsApp in Russia.
Who Is Facebook’s Biggest Competitor?
TikTok is the rival Meta names in the risk factors of its latest quarterly filing. The Form 10-Q says user growth and engagement are affected by competitive products and services, such as TikTok, that have reduced some users’ engagement with our products and services.
The head-to-head usage numbers for the two short-video apps sit in our TikTok vs Instagram statistics.
Conclusion
Meta averaged 3.60 billion daily active people at its latest count and booked $60.80 billion of quarterly revenue, an increase of 28% year-over-year, with users growing slowly and revenue per person climbing fast. Advertising still funds almost everything, while WhatsApp messaging and Meta One subscriptions build a second revenue line.
The open question is cost. Capital spending keeps rising, and Reality Labs still loses billions each quarter, so the next filings will show whether AI-driven ad gains can outpace the infrastructure bill.

title: RBI MPC Explained: Everything That Changed On Repo Rate, GDP, And Inflation
snippet: Aug 5, 2026 · RBI MPC August 2026: Repo Rate Decision, Growth Outlook, Inflation Forecast - Top Highlights From interest rates and inflation to growth forecasts and liquidity measures, here's a quick roundup of the RBI's key decisions from the August 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting.
content:
The RBI kept the benchmark repo rate unchanged at 5.25%. The Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously for this decision, maintaining a Neutral stance.
RBI MPC August 2026: Repo Rate Decision, Growth Outlook, Inflation Forecast - Top Highlights
From interest rates and inflation to growth forecasts and liquidity measures, here's a quick roundup of the RBI's key decisions from the August 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting.
- RBI maintained repo rate, improved growth and inflation outlook.
- Global uncertainty prompted pause, India's economy remained robust.
- FY27 GDP growth upgraded to 6.7%, inflation forecast trimmed.
RBI MPC Highlights: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) delivered a largely expected policy outcome on Wednesday, leaving the benchmark repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent, but its latest assessment of the economy carried a more optimistic tone than its June review.
While policymakers chose not to alter interest rates, the central bank raised its FY27 growth forecast to 6.7 per cent and trimmed its inflation projection to 5 per cent, signalling greater confidence in the resilience of domestic demand even as geopolitical tensions, volatile oil prices and an uneven monsoon continue to cloud the global outlook.
The six-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), chaired by Governor Sanjay Malhotra, voted unanimously to maintain the policy repo rate and retain its Neutral stance, indicating that it wants more clarity on inflation before considering any change in monetary policy.
Why The RBI Chose To Pause
Unlike previous policy reviews that were largely centred on inflation, this time the RBI acknowledged that the biggest challenge is uncertainty.
Governor Malhotra said the global economy continues to grapple with renewed conflict in West Asia, fresh tariff actions by the United States and volatile financial markets, all of which have complicated the outlook for growth and inflation. Oil prices have remained unpredictable, supply chains have once again come under pressure and several global central banks have either tightened policy or maintained a cautious approach as inflation concerns linger.
Against this backdrop, the MPC concluded that maintaining the current policy settings was the most appropriate course of action until there is greater visibility on the inflation trajectory.
Also Read : RBI MPC August 2026: Repo Rate Unchanged At 5.25%, MPC Retains Neutral Stance
India Continues To Outperform
Despite the uncertain external environment, the RBI believes the domestic economy has held up better than expected.
Governor Malhotra noted that economic activity during the April-June quarter exceeded the central bank's earlier expectations. Consumption remained healthy, manufacturing activity continued to expand, services maintained strong momentum and exports recovered, helping India retain its position as the world's fastest-growing major economy.
The RBI also pointed to sustained government spending on infrastructure, resilient investment activity and robust bank credit as factors supporting growth.
Also Read : RBI Upgrades FY27 GDP Forecast, Cuts Inflation Outlook: What It Means For India's Economy
GDP Forecast Raised
Reflecting this resilience, the central bank raised its FY27 GDP growth estimate to 6.7 per cent, marginally higher than the 6.6 per cent projected in June.
The revised quarterly projections are:
Q1 FY27: 7.0% (Earlier: 6.6%)
Q2 FY27: 6.4% (Earlier: 6.3%)
Q3 FY27: 6.5% (Unchanged)
Q4 FY27: 6.8% (Unchanged)
The RBI expects investment activity to remain supported by high capacity utilisation, healthy credit growth and continued public infrastructure spending. It also expects services exports and recently signed trade agreements to provide additional support to economic activity.
Inflation Still A Concern, But The Outlook Has Improved
Although the RBI lowered its FY27 inflation projection to 5 per cent, Governor Malhotra made it clear that inflation risks have not disappeared.
Headline retail inflation moved back above the RBI's target in June after remaining below it for more than a year. According to the central bank, the increase has largely been driven by higher food and fuel prices rather than broad-based demand pressures. Encouragingly, core inflation has remained relatively contained, suggesting underlying price pressures have yet to become widespread.
Also Read : RBI MPC Lowers CPI Inflation To 5%, Says El Nino Continues To Be A Major Risk
The revised CPI projections are:
Q2 FY27: 4.7% (Earlier: 5.1%)
Q3 FY27: 5.9% (Unchanged)
Q4 FY27: 5.5% (Earlier: 5.4%)
The Risks Haven't Gone Away
Even as it upgraded growth and lowered inflation forecasts, the RBI avoided sounding overly optimistic.
The central bank warned that renewed hostilities in West Asia, elevated energy prices, global trade uncertainty and weather disruptions linked to El Niño continue to pose meaningful risks.
A deficient and uneven south-west monsoon could weigh on agriculture and rural consumption, although government measures such as crop diversification, climate-resilient farming and adequate foodgrain stocks are expected to soften the impact.
Banking System Remains Comfortable
The RBI said liquidity conditions remain comfortable, with the banking system continuing to operate in surplus. Credit growth has remained strong across retail, industry and services despite some moderation in the transmission of lower policy rates.
The central bank also highlighted improvements in India's external position, with healthy foreign direct investment inflows, a rebound in portfolio investments and foreign exchange reserves remaining adequate to cushion external shocks.
Other Key Announcements
Apart from the policy decision, the RBI announced draft guidelines for restarting the licensing of Urban Cooperative Banks, proposed changes to the credit monitoring framework for rural cooperative banks and said it plans to standardise the regulatory framework governing lending rates across regulated entities to improve transparency and consumer protection.
Frequently Asked Questions
What was the Reserve Bank of India's decision on the repo rate?
How did the RBI revise its economic forecasts?
The RBI raised its FY27 growth forecast to 6.7% from 6.6%. It also trimmed its inflation projection to 5% for FY27, showing increased confidence in the economy.
Why did the RBI decide to keep the policy rates unchanged?
The RBI chose to pause due to uncertainty in the global economy, including geopolitical tensions and volatile oil prices. They want more clarity on inflation before changing monetary policy.
How is India's economy performing according to the RBI?
The RBI noted India's economy held up better than expected, driven by healthy consumption, manufacturing, and services. This helps India retain its position as the world's fastest-growing major economy.
Is inflation still a concern for the RBI despite the lowered projection?
Yes, Governor Malhotra made it clear that inflation risks have not disappeared, despite lowering the FY27 projection to 5%. Increased food and fuel prices, along with El Niño, remain potential threats.

title: RBI Policy Meet August 2026 highlights: Central bank holds interest rates for fourth straight meeting
snippet: Aug 5, 2026 · RBI MPC Meeting August 2026 Live Updates: Follow the latest updates on the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, the repo rate decision, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra's policy announcement, inflation outlook, GDP growth projections, and other key announcements.
content:
RBI Policy Meet August 2026 highlights: Central bank holds interest rates for fourth straight meeting
RBI MPC Meeting August 2026 Live Updates: RBI MPC keeps repo rate at 5.25%, maintains neutral stance. Inflation edged up, but core inflation remains benign.
The six-member panel also decided to continue with the neutral stance, indicating that the central bank will remain data-dependent while assessing inflation and growth dynamics.
The RBI said headline inflation has edged up above the target, in line with expectations. However, realised inflation in the first quarter was marginally lower than projections, reflecting limited pass-through of cost pressures.
The central bank added that core inflation, excluding precious metals, continues to remain benign.
Catch LIVE udpates on RBI policy here:
RBI Policy Meet August 2026: That’s all from the RBI policy live blog today
Thank you for staying with us for all the key updates, announcements and expert reactions.
RBI Repo Rate: Central Bank targets rollout of polymer currency notes in early FY28
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the central bank is aiming to introduce polymer currency notes at the start of FY28, with the more durable notes expected to be used initially for lower denominations that see high circulation.
RBI MPC Meet August 2026 Live Updates: UPI MDR proposal explained
The Finance Ministry’s proposed amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act does not reintroduce charges on UPI transactions. Instead, it gives the government the flexibility to decide in the future which digital payment modes remain exempt from Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) and which could attract it.
RBI Monetary Policy: Central Bank proposes uniform lending rate framework for banks, NBFCs
The RBI has proposed harmonising interest rate regulations across banks, NBFCs and other regulated entities to make loan pricing more transparent and consistent. The move aims to standardise lending practices, improve monetary policy transmission and strengthen consumer protection, with draft guidelines to be released for public consultation.
RBI Repo Rate: Central Bank proposes new urban co-operative bank licences after 22-year gap
The RBI has issued draft guidelines for licensing new urban co-operative banks (UCBs), reopening the framework after more than two decades. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the central bank will seek stakeholder feedback before finalising the norms, with the move aimed at expanding the sector while strengthening governance and regulatory oversight.
RBI Policy Meet August 2026 Live Updates: SBI sees no rate hike in FY27, expects FCNR(B) inflows to boost liquidity and margins
Following the RBI’s decision to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25%, SBI MD – Corporate Banking & Subsidiaries Ashwini Kumar Tewari said the bank does not expect any rate hikes this financial year. He also said robust FCNR(B) inflows should improve liquidity conditions and support margins, while highlighting the resilience of the Indian economy and strong credit growth despite global uncertainties.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: RBI holds rates, but debate shifts to when the next hike could come
The RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% and retained its neutral stance, but economists remain divided on how long that can last. While SBI’s Ashwini Kumar Tewari sees no rate hikes this financial year, Deutsche Bank’s Kaushik Das expects up to 100 basis points of hikes over the next six to nine months. Kotak Mahindra Bank’s Upasna Bhardwaj also sees scope for rate hikes, retaining her base case of a 50-basis-point increase starting December.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Piramal's Jairam says RBI has ruled out EBLR-like norms for NBFCs
Reacting to the RBI Governor’s clarification, Piramal’s Jairam said the draft guidelines are “an Amol Palekar movie, not an action film,” signalling that they are evolutionary rather than disruptive. He said the clarification that no EBLR-like framework is proposed for NBFCs is significant, as it rules out a key area of market speculation.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: RBI Governor on UPI MDR: 'Someone will have to pay the cost'
On merchant discount rate (MDR) for UPI transactions, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says it is “premature now, government [is] still carrying out amendments.” He adds, “Costs have to be paid by someone; we all want this public infrastructure to strengthen,” and notes, “Someone will have to pay the cost.” Malhotra said it is important to “continue to invest and find the means—through MDR or other means,” while urging stakeholders to “wait and watch for further developments on this.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: RBI Governor says 6.7% GDP growth estimate carries risks on both sides
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says, “6.7% GDP growth outlook is an estimate, with risks evenly balanced on both sides.” He adds, “If you see our fan chart, there is a possibility that growth may be 7% or more.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Bulk deposit rate norms not linked to banks' NIM pressures
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says the guidelines on bulk interest rate deposits are “not linked to NIM pressures for banks.” He adds that the RBI has kept in mind that “underlying cost of bulk deposits can be varied for different categories” while framing the guidelines.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Central Bank says policy guided by headline inflation, not core inflation
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says, “We are neither dovish nor hawkish” and “we feel this is the right policy rate given current dynamics & outlook.” Stressing the RBI’s inflation framework, he says, “there should be no confusion about the framework—our target is headline inflation, and not core,” adding that the central bank “will take action as may be required given the outlook, how growth inflation dynamics play out.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Rupee could strengthen further if conflict de-escalates, says RBI Governor
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says the “underlying fundamentals of Indian economy [are] very strong” and that “it is quite possible rupee may further strengthen as conflict de-escalates.” He reiterates that “markets determine exchange rate prices; we don’t pursue any band,” adding that the RBI intervenes only in cases of “excessive volatility” or “speculative pressures.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: RBI expects healthy FCNR inflows, no plans to end scheme early
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says, “We have got robust FCNR flows so far, and expect to get good, healthy flows going forward.” He adds that there is “no proposal under consideration to close this scheme prematurely.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Central Bank says draft lending rate norms will focus on transparency, robust FCNR inflows have strengthened India's external position
RBI Deputy Governor Swaminathan J. Murmu says the emphasis in the draft guidelines on interest rates on advances will be on “transparency and conduct-related measures.”
Governor Sanjay Malhotra says “foreign inflows have ticked all boxes,” adding that “FCNR flows have been robust; it further fortifies our external position including BoP.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Central Bank to issue draft guidelines on lending rates, says no major change for NBFCs
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says the central bank will “issue draft guidelines on Interest Rates on Advances across REs for rationalising rates keeping in mind consumer protection.” He adds that “there is no major change in requirements for NBFCs” and “no major change on EBLR, but only rationalisation.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: RBI expects healthy FCNR inflows, no plans to end scheme early
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says, “We have got robust FCNR flows so far, and expect to get good, healthy flows going forward.” He added that there is “no proposal under consideration to close this scheme prematurely.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Knight Frank India sees support for real estate demand
Knight Frank India Chairman and Managing Director Shishir Baijal says, “Knight Frank welcomes the RBI’s decision to keep the policy rates unchanged,” calling it “a well-calibrated move” amid inflationary pressures and geopolitical uncertainties.
He adds that “a stable interest rate environment is likely to reinforce buyer confidence, provide greater certainty to businesses and investors, and ensure continued access to affordable financing,” saying the policy continuity is expected to sustain housing demand and investment activity across the residential and commercial segments.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: NAREDCO welcomes RBI's repo rate pause, sees boost for housing demand
NAREDCO President Parveen Jain says, “We welcome RBI’s decision to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25%.” He adds that “stability in interest rate will have positive impact on home buyers as well as developers and will maintain the momentum in demand for housing.”
Jain also said the decision “will give fillip to construction activity, MSMEs, building material industries and lakhs of workers associated with it,” and expects it to have a “positive impact on festive season sales of under-construction properties.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Economists see October pause, differ on timing of RBI's first rate hike
Kotak Mahindra Bank Chief Economist Upasna Bhardwaj says, “I’m not convinced necessarily that a stance change has to happen in a policy prior to the rate hike,” adding that “it’s going to be fairly data dependent for October.” She said, “It could still continue to be neutral… or even in a neutral stance, we can see 50 basis of a rate hike,” while adding that “a pause looks for now in October.”
DBS Bank India’s Ashhish Vaidya said, “October… is more of a pause unless the entire macro situation completely changes,” though he expects 100 basis points of rate hikes over this cycle, which “might actually take 12 to 18 months.”
Deutsche Bank Chief Economist Kaushik Das says, “October looks very unlikely unless things change very drastically from now till October,” adding, “You need 100 basis points rate hikes in this cycle… whether October or December, data will determine that.” He said the RBI would need to raise rates over the next six to nine months to take the repo rate to at least 6%.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Deutsche Bank's Kaushik Das sees repo rate rising to 6.25%
Deutsche Bank Chief Economist Kaushik Das says, “Rate hikes definitely have to happen,” arguing that with “growth being above 7% forward-looking” and inflation around 5%, the current repo rate is below where it should be.
Drawing a comparison with the pre-COVID period, he says, “the terminal repo rate should be 6.25%,” adding that “RBI needs to hike,” Das also said interest rate differentials with the US and other Asian economies “will matter over a period of time” in attracting debt inflows.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Kotak Mahindra Bank's Upasna Bhardwaj sees scope for rate hikes, retains December view
Kotak Mahindra Bank Chief Economist Upasna Bhardwaj says, “The governor has sounded fairly balanced,” adding that “growth is robust” and “if I look at the first quarter FY28 inflation estimates, they too are north of 5%, 5.3%.”
She adds, “In that background, can we have repo rate at 5.25% when we are looking at one year ahead inflation at above 5%… that is the reason, I am of the opinion that there is still scope for rate hikes.” Bhardwaj says, “We still retain as of now 50 basis of a rate hike in FY27, but starting December.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: DBS Bank's Ashhish Vaidya calls RBI policy 'slightly dovish', sees rupee staying stable
DBS Bank India Managing Director and Treasurer Ashhish Vaidya says the RBI policy was “a little bit more dovish than what we really expected,” adding that the central bank appeared “very comfortable on the inflation situation, very comfortable on growth,”
On markets, he said bond yields would remain “quite range bound” in the near term, while on the rupee, he says “the currency should be well behaved” as FCNR inflows and the RBI’s focus on curbing volatility support stability.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: SBI's Ashwini Kumar Tewari sees no rate hikes this fiscal despite inflation risks
SBI MD Ashwini Kumar Tewari says the RBI policy was “on expected lines” and that “the banking sector credit growth continues to be very strong,” with the economy showing “tremendous resilience.”
On the rate outlook, he says, “our house view is that the rates are not likely to be taken up in this financial year,” adding that “so far, there seem to be no indication of any rate increases,” while noting the RBI would continue to watch inflation data.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: CBRE's Anshuman Magazine says repo pause a 'positive signal' for real estate
CBRE Chairman & CEO Anshuman Magazine said, “Predictable borrowing costs provide homebuyers the confidence to move ahead with long-deferred purchase decisions, while developers benefit from a stable financing environment.” He added that the RBI’s decision to hold the repo rate at 5.25% “reflects a calibrated approach” and is “a positive signal heading into the festive season, which is typically the strongest period for housing demand in India.”
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: CPI estimates revised to 5% for FY27
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: GDP forecast raised to 6.7% for FY27
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Central Bank to standardise lending rate framework, ensure adequate liquidity
The governor says the central bank “will proactively ensure sufficient liquidity in the system.” He also announces a proposal to “harmonise and standardise” the regulatory framework on interest rates across all regulated entities to enhance transparency in lending rates.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: Credit growth remains robust, assures adequate liquidity
Governor Sanjay Malhotra says transmission in the credit market “moderated slightly during May and June,” but stresses that “credit growth continues to remain robust and broad-based.” He adds that the RBI “will proactively ensure sufficient liquidity in the system” to meet the economy’s funding needs.
RBI MPC August 2026 LIVE: GDP forecast raised to 6.7%
The Reserve Bank of India’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has incraesed its forecast for India’s gross domestic product (GDP) growth for the financial year 2027 to 6.7%. The RBI MPC had earlier forecast 6.6% for the same in June.

title: Reliance Industries shares surge most in 9 months, add over ₹1 lakh crore to market cap after Q2 results
snippet: Reliance Industries Ltd experiences its largest share surge in 9 months, gaining over ₹1 lakh crore in market cap following impressive Q2 FY27 results, driven by Oil-to-Chemicals and Jio Platforms ...
content:
- Oil & Gas
- 2 min read
Reliance Industries shares surge most in 9 months, add over ₹1 lakh crore to market cap after Q2 results
                    The shares rallied after a stronger-than-expected Q2, with a sharp rise in O2C earnings and improving net debt levels outweighing weakness in Reliance Retail.
                                    
            
        
                    
                    
                    
                                        Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) shares clocked their biggest single-day percentage gain in nine months on Monday, surging over 7 per cent in early BSE trade to a day's high of ₹1,246.45 against the previous close of ₹1,163.55.
The steepest jump since February 3, 2026 lifted RIL's market cap by over ₹1 lakh crore to around ₹16.86 lakh crore at the day's peak. The stock had touched a 52-week low of ₹1,152.30 on October 13.
Still down nearly 22.5 per cent from its record high, the counter trades above its 30-day and 50-day simple moving averages (SMAs) but below its 100-day, 150-day, and 200-day SMAs.
The rally followed RIL's strong Q2 FY27 results. According to Emkay Global, RIL posted a beat in consolidated EBITDA and adjusted net profit at ₹56,600 crore and ₹25,500 crore, respectively. Net debt fell 5 per cent sequentially to ₹1.17 lakh crore.
Emkay Global noted the beat was led by a 48 per cent sequential jump in Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C) EBITDA to ₹25,200 crore, driven by better margin capture in refining (effective product placement) and improved gasifier performance, alongside higher petrochemical deltas.
Emkay Global highlighted that Jio Platforms' consolidated EBITDA rose 5 per cent sequentially to ₹22,220 crore, beating estimates by 1 per cent, driven by 9.1 million net subscriber additions and an ARPU of ₹218.8.
Conversely, Reliance Retail was weak, with revenue up 1 per cent year-on-year at ₹91,700 crore and EBITDA down 10 per cent to ₹6,120 crore amid a festive-season mismatch and input cost inflation, though Reliance Consumer Products Ltd's revenue grew 1.6 times year-on-year to around ₹8,300 crore, the brokerage noted.
Emkay Global said management sounded constructive on O2C with 5 million barrels per day of refining capacity offline and higher ethane sourcing from two incoming ships, while New Energy projects remain on track.
"We believe Jio is on a steady trajectory while Retail should recover in ensuing quarters as festive demand picks up," the brokerage noted.
Building in stronger O2C and upstream earnings, Emkay Global raised FY27, FY28, and FY29 consolidated EBITDA estimates by 8 per cent, 4 per cent, and 1 per cent, and hiked EPS estimates by 15 per cent, 8 per cent, and 3 per cent to ₹69.8, ₹71.1, and ₹78.2.
However, citing weaker retail, macro volatility, and a 20 per cent holdco discount on Jio, Emkay Global cut its blended target multiple from 13x to 11.5x. It trimmed its September 2027 target price by nearly 8 per cent to ₹1,550 per share, while reiterating a ‘Buy’ rating, as valuations are highly attractive given recent stock weakness.

title: Reliance Industries: Q2 FY27 Revenue Hits ₹362,268 Crore, Up 27.8%
snippet: Reliance Industries Limited announces record-breaking Q2 FY27 financial results. Consolidated revenue surged 27.8% to ₹362,268 crore, with EBITDA reaching ₹62,409 crore. Key highlights include JPL's ...
content:
Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) has announced its financial results for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026. The company reported a record quarterly revenue of ₹362,268 crore, marking a significant 27.8% increase year-on-year. EBITDA also hit a new high of ₹62,409 crore, up 23.9% YoY. Profit After Tax (PAT) for the quarter reached ₹29,550 crore, surging 33.8%.
Record Financial Performance in Q2 FY27
Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) has achieved record financial milestones for the second quarter and first half of the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026. The company announced a consolidated revenue of ₹362,268 crore for the quarter, an impressive 27.8% increase compared to the same period last year. This performance highlights the company’s robust growth trajectory and market leadership across its diverse business verticals.
EBITDA and Profitability Highlights
EBITDA for the quarter reached an all-time high of ₹62,409 crore, reflecting a substantial 23.9% year-on-year growth. This strong operational performance, coupled with efficient cost management, led to a significant increase in profitability. Profit After Tax (PAT) for the quarter stood at ₹29,550 crore, a remarkable 33.8% surge over the previous year. The first half of FY27 also saw PAT crossing the ₹50,000 crore mark.
Segmental Performance and Key Achievements
The company’s Oil to Chemicals (O2C) business delivered its best-ever performance with EBITDA at ₹25,203 crore, up 67.9% YoY. Digital Services EBITDA also grew strongly by 17.7% to ₹22,223 crore. A significant event for the quarter was the momentous capital market debut of Jio Platforms Limited (JPL), becoming India’s second most valuable company.
Consolidated Financial Highlights (Q2 FY27 vs. Q2 FY26)
The consolidated financial highlights showcase strong year-on-year growth:
- Gross Revenue: ₹362,268 crore (up 27.8%)
- EBITDA: ₹62,409 crore (up 23.9%)
- Profit After Tax: ₹29,250 crore (up 32.1%)
- Profit After Tax and Share of Profit/(Loss) of Associates & JVs: ₹29,550 crore (up 33.8%)
Key Operational Updates
Jio Platforms Limited (JPL) reported quarterly revenue growth of 11.3% YoY to ₹47,485 crore, with EBITDA up 16.6% YoY to ₹21,879 crore. JPL achieved milestones of 30 million Fixed Broadband and 300 million 5G mobility subscribers. Reliance Retail Ventures Limited (RRVL) saw revenue grow by 6.4% YoY to ₹91,716 crore, though EBITDA declined by 11.1% to ₹5,886 crore. The Oil to Chemicals (O2C) segment achieved record quarterly revenue of ₹231,601 crore, up 44.2% YoY, with EBITDA surging 67.9% to ₹25,203 crore. The Oil and Gas segment revenue marginally declined by 0.6% YoY to ₹6,020 crore, with EBITDA down 2.0% to ₹4,901 crore.
JioStar reported revenue growth of 10.1% YoY to ₹6,806 crore, with EBITDA at ₹1,372 crore. The quarter also saw the rebranding and relaunch of JioHotstar in international markets.
Source: BSE

title: ‘Could easily go to $5,000, $10,000’: Jamie Dimon predicted gold’s 2026 surge. Here's where its price may go in 2027
snippet: Gold soared to record highs before giving back much of its gains. Now major Wall Street banks are fo...
content:
‘Could easily go to $5,000, $10,000’: Jamie Dimon predicted gold’s 2026 surge. Here's where its price may go in 2027
Laura Grande
9 min read
Moneywise and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue through links in the content below.
JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon isn't known for making bold price calls on gold. But in October 2025, he said the precious metal could reach $5,000 or even $10,000 an ounce, despite admitting he wasn't a buyer himself.
Roughly a year later, gold has had a wild ride (1). Prices surged to record highs in January 2026 before retreating sharply, leaving investors wondering whether Dimon's prediction still holds up and what could happen next year.
A single line on your car insurance policy could be inflating your premium by up to 30% — here's what to change
Gold has overtaken U.S. Treasuries as central banks' top reserve asset. Get Priority Gold's 2026 Precious Metals IRA Playbook for free
But during that interview with Fortune in late 2025 (2), Dimon made some pretty punchy claims when asked whether he thought gold was overvalued or undervalued.
Dimon started by saying, "I don't know. I mean, I'm not a gold buyer — it costs 4% to own it."
He was referring to the costs that can come with owning physical gold, including storage, insurance and other fees. Those expenses can eat into returns, particularly if prices stall or fall.
Still, Dimon didn't dismiss gold outright.
Gold has since climbed above $5,000 an ounce, only to give back a substantial chunk of those gains. As of mid-October 2026, spot prices had fallen to around $4,084, putting the metal well below its January peak (3).
Here's what drove gold's dramatic 2026 performance, what analysts expect in 2027, and how investors can weigh the potential benefits against the risks.
Why gold soared, then stumbled in 2026
Dimon's comments come as investors were already turning to gold amid growing concerns over the state of the economy, geopolitical tensions, and elevated asset prices.
For instance, Dimon expressed concerns over the floundering job market in America during an interview with CNN (4), a key indicator of a slowing economy.
"Asset prices are kind of high," he added. "In the back of my mind, that cuts across almost everything at this point."
This remark echoes a growing unease among market watchers: Valuations across multiple asset classes have swelled after years of easy money and resilient investor appetite. Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell recently cautioned that stock prices "are fairly highly valued" (5).
Dimon has continued to flag the risks facing markets. In a Sept. 17 interview with Yahoo Finance, he said, "It's not clear to me we've slayed inflation," warning that persistent price pressures, government deficits and heavy investment spending could keep interest rates higher than investors expect (6).
Gold carried that momentum into 2026, after rising 64% in 2025. Prices pushed past $5,500 an ounce in January, setting fresh records as investors sought a safe haven amid geopolitical uncertainty and strong central bank buying (7).
One of the biggest reasons investors turn to gold is that it's widely viewed as the ultimate safe haven asset. Gold isn't tied to any single country, currency or economy, and when financial markets turn volatile or geopolitical tensions flare, investors often flock to it — driving prices higher.
Gold's safe-haven status doesn't guarantee it will rise whenever markets get nervous. In 2026, prices swung sharply as investors reassessed inflation, interest rates and the U.S. dollar.
By late June, gold had slipped below $4,000 an ounce and was down about 7% for the year, despite its strong gains over the previous 12 months, according to the World Gold Council (8).
The slide continued into October. On Oct. 14, gold fell 1.8% to $4,083.94 an ounce after hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data lifted the dollar and Treasury yields, fuelling bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike (1).
That creates a challenge for gold because, unlike a savings account or bond, bullion doesn't generate interest income. Therefore, higher rates can make it less appealing compared with assets that pay a return (9).
Dimon has also warned that borrowing costs could climb higher than investors expect. On Oct. 13, he told reporters that inflation was proving stubborn and a jump in 10-year Treasury yields from 5% to 6% would be painful. "I am not predicting, but people need to prepare for it," he said (6).
Gold is now well below the $5,000 mark that Dimon said it could reach, let alone $10,000. For the metal to climb from $4,084 to $10,000, it would need to gain roughly 145% (1).
That doesn't rule out another rally, but $10,000 is still a long way off.
Dimon isn't the only one pointing to gold's potential. Prominent investors have long highlighted the metal's role in building a resilient portfolio.
Ray Dalio, founder of the world's largest hedge fund, Bridgewater Associates, told CNBC that "people don't have, typically, an adequate amount of gold in their portfolio," adding that "when bad times come, gold is a very effective diversifier" (10).
One way to get into gold that can also provide significant tax advantages is to open a gold IRA with the help of Priority Gold.
Gold IRAs allow investors to hold physical gold or gold-related assets within a retirement account, which combines the tax advantages of an IRA with the protective benefits of investing in gold. This can make it an attractive option for those looking to potentially hedge their retirement funds against economic uncertainties.
Gold's pullback hasn't stopped some big banks from betting on another rally.
Goldman Sachs expects prices to reach $5,400 an ounce by the end of 2027, while JPMorgan Global Research sees gold climbing to around $6,300. Both forecasts point to more upside, though neither comes close to Dimon's $10,000 prediction (11, 12).
Of course, a lot can change between now and then. If inflation stays high and interest rates remain elevated, gold could struggle to gain ground. A stronger U.S. dollar or easing geopolitical tensions could also take some shine off the metal.
But there are reasons prices could rebound, too. Falling interest rates, fresh market turmoil, and continued central bank buying could all help support gold, according to factors highlighted in the World Gold Council's outlook (8).
For investors, the big takeaway is that gold's recent run doesn't guarantee more gains ahead. Even a traditional safe haven can take a hit, and Dimon's $10,000 target remains a long way off.
A time-tested income play
Gold isn't the only asset investors turn to during inflationary times. Real estate has also proven to be a powerful hedge, with the added benefit of generating passive income through rent.
When inflation rises, property values often increase as well, reflecting the higher costs of materials, labor and land. At the same time, rental income tends to go up, providing landlords with a revenue stream that adjusts for inflation.
For instance, according to RealPage, a software provider to the real estate industry, average effective asking rents for market-rate apartments in the U.S. are expected to grow in 2026 (13).
In fact, RealPage forecasts a 2.3% rent climb across the country this year. If true, that would be a stark contrast from the 0.7% rent price decline during 2024.
Invest in real estate without locking in a mortgage
High home prices and elevated mortgage rates can make buying property a stretch. And becoming a landlord brings its own headaches, from finding tenants to dealing with maintenance and unexpected repairs.
The good news? You don't need to buy a property outright — or deal with leaky faucets — to invest in real estate today.
Arrived, a real estate platform company backed by investors such as Jeff Bezos, helps investors get into SEC-qualified investments in real estate, including rental homes, vacation rentals and diversified funds.
In addition to any property appreciation, Arrived's properties can help you earn a passive income stream without any of the extra work that comes with being a landlord. No midnight maintenance calls over burst pipes required.
Once you become an investor with Arrived, you'll have access to more than 596 properties in 67 plus markets. Eligible investors can also take advantage of Arrived's secondary market if you want to reshuffle your portfolio.
And, for a limited time, investors can get a 2% account match when opening an account and adding $2,000 or more.
Diversify with commercial real estate
Accredited investors can now tap into this opportunity through platforms such as Lightstone DIRECT, which gives you access to single-asset multifamily and industrial deals.
Lightstone DIRECT's direct-to-investor model ensures a high degree of alignment between individual investors and a vertically-integrated, institutional owner-operator — a sophisticated and streamlined option for individual investors looking to diversify into private-market real estate.

title: Gold Prices Crash 4.5% in Biggest Weekly Fall Since June | Dynamite News
snippet: Gold prices have suffered their steepest weekly decline since June, falling 4.5% amid concerns over US Federal Reserve ...
content:
Mumbai: Gold and silver prices are facing renewed selling pressure in domestic and international bullion markets, with gold registering its sharpest weekly decline since June. The correction has brought some relief to Indian jewellery buyers, as prices of precious metals remain below their levels at the beginning of November.
The decline comes amid growing uncertainty over the US Federal Reserve's monetary policy, concerns about persistent inflation and elevated crude oil prices. Investors are closely tracking global economic indicators, interest-rate expectations and movements in the US dollar to assess the next direction of bullion prices.
For Indian consumers planning jewellery purchases during the ongoing wedding season, the latest correction could offer a relatively favourable buying opportunity. However, gold and silver rates continue to fluctuate, and the final price of jewellery will depend on purity, making charges, GST and city-specific retail pricing.
International gold prices registered a 4.5 percent decline during the week, marking their steepest weekly fall since June. Spot gold edged up 0.1 percent to USD 3,879.71 per ounce after briefly touching USD 3,922.97 following the release of US Producer Price Index data. Meanwhile, US gold futures for December delivery settled largely unchanged at USD 3,886.30 per ounce.
The weekly correction reflects changing expectations surrounding the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory. Market participants are assessing whether persistent inflationary pressures could encourage the US central bank to maintain restrictive monetary conditions or consider further rate increases.
Higher interest rates generally create an unfavourable environment for gold because the precious metal does not generate interest income. When yields on interest-bearing assets become more attractive, investors may reduce their exposure to non-yielding assets such as gold. Elevated crude oil prices have added another layer of uncertainty by raising concerns about inflation and the possibility of tighter monetary policy.
The weakness in international bullion markets has extended beyond gold. Spot silver declined 1.9 percent to USD 49.05 per ounce, reflecting selling pressure across the precious metals segment. Platinum also fell 1.9 percent to USD 1,490.06 per ounce, while palladium moved in the opposite direction, gaining 1.1 percent to USD 1,004.40 per ounce. The contrasting movements underline the different demand and investment dynamics influencing individual precious metals.
Silver, in particular, is influenced by both investment demand and industrial consumption. Its exposure to manufacturing, electronics, solar energy and other industrial applications can make its price movements different from those of gold.
Domestic gold and silver prices remain below their November 1 levels, according to the retail price data cited in the report. At the time of reporting, a separate bullion market quotation placed gold at Rs 1,37,320 per 10 grams and silver at Rs 1,77,280 per kilogram. Goodreturns retail pricing, meanwhile, placed 24-karat gold at Rs 13,762 per gram and silver at Rs 195 per gram.
These figures represent different reported price references and should not be treated as directly interchangeable. Consumers should check the applicable jeweller or bullion benchmark before making a purchase.
According to the cited retail data, 24-karat gold was priced at Rs 13,762 per gram on November 15, compared with Rs 13,888 on November 1. This represents a decline of Rs 126 per gram. On a 10-gram basis, the corresponding price reduction amounts to Rs 1,260, while the difference across one kilogram of gold works out to Rs 1,26,000.
The 22-karat gold rate has also declined during the same period. Its price fell from Rs 12,730 per gram on November 1 to Rs 12,615 on November 15, representing a reduction of Rs 115 per gram. Consequently, the 10-gram price of 22-karat gold declined from Rs 1,27,300 to Rs 1,26,150, a reduction of Rs 1,150. For buyers purchasing larger quantities, the equivalent difference per kilogram is Rs 1,15,000.
Silver has also experienced a significant correction after reaching higher levels earlier in the month. According to the cited Goodreturns data, silver was priced at Rs 195 per gram on November 15, compared with Rs 200 per gram on November 1. On a kilogram basis, the rate declined from Rs 2,00,000 to Rs 1,95,000, representing a reduction of Rs 5,000 or 2.5 percent.
The metal had reached a reported peak of Rs 2,10,000 per kilogram on November 5 before declining to Rs 1,95,000 on November 13. Prices have remained broadly unchanged since that correction. The movement highlights the volatility in silver markets, where investment sentiment, industrial demand and international commodity trends collectively influence domestic retail prices.
Also Read: NZ vs India 5th ODI: Arshdeep, Siraj Star As India Beat New Zealand To Clinch Series 3-1
Gold prices continue to show marginal differences across major Indian cities because of variations in local taxes, transportation expenses, logistics and jewellery market conditions.
According to the cited retail rates, 24-karat gold was priced at Rs 13,777 per gram in Delhi, while 22-karat gold stood at Rs 12,630 per gram. Delhi's 24-karat rate was approximately Rs 15 higher than the cited national retail benchmark.
Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Kerala were reporting 24-karat gold at Rs 13,762 per gram. Ahmedabad and Vadodara were quoting the metal at Rs 13,767 per gram.
These differences are relatively small but can influence the final purchase cost, particularly for consumers buying larger quantities of gold jewellery. For buyers comparing prices, it is important to distinguish between the bullion rate, the retail jewellery rate and the final invoice value charged by an individual jeweller.
Gold purity is an important consideration when purchasing jewellery or investing in physical gold. 24-karat gold represents approximately 99.9 percent purity and is commonly associated with investment products such as gold bars and coins. Its relatively high purity makes it softer and less suitable for many types of everyday jewellery.
22-karat gold contains approximately 91.6 percent pure gold, with the remaining proportion consisting of other metals used to improve durability. It is widely preferred for traditional Indian jewellery, including wedding ornaments. 18-karat gold contains 75 percent pure gold and is frequently used in contemporary jewellery, diamond-studded ornaments and designer pieces.
The price of 18-karat gold is generally lower than that of 22-karat and 24-karat gold because of its lower gold content. However, the final retail price also depends on craftsmanship, design complexity, gemstone settings and making charges. Consumers should check the BIS hallmark and HUID identification details when purchasing hallmarked gold jewellery to verify its declared purity.
Gold prices had climbed significantly during the festive season, supported by traditional jewellery purchases, investment demand and increased buying activity around Dhanteras and Diwali. According to the cited retail price data, 24-karat gold reached Rs 14,460 per gram on November 9, the first trading session following the festival. Since then, prices have declined on most trading days as festive buying momentum eased and some investors booked profits after the earlier rally.
From the November 9 peak, gold has shed Rs 698 per gram. Silver has also corrected substantially, falling Rs 15,000 per kilogram from its November 5 peak. The decline reflects a combination of seasonal demand normalisation, profit-booking activity and pressure from international bullion markets.
The festive season often produces a temporary increase in jewellery purchases in India, one of the world's largest gold-consuming markets. Once this concentrated demand begins to ease, prices can become more sensitive to international market developments and investment flows.
The outlook for gold will depend heavily on developments in the global economy and financial markets. The US Federal Reserve's interest-rate decisions remain a major factor influencing bullion prices. Expectations of higher interest rates can increase the opportunity cost of holding gold, while expectations of monetary easing may improve its investment appeal.
The US dollar is another important variable. Gold is internationally traded in dollars, meaning fluctuations in the American currency can influence its affordability for buyers using other currencies, including the Indian rupee. Crude oil prices, inflation expectations, geopolitical developments and central-bank gold purchases can also influence investor sentiment.
In India, domestic gold prices additionally depend on rupee-dollar exchange rates, import-related costs, local demand and applicable taxes. Consequently, even when international gold prices decline, the extent of the benefit passed on to Indian consumers may vary depending on currency movements and domestic market conditions.
The latest correction could provide some relief to households preparing for weddings and other important occasions. For families planning to purchase traditional jewellery, even a modest reduction in the per-gram price can translate into meaningful savings when buying heavier ornaments.
For example, the metal value of a 10-gram 22-karat gold ornament has declined from Rs 1,27,300 on November 1 to Rs 1,26,150 on November 15, according to the cited retail figures. However, the final jewellery bill will be higher because the quoted gold rate represents only the underlying metal value.
Making charges generally range from approximately 5 percent to 18 percent, depending on the design, craftsmanship and jeweller. A 3% Goods and Services Tax is also applicable to jewellery purchases under the prevailing tax framework.
Consumers should therefore compare the complete invoice value rather than relying exclusively on the advertised gold rate. Jewellery buyers should also check purity certification, wastage calculations, buyback conditions and exchange policies before completing a transaction.

title: Goldman forecasts gold price to take two years to recapture all-time highs
snippet: It took gold just one month to climb more than 30% to a record, but its likely to take another two years before the precious ...
content:
Goldman forecasts gold price to take two years to recapture all-time highs
It took gold just one month to climb more than 30% to a record, but its likely to take another two years before the precious metal takes out a new peak, according to Goldman Sachs.
The bank expects further weakness and heightened volatility in the near term as continued Federal Reserve tightening weighs on non-yielding bullion.
“Once the Fed starts cutting, we expect Western ETF demand to recover, supporting a stronger gold rally to $5,600/ounce by end-2028,” strategists led by Lina Thomas wrote in a note Monday, adding gold prices could rally if macro-policy hedge demand were to return.
Gold has had a bruising year since hitting an all-time high of nearly $5,600 an ounce in late January. The yellow metal is on track for its worst annual loss in more than a decade, down nearly 11% as the artificial intelligence investment boom, soaring bond yields and expectations for higher interest rates have sapped demand for bullion.
If history is any guide, 2027 will look increasingly like 2022: a rising Fed policy rate weighs on private investor demand, but structural central bank buying keeps a firm bid under gold, according to the strategists.
Those bank purchases may help push gold higher to $4,650 an ounce by the end of next year, they said.
The metal traded at around $3,860 on Monday. Gold has been trending lower since late August, when Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warned that the central bank had “work to do” to rein in inflation. Policymakers are widely expected to hike rates at the upcoming policy meeting in December.
Firm inflation data last week prompted traders to bet on a more prolonged tightening cycle stretching into 2027. The Fed began raising rates in September for the first time in three years, lifting the benchmark to a range of 3.75% to 4%.
(By Yvonne Yue Li)

title: FII Inflows Hit ₹45,960 Crore as Nifty Rallies 8.6%
snippet: Nov 8, 2026 · FII inflows reached ₹45,960 crore in the week ended November 6 as Nifty rose 8.6%. Check foreign investor buying, DII selling and reasons for the rally.
content:
FII Inflows Surge to ₹45,960 Crore in a Week as Nifty Rallies 8.6%; What's Behind the Rise?
Foreign investors returned to Indian equities after heavy selling in October, while domestic institutions booked profits during the market rally. Lower crude oil prices, improving earnings and a selloff in global AI stocks were among the factors cited for the change in fund flows.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) invested a net ₹45,960 crore in Indian equities during the week ended November 6, 2026, as the Nifty 50 rallied 8.6% and the Sensex gained 8.8%. The inflows came after months of foreign selling and coincided with a sharp fall in crude oil prices, a selloff in global artificial intelligence (AI) stocks and strong buying in Indian large-cap shares.
FIIs remained net buyers throughout the five trading sessions, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) sold shares worth ₹24,197 crore during the week, according to exchange data. The buying also extended the FII inflow streak to 14 consecutive trading sessions by Friday, November 6.
The latest weekly inflows were higher than the ₹45,162 crore withdrawn by foreign investors in October, marking a sharp change in fund flows. FIIs invested ₹14,975 crore on Thursday and another ₹13,750 crore on Friday, taking their combined purchases over the two sessions to ₹28,725 crore.
The change in foreign investor activity came as Indian benchmark indices recorded their strongest weekly gains in nearly six years. The Nifty 50 ended the week above 25,000, while the Sensex closed above 81,000.
FII Inflows Rise as Domestic Investors Turn Net Sellers
Foreign investors have increased their purchases of Indian equities since the second half of October. According to exchange data, cumulative FII inflows reached ₹53,154 crore between October 16 and November 6.
The pace of buying picked up during the final two trading sessions of the week. Thursday's inflow of ₹14,975 crore was the highest single-day FII purchase in more than a year, followed by ₹13,750 crore on Friday.
Domestic investors, meanwhile, moved in the opposite direction. DIIs sold shares worth ₹10,445 crore on November 5 and ₹5,969 crore on November 6, taking their combined selling over the two sessions to ₹16,414 crore.
For the full week, domestic institutional selling reached ₹24,197 crore, ending an 11-week buying streak.
The change is notable because domestic institutions had been supporting Indian equities during the earlier period of foreign selling. With stock prices rising sharply during the week, DIIs booked profits while foreign investors increased their purchases.
The figures also show a difference between exchange-based FII data and foreign portfolio investor (FPI) figures reported by NSDL. While exchange data showed net FII purchases of ₹45,960 crore for the week, separate NSDL-based reports placed FPI inflows at ₹38,971 crore. The two figures are based on different reporting methods.
Why Are Foreign Investors Returning to Indian Equities?
The return of foreign investors comes as global technology shares face selling pressure over concerns about AI-related spending and valuations.
Investors have been reassessing their exposure to companies linked to artificial intelligence after a sharp rise in technology stocks in recent years. The correction has affected several overseas markets, including the US and major Asian technology markets.
India has relatively limited exposure to large AI-focused companies compared with some of these markets. Market participants have cited this difference, along with valuations and earnings growth, as possible reasons for renewed foreign interest in Indian equities.
Lower crude oil prices have also supported sentiment. Brent crude fell more than 16% during the week and touched a low of $93.22 per barrel before closing at $97.75 on Friday, according to Upstox's weekly market report.
India imports most of its crude oil requirements, making changes in international oil prices important for the domestic economy. Lower crude prices can reduce the country's import bill and ease pressure on the rupee.
Corporate earnings have been another factor. Results from several large Indian companies have supported buying in banking, financial services, automobiles and other heavyweight stocks.
Market participants have also pointed to the valuation gap between large-cap shares and smaller companies. The Nifty 50 was trading at a price-to-earnings multiple of around 19 times, compared with higher valuations in the mid-cap and small-cap segments, according to market data cited by Upstox.
Nifty Rallies 8.6%, Sensex Gains 8.8% During the Week
Indian benchmark indices recorded sharp gains during the November 2–6 trading week as foreign investors increased their purchases.
The Nifty 50 gained around 1,977 points, or 8.6%, during the week, while the Sensex advanced about 6,568 points, or 8.8%.
The rally was broad-based, with 46 of the 50 Nifty stocks ending the week higher. Three stocks declined and one remained unchanged.
Among the major gainers, Shriram Finance rose 16.8%, Bajaj Finance gained 15.8%, Mahindra & Mahindra advanced 15.7%, HDFC Bank climbed 13.8% and Reliance Industries increased 13.3%.
Power Grid Corporation of India, Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services were among the few Nifty stocks that ended the week lower.
The gains came despite weakness in global technology markets, with Indian equities benefiting from foreign inflows, lower crude prices and buying in large-cap stocks.
The Nifty and Sensex will resume regular trading on Monday, November 9, following the weekend. The next trading session will show whether foreign investors continue their buying streak after the sharp rise in benchmark indices.

Understanding Nifty Indices & Option Trading
What is the Nifty 50, exactly?
The Nifty 50 is a basket of the 50 largest companies on the NSE, weighted by free-float market capitalisation. Its 10 biggest constituents — mostly banks, IT and energy majors — drive most of any day's move, which is why watching Bank Nifty and Nifty IT alongside Nifty 50 gives a fast read on what's really moving the index.
What is option trading, in plain terms?
An option gives you the right, not the obligation, to buy (a "call") or sell (a "put") an index or stock at a fixed price by a set expiry date. Nifty 50 options — with weekly expiry every Tuesday — are the most actively traded derivatives contract in the world by volume, which is why so much of this page is built around Nifty's live level and trend.
How NSE Trends helps option traders specifically
Option premiums move on two things: where the underlying index is headed, and how much conviction the market has. This page gives you both — live index levels and signals for direction, and the FII/DII flow plus the after-market gap engine for conviction, all in one screen instead of five different tabs.
Where do all these Nifty 50 stock prices come from?
Every stock in the searchable list below is a live constituent of the Nifty 50, refreshed roughly once a minute. Advances vs declines (market breadth) and the gainers/losers lists update on the same cadence, so you can see whether a Nifty move is broad-based or being carried by one or two heavyweight stocks.
Reading FII and DII flows the right way
When Foreign Institutional Investors are net sellers and Domestic Institutional Investors are net buyers on the same day, domestic funds are often absorbing foreign outflows — a pattern option traders watch as one input among several, never a signal on its own. Cash and derivative flows can diverge too, which is why both are shown here.
Sector indices for spotting rotation early
Nifty IT, Nifty Auto, Nifty Metal, Nifty Pharma and the rest of the sector indices help you spot money rotating from one sector to another — often well before that rotation becomes visible in the Nifty 50 headline number itself.
Common Questions
What is the Nifty 50 doing today?
The live level, today's change, and a plain-English signal are shown at the top of this page in the headline indices section, refreshing automatically through the trading day.
What is option trading and how does it relate to Nifty?
Option trading means buying or selling the right — not the obligation — to trade an index or stock at a fixed price by a certain date. Nifty 50 options, with weekly expiry every Tuesday, are the world's most actively traded derivatives contract by volume.
What does FII and DII net buying or selling mean?
These figures show whether Foreign and Domestic Institutional Investors were net buyers or net sellers that day, across both cash and derivatives segments — we show both since they often tell different stories.
How often is data on this site updated?
Index prices refresh roughly every 15 seconds during market hours, Nifty 50 stock data about once a minute, and FII/DII figures every 30 minutes as official numbers land.
Is any of this investment advice?
No. NSE Trends shows live market data and technical context for informational purposes only. Nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell any security, index derivative, or option contract. Please do your own research or consult a registered financial advisor.

content:
US yield on the 10-year Treasury rose to 4.86 per cent from 4.84 per cent late Thursday. It had topped 5.30 per cent last month when worries about inflation, higher interest rates and rising government debt were spiking. US 30-year yields edged up 1 bp to 5.262 per cent after sliding in earlier trading to its lowest level since early September. The yield has fallen for five straight weeks. On the front end of the curve, the 2-year yield, which reflects interest rate expectations, climbed 4.7 bps to 4.524 per cent, but closed out the week with its sixth weekly decline in yield.
US Treasuries fell on Friday, pushing yields higher, after the world's largest economy created far more jobs than expected last month, bolstering expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at the December policy meeting.
When bond prices fall, yields rise. Despite Friday's jump, yields have steadily moved lower in recent weeks. For the week, the 10-year yield posted its fifth straight decline.
Why Did Yields Jump on Friday?
The rise in yields came after nonfarm payrolls jumped by 165,000 last month, following an upwardly revised 60,000 gain for September, the US Labor Department said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls advancing 65,000 after a previously reported 29,000 increase in September.
Helping to support yields was a report released Friday morning showing US employers hired many more workers last month than economists expected. It's the latest signal that the US economy continues to chug along despite high inflation.
On one hand, the encouraging data could mean the US economy may be able to absorb a slowdown in construction of AI data centres. But at the same time, the strong growth in jobs could push upward on inflation. Following the report, traders saw a greater probability of the Federal Reserve hiking its short-term interest rate at its next meeting in December, according to data from CME Group.
Rate hikes by the Fed can rein in inflation, but they do so by making borrowing money more expensive for everyone and slowing the overall economy.
A separate report, meanwhile, suggested that sentiment among US consumers unexpectedly improved. The preliminary report from the University of Michigan said sentiment rose for lower- and middle-wealth Americans but fell for those with the largest stock portfolios.
Perhaps more importantly for the bond market, the survey also suggested expectations for inflation in the coming year eased for Americans. That could prevent a vicious cycle where expectations for high inflation drive behaviour that only worsens inflation.
