title: Infosys: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
snippet: Large deal wins provide multiyear revenue visibility even as near-term pricing pressure forces guidance cuts.
content:
On its second-quarter fiscal year 2027 earnings call, held on Oct. 23, 2026, Infosys (NYSE:INFY) revised its full-year revenue growth guidance to 1% to 2% in constant currency terms. Competitive intensity and client demands for artificial intelligence (AI) productivity gains are pressuring pricing, but expanding deal pipelines show where future revenue will come from. Three takeaways from management explain how the company's navigating this shift.
1. Artificial Intelligence Revenue Grows Rapidly Amid Broader Pricing Pressure
Enterprise adoption of automated tools is accelerating across client operations, even as buyers demand productivity discounts on standard technology contracts. AI revenue grew 29% sequentially to account for over a tenth of total sales.
      Q2 AI revenue is now 10.5% of total revenue, with strong sequential growth of over 29%.
-- Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO  
2. Large Deal Wins Provide Multiyear Revenue Visibility
Management secured $5.2 billion in total contract value (TCV), the total dollar value of signed commitments, during the quarter. For the first half (H1) of the fiscal year, total large contract wins reached $8.8 billion.
      This takes H1's total large deal wins to $8.8 billion, which is an year-on-year growth of 28% with 62% net new.
-- Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO  
3. Soft Discretionary Spending Triggers Guidance Revision
Reduced client spending in retail and high-tech segments, combined with lower volume growth, forced management to lower its annual growth outlook. The company didn't change its operating margin (operating profit as a percentage of revenue) target of 20% to 22%.
      We are revising our full-year revenue growth guidance to 1%-2%, reflecting softer than expected H1 performance and our updated assessment for the rest of the year.
-- Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO  
Looking Ahead
Client spending remains cautious across several sectors, but expanding engagements in banking and energy help balance retail headwinds. The company holds structural advantages in offshore delivery models, while management tracks pricing discipline and client cost-optimization requests.
      While geopolitical and interest rate uncertainty continues to drive cautious spending, strong deal wins and a healthy pipeline positions us well for sustained growth.
-- Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO  
Long-term execution hinges on converting large contract commitments into active billing while expanding higher-margin technology deployments.
      As AI remains central to enterprise transformation in the years ahead, Infosys is well positioned to help navigate this shift.
-- Salil Parekh, CEO and MD

title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Marvell Technology: Which Artificial Intelligence Stock Is a Better Buy Going into 2027?
snippet: Marvell's forward P/E sits well below AMD's, but its revenue jump and rising margins raise a tougher...
content:
The race for artificial intelligence dominance is shifting from experimental software to heavy-duty hardware. Investors deciding between Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) must determine which niche offers the better long-term return.  
        AMD is a direct competitor in the high-end processor market, challenging incumbents with its CPU and AI-focused GPU semiconductor chips. Marvell specializes in data infrastructure, providing the connectivity and storage solutions that keep information moving within modern data centers. Both companies are essential players in the expanding digital economy, though they serve different corners of the tech stack among semiconductor stocks.  
            The case for Advanced Micro Devices  
        AMD designs high-performance computing products for data centers, gaming, and embedded systems. It serves major hyperscale customers like Microsoft and is expanding its compute-for-equity partnership with Meta Platforms. Recently, the company secured a multiyear partnership with OpenAI to deploy its Instinct MI450 series AI accelerators in massive data center environments.  
        In the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, revenue reached $34.6 billion, representing growth of 34.3% compared with the prior fiscal year. This expansion helped the company achieve net income of $4.3 billion for the period. Its net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining after all expenses are paid, was 12.5%.  
        As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.1x, a metric that compares total debt to shareholder equity to show reliance on borrowed money. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with liquid assets, was 2.9x. For the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, free cash flow was $6.7 billion, though stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 21.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.  
            The case for Marvell Technology  
        Marvell Technology operates as a fabless semiconductor company, designing hardware for data centers and communications networks. Its product line includes custom chips and storage controllers for high-speed connectivity. The company serves major cloud providers and has expanded its portfolio through the acquisition of Celestial AI and an agreement to acquire Lumentum Holdings.  
         In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year (FY) ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached $8.2 billion. This was a significant increase of 42.1% year over year, resulting in net income of $2.7 billion. Its net margin hit 32.6% for the period, marking a significant shift in profitability compared to the losses reported in previous fiscal years.  
            Based on its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.3x, while the current ratio was 2.0x to indicate sufficient liquidity for short-term needs. Free cash flow for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, was $1.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented 33.8% of operating cash flow.  
          Risk profile comparison  
       Advanced Micro Devices faces intense competition from Intel and Nvidia, especially following their recent strategic partnership. The company relies heavily on a limited number of manufacturing partners, creating vulnerability to supply chain disruptions. Additionally, strict government export restrictions on advanced AI chips to certain markets have resulted in inventory charges and limit future market access.  
       Marvell Technology contends with revenue concentration, as a significant portion of sales comes from a small group of large distributors and direct customers. Like many peers, it depends on third-party foundries in the Pacific Rim, creating risks from geopolitical tensions or regional natural disasters. The company also faces pressure from major cloud providers developing their own proprietary chips, which could reduce long-term demand for its custom products.  
       Valuation comparison  
       Based on the Forward P/E, which compares price to future earnings estimates, and the P/S ratio, Marvell Technology appears to be the more attractively valued option.  
          Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.  
       Which stock would I buy for 2027?  
       AMD and Marvell have become powerhouses amid the artificial intelligence boom. AMD's business is firing on all cylinders, as illustrated by its Meta partnership, announced Oct. 27, a $2.5 billion investment in Anthropic stock, and its $13.4 billion in fiscal Q3 sales, representing a 45% year-over-year increase. Even so, I would buy Marvell Technology stock going into 2027.  
          Because of AMD's streak of successes in the AI sector, and the recently-revealed investigation into chief rival Nvidia's CEO by that company's Board of Directors, shares of AMD have become pricey, as Wall Street shifts away from GPU market leader Nvidia. This makes Marvell stock the better value, evidenced by both its forward earnings and sales multiples.  
       Marvell is also delivering spectacular results. During its investor day on Oct. 6, management shared updated revenue guidance that exceeded Wall Street expectations. The company raised sales in its 2028 fiscal year, which ends Jan. 31, 2028, to $20 billion, up from its prior guidance of $18 billion, and well above the $8.2 billion generated in FY 2026. It also set a FY 2031 revenue target of $70 billion to $90 billion.  
       Those figures were before Marvell announced it was acquiring Lumentum, a fast-growing optical components provider seeing massive demand due to AI's need for speed. Lumentum's sales of $1.3 billion for its fiscal Q1, ended Sept. 26, represented an impressive 137% year-over-year increase. With Lumentum, Marvell is poised to deliver strong growth in the coming years.

title: Qualcomm Demonstrates HBC Memory With 18X Better Bandwidth
snippet: Qualcomm has validated High Bandwidth Compute, the memory cornerstone of its data-center strategy...
content:
Qualcomm has reached a major milestone in the development of the memory technology which underpins their entire data center strategy revealed at the company's Investor Day event in June: High Bandwidth Compute, or HBC.
It is unusual for a company to announce an internal development benchmark, but the industry has been skeptical of Qualcomm's multi-year roadmap into the datacenter of the AI world, so this will be seen as positive news. The strategy is to focus on servers used in AI inference, power efficiency, high-bandwidth memory, and custom hyperscaler silicon—not on competing head-on in GPU training. The company is packaging these components under the new Dragonfly brand, with a stated goal of more than $15 billion in annual data-center revenue by fiscal 2029.
Discussing this goal with ex-Alphawave Semi CEO Tony Pialis (now EVP and GM of the data center segment at Qualcomm) at the Company's recent Snapdragon Summit, Mr. Pialis asserted that he sees so much demand for Dragonfly at major AI players that he expects to meet or exceed that goal, even if he managed to "massively screw this up". After all, the $15B goal is less that 10% of Nvidia's 2026 data center revenue, and Qualcomm has already announced deals with major players. (Note that Qualcomm is a client of my company, Cambrian-AI Research.)
HBC is the Cornerstone of Qualcomm's Data Center Strategy
The underlying thesis here is that inference increasingly becomes constrained by memory movement, latency, and data-center power—not simply raw compute. Solving this problem, ideally first and better than the competition, would launch Qualcomm Qualcomm's High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) architecture is meant to put compute and memory closer together, while its connectivity portfolio extends from copper to optical links for rack- and cluster-scale systems. The HBC memory approach will be deployed on both AI accelerators (AI250/300) and CPUs (C1000 and Snapdragon).
Target Customers Like What Qualcomm is Showing Them
While still about a year out, Qualcomm has already been able to secure some major wins with its roadmap:
• Meta: A multigenerational agreement to deploy the Dragonfly C1000 CPUs in Meta's next-generation server fleet, with production expected to begin in 2028.
• Amazon Web Services: A multigenerational custom-silicon and optical-networking agreement; Qualcomm said associated commercial processors were already in production, with revenue expected to begin in fiscal Q1 2027.
• Two additional hyperscaler custom-silicon wins: Qualcomm disclosed two large, unnamed hyperscaler designs, with meaningful revenue expected to start in fiscal 2027.
• Microsoft/Azure signal: Microsoft leadership indicated Azure deployment interest around Qualcomm's HBC accelerator, though Qualcomm's most explicit named CPU customer at launch was Meta.
• Capability-building acquisitions: Qualcomm acquired Alphawave Semi for high-speed wired/optical connectivity and Modular to strengthen a hardware-neutral AI software layer—important pieces for selling complete data-center platforms rather than isolated chips.

title: FCNR(B) Inflows Squeeze Private Bank Margins in Q2, Recovery Expected
snippet: Leading private banks in India, including HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank, experienced a decline in net interest margins ...
content:
Leading Indian private banks, including HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Axis Bank, faced pressure on their net interest margins in the second quarter due to substantial Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposit inflows, though they anticipate a recovery as funds are deployed and interest rates stabilise.
Key Points
- Leading private banks, including HDFC, ICICI, and Axis, reported a decline in Net Interest Margins (NIMs) in Q2 due to large FCNR(B) deposit mobilisations.
- HDFC Bank's NIM fell by 10 basis points to 3.16 per cent, with management expecting a reversal as the interest rate cycle turns upwards and loan portfolios shift towards retail and MSMEs.
- ICICI Bank's NIM declined by 18 basis points to 4.18 per cent, attributing the contraction to FCNR(B) deposits, but anticipates margins to improve after Q3.
- Axis Bank saw a 10-basis point NIM drop to 3.36 per cent, partly due to FCNR(B) deposits, but remains on track for its 3.8 per cent NIM guidance.
- Banks are strategically deploying FCNR(B) funds, including repaying existing deposits and supporting loan growth, which is expected to aid margin recovery in future quarters.
The margins of leading private banks in the second quarter this financial year came under pressure from the large mobilisation of deposits under Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank), or FCNR (B), which came through the Reserve Bank of India's special window.
However, banks expect margins to recover over the coming quarters because the funds are being deployed and the turnaround in the interest-rate cycle supports lending yields.
HDFC Bank's Performance and Outlook
HDFC Bank, the country's largest private lender, reported a 10-basis point decline in the net interest margin (NIM) to 3.16 per cent in the September quarter from 3.26 per cent in the preceding quarter.
According to HDFC Bank Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan, the bank's margins, which had faced pressure from a faster repricing of assets and a lag in the cost of funds during the declining interest-rate cycle, were positioned for a reversal as the rate cycle turned upwards.
A shift in the loan portfolio towards retail and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), relative to corporate loans and home loans, would further support margins over time, he said.
ICICI Bank's Margin Contraction and Recovery Plan
ICICI Bank, the country's second-largest private lender, saw its NIM decline by 18 basis points to 4.18 per cent in the quarter from 4.36 per cent in the previous quarter. Sandeep Batra, executive director, attributed the contraction largely to FCNR (B) deposits and said the full impact would be reflected in the December quarter.
"After the third quarter, we expect the margins to start moving up, even based on the current level of policy rates," Batra said, adding that the bank was focused on deploying the funds optimally.
The deposits have provided the bank a stable source of funding for three to five years.
ICICI Bank has used a portion of the funds to repay existing deposits and support loan growth during the quarter, while the remaining amount will be deployed over the next two quarters, Batra said.
Axis Bank's Q2 Results and Future Guidance
Axis Bank, the country's third-largest private lender, reported a 10-basis point decline in the NIM to 3.36 per cent in Q2FY27 from 3.46 per cent in the previous quarter.
The bank attributed the pressure, in part, to FCNR (B) deposits, but said it remained on track to meet its NIM guidance of 3.8 per cent.
During the analyst call, the bank's management said it had used a portion of the funds towards the end of the September quarter to retire higher-cost non-retail term deposits (NRTDs), with the benefit expected to flow through to margins in the current quarter.
"Last quarter we utilised some portion of these funds to retire the more expensive NRTDs, which was done towards the end of the quarter.
"We should be able to see some benefit of that come through in the next quarter in terms of NIM uplift," the management said.
FCNR(B) Mobilisation by Top Lenders
ICICI Bank mobilised $17.88 billion in gross FCNR (B). Its international branches and subsidiaries extended $9 billion in loans against these deposits and issued $3.63 billion in standby letters of credit (SBLCs).
HDFC Bank rang up approximately $11.5 billion, the second-largest amount among private lenders.
Its overseas arms extended around $5.7 billion in loans against these deposits and issued $3.1 billion in SBLCs.
Axis Bank mobilised $10.62 billion, deploying $4.57 billion to support lending via its overseas branches and using the remaining funds to help retire high-cost non-retail term deposits.

title: HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Margin blues to growth drivers in Q4- 7 key takeaways
snippet: Apr 20, 2026 · The era of 4%+ net interest margins (NIM) may be ending for India's banking giants. While HDFC and ICICI Bank reported higher profits in Q4 FY26, "sticky" deposit costs are now anchoring earnings ...
content:
Two big banking results were declared over the weekend – HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank both announced their Q4 performance. It was interesting to note that ICICI Bank’s net interest margin of 4.32% for the quarter and full year was unchanged from last fiscal, while HDFC Bank reported a net interest margin of 3.38% in Q4 as it continues to adjust its balance sheet post-merger.
At the same time, both banks reported higher profits, stable asset quality and sustained credit demand, alongside dividend payouts.
Here is a quick look at the performance of both banks in Q4FY26.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Net interest margins hold in a defined range
HDFC Bank reported a net interest margin of 3.38% for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, with net interest income increasing to Rs 33,100 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 32,100 crore in Q4 FY25, marking a 3.2% YoY increase. The increase in income comes despite pressure from rising deposit costs and a higher share of term deposits.
In parallel, ICICI Bank reported a net interest margin of 4.32% for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, compared with 4.30% for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, while the margin for the year ended March 31, 2026 remains at 4.32%, unchanged from the year ended March 31, 2025. Net interest income increased to Rs 23,000 crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 21,200 crore in Q4 FY25, reflecting 8.4% growth YoY.
Anindya Banerjee, Senior Management/Financial Officer, ICICI Bank, said, “I guess at a margin level, we continue to look at sort of range-bound margins, unlikely to move up, but should be broadly in this range is what we would think.” Banerjee adds that cost of deposits declines to 4.43% in Q4 FY26 from 4.55% in Q3 FY26.
At the same time, Kaizad Bharucha, Deputy Managing Director, HDFC Bank, added that, “ The cost of funds, while time deposit repricing can continue to be there. Again, it depends on the rate cycle and what happens. You see that there’s a stickiness in the rates across. For the last, I think at least four months, we have not seen our time deposit rate change in the market. We are fairly priced with the competition, and we’ve not seen four months of any kind of change that has happened. Which, again, as one would give some time for change, you’ve seen that there are other things in the month of March, the geopolitical thing that’s coming about, that has hardened the rates again. It remains to be seen, but it’s range-bound, is what I would say, but focus more on the returns.”
Taken together, the data and commentary indicate that margins are stabilising within a narrower band, with funding costs shaping outcomes.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Loan growth continues
HDFC Bank reported gross advances increasing to Rs 29.60 lakh crore at March 31, 2026 from Rs 26.44 lakh crore at March 31, 2025, marking an increase of Rs 3.16 lakh crore. Advances under management increased to Rs 30.57 lakh crore at March 31, 2026 from Rs 27.73 lakh crore at March 31, 2025.
Meanwhile, ICICI Bank reported total advances increasing to Rs 15.54 lakh crore at March 31, 2026, from Rs 13.42 lakh crore at March 31, 2025, a rise of Rs 2.12 lakh crore. Domestic advances increased to Rs 15.12 lakh crore from Rs 13.11 lakh crore over the same period.
Sandeep Bakhshi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, ICICI Bank, said, “Looking ahead, we see many profit opportunities to drive risk-calibrated profitable growth and grow market share across key segments. We remain focused on maintaining a strong balance sheet, prudent provisioning, and healthy levels of capital while delivering sustainable and predictable returns to our shareholders.”
Similarly, Sashidhar Jagdishan, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, HDFC Bank, added that, “You sort of make the math, it comes to somewhere around the 13.5%-13.9%. That’s the system growth. Obviously, it has been faster. It is something that we have to navigate, but it’s not too far away from the momentum we have seen from a 5.4% growth in FY25 to a 12% growth. I think, as Kaizad was mentioning, we are very well-positioned to continue that kind of momentum in a manner that we do responsible growth, and we don’t want to overstretch beyond what could potentially have some landmines in future.”
Jagdishan adds that the bank continues to calibrate growth in line with system trends while maintaining balance sheet discipline.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Deposit growth and funding mix remain central
HDFC Bank reports deposits increasing to Rs 31.05 lakh crore at March 31, 2026 from Rs 27.15 lakh crore at March 31, 2025, an increase of Rs 3.90 lakh crore. Average deposits increased to Rs 28.51 lakh crore in Q4 FY26 from Rs 25.28 lakh crore in Q4 FY25.
In comparison, ICICI Bank reports total deposits increasing to Rs 17.95 lakh crore at March 31, 2026 from Rs 16.10 lakh crore at March 31, 2025, an increase of Rs 1.85 lakh crore.
Sashidhar Jagdishan, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, HDFC Bank, says, “On the deposits. Let me first take the granularity of deposits. Retail has always been, as a proportion of total deposits, about 80%-85% of the total bank’s deposits. You have three significant verticals where we have a lot of close relationships, whether it’s corporate banking or whether it is the capital market segment as well. Now let’s talk about the 80%-85%, which is the retail segment. Within that, there is definitely a focus on trying to see how we can garner more granular time deposits.”
On the other hand, Anindya Banerjee, Senior Management/Financial Officer, ICICI Bank, said, “Post all the measures that were taken at a policy level through last year, and from our own side, I think with some of the factors like the interest rate stabilizing, benchmark stabilising, growth has picked up and the general outlook on the economy has been quite positive.”
Banerjee adds that deposit growth remains aligned with improving economic activity and internal initiatives.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Dividend payout trend
HDFC Bank recommended a final dividend of Rs 13.00 per share for the year ended March 31, 2026, following a special interim dividend of Rs 2.50 per share, taking the total payout to Rs 15.50 per share. Standalone profit after tax increases to Rs 0.747 lakh crore in FY26 from Rs 0.673 lakh crore in FY25, while consolidated profit increases to Rs 0.760 lakh crore from Rs 0.708 lakh crore.
At the same time, ICICI Bank recommended a dividend of Rs 12 per share for the year ended March 31, 2026. Standalone profit after tax increases to Rs 0.501 lakh crore in FY26 from Rs 0.472 lakh crore in FY25, while consolidated profit increases to Rs 0.542 lakh crore from Rs 0.510 lakh crore.
The continuation of dividend payouts across both banks aligns with steady earnings growth and strong capital adequacy positions.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Asset quality stable
HDFC Bank reports gross NPA ratio declining to 1.15% at March 31, 2026 from 1.33% at March 31, 2025, while net NPA ratio declines to 0.38% from 0.43% over the same period.
Kaizad Bharucha, Deputy Managing Director, HDFC Bank, said , “Our asset quality is extremely healthy at 1.15% gross NPAs. This has been tested across three decades of business cycles. The bank has created a large provisioning buffer of almost 125 basis points to absorb any shocks in the future. Where this is obviously contingent upon any future events that may occur in the future, we don’t have any stress in our portfolio as we speak.”
Meanwhile, ICICI Bank reports a net NPA ratio declining to 0.33% at March 31, 2026, from 0.39% at March 31, 2025, with a provisioning coverage ratio at 75.8% and contingency provisions at Rs 0.131 lakh crore.
Anindya Banerjee, Senior Management/Financial Officer, ICICI Bank, added, “I think a couple of things on the provisioning side. One, if you look at it even on a year-on-year basis on the retail side, the net additions are lower. In particular, over the last few quarters, the additions to NPLs on the unsecured side, which are provided pretty aggressively, have been coming down. That has brought down the provisioning requirements even on the retail side.”
Banerjee added that lower additions to non-performing loans are helping contain provisioning requirements.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Guidance signals stability in margins and continued growth
HDFC Bank’s management indicates that the focus remains on return on assets, loan growth and deposit quality rather than margin expansion, while digital adoption levels of 97% for payments and 92% for service interactions support operational efficiency.

title: HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: CASA, Margins and Asset Quality | Altys Labs
snippet: Jul 7, 2026 · HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank both expanded deposits and net interest income in the September 2026 quarter. Their latest disclosures nevertheless describe different funding and earnings profiles, and comparing them requires more care than ranking two margin percentages.
content:
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: CASA, Margins and Asset Quality
Compare HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank through deposits, CASA, net interest margin, asset quality and returns. A bank-analysis framework, not a stock recommendation.
HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank both expanded deposits and net interest income in the September 2026 quarter. Their latest disclosures nevertheless describe different funding and earnings profiles, and comparing them requires more care than ranking two margin percentages.
Updated 5 November 2026 for the quarter ended 30 September. This replaces broad historical descriptions with dated observations while retaining the established comparison URL. Figures below concern the standalone banks unless explicitly labelled otherwise.
Deposit growth is not one interchangeable number
HDFC’s 17 October release filed with SGX, pages 19–21 distinguishes average from period-end deposits. ICICI’s September-quarter performance review also separates those measures and gives an additional FCNR-related comparison.
View the chart data
| Observation | Per cent year-on-year, average deposits in Q2 FY27 | 
|---|---|
| HDFC Bank | 16.8 | 
| ICICI Bank | 21.2 | 
Average quarterly balances, not period-end deposit growth. Source: HDFC release page 20 and ICICI performance review, Deposit growth section. Source: Both banks' 17 October disclosures.
HDFC’s period-end deposit growth was 18.8%. ICICI reported 27.1%, or 17.0% excluding FCNR(B) deposits. That exclusion is disclosed by ICICI; it is not an Altys adjustment applied to both banks.
Altys interpretation: a headline growth gap does not establish the same gap in recurring domestic funding strength. Average balances, closing balances and a disclosed exclusion illuminate different parts of the funding picture. None should be substituted silently for another.
Deposits also have prices and maturities. A bank can raise more funding while paying more for it. Whether that supports earnings depends on the assets funded and their repricing, rather than deposit growth in isolation.
Net interest income grew, but it is not a margin
View the chart data
| Observation | Per cent year-on-year, Q2 FY27 standalone NII | 
|---|---|
| HDFC Bank | 9.7 | 
| ICICI Bank | 17.7 | 
Growth in rupee net interest income, not growth in NIM. HDFC release page 19; ICICI performance review, Profit and loss section. Source: HDFC and ICICI quarter disclosures.
HDFC reported NIM of 3.16% on total assets and 3.32% on interest-earning assets. ICICI reported NIM of 4.18%, versus 4.36% in the prior quarter; its review identifies an eight-basis-point tax-refund-interest benefit in that earlier quarter.
These figures should keep their company definitions. They are not the same as an ordinary industrial company’s operating margin, and the difference between unlabelled percentages is not a clean measure of competitive advantage.
Altys interpretation: growth in the earning base can support NII even when the spread earned on that base is under pressure. Conversely, a stable margin does not guarantee fast income growth. The bank NIM guide separates the balance and pricing effects.
CASA needs a matching observation basis
HDFC reports period-end CASA of 31.6%; ICICI reports an average CASA ratio of 35.8%. They are deliberately not presented as a like-for-like peer ranking here.
Averaging matters when balances change within a quarter. Deposit composition also matters: an increase in term funding can change the ratio without proving that current and savings balances declined in rupees. For HDFC, the merger-era funding change remains historical context, not an explanation that can automatically be attached to every later quarterly movement.
Correction retained from 17 October 2026: borrowings do not directly dilute CASA’s denominator. CASA uses total deposits, not total funding or liabilities.
Asset quality is a stock and a process
At September-end, HDFC reported gross and net NPA ratios of 1.11% and 0.37%. ICICI reported 1.20% and 0.30%. These are dated ratios, not forecasts of future credit losses.
A lower stock ratio can accompany recoveries, write-offs or growth in the denominator. Interpreting it requires the changes that produced it, the lending mix and the provisions held. Net NPA also depends on provisions, so it should not be treated as an independent ranking of underwriting quality.
Altys interpretation: the useful comparison is the earnings supported by funding, operating costs and credit outcomes together. A bank that grows quickly still needs to collect; a bank with low current NPAs still faces the risk in newly originated loans. This report does not award an overall winner.
What to retain for the next result
The September disclosures support a more specific research record: how average funding develops, what drives NII, whether a margin change contains a special item, and how asset quality evolves alongside loan mix. Later results can confirm or challenge each point separately.
The Excel-readable inputs retain the plotted growth rates and source definitions. Continue with HDFC’s CASA history and the bank-results framework.
Altys helps teams monitor companies and revisit earlier guidance, filings and financial observations. Available Excel exports let analysts check the underlying work outside the narrative. Request access.
Public-disclosure comparison for information and education. No securities recommendations, price targets or expected-return claims.
Frequently asked questions
What changed in the latest HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank comparison?
The comparison now uses public September 2026 quarter disclosures. Both banks grew deposits and net interest income, but their funding mixes, reported margin definitions and asset-quality observations require separate interpretation.
Why must the two banks' NIM figures be compared carefully?
HDFC reports NIM on total assets and separately on interest-earning assets. A comparison must preserve those denominators and the other bank's disclosed methodology rather than ranking unlabelled percentages.
Why did HDFC Bank's CASA ratio change after the merger?
The merger changed the deposit and funding mix, including inherited term deposits and borrowings. CASA is divided by deposits, not all liabilities. Borrowings affect funding cost but do not directly enter that denominator.
Which is the better buy, HDFC Bank or ICICI Bank?
This article makes no investment recommendation. It compares dated public disclosures and the questions they raise, not expected stock returns.

title: HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Scale vs Returns
snippet: Jun 12, 2026 · Compare HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank across business models, financial metrics, competitive strengths, strategy and key risks using official disclosures.
content:
HDFC Bank operates at greater balance-sheet scale after its merger. ICICI Bank has delivered strong return and asset-quality metrics. The comparison turns on deposits, margins, credit costs and integration.
Why This Comparison Matters
HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank are India’s two largest private-sector banking franchises. HDFC Bank’s merger with HDFC Limited materially changed its balance sheet, funding mix and loan composition, making pre-merger trends less comparable.
For the March 2026 quarter, HDFC Bank reported net profit around ₹19,221 crore and net interest income near ₹33,080 crore. ICICI Bank reported net profit around ₹13,700 crore, net interest income near ₹22,979 crore, net interest margin around 4.32% and gross NPA near 1.40%. Exact definitions and consolidated-versus-standalone basis must be checked.
Loan growth without deposit quality can weaken the funding franchise. The most important comparison is therefore not profit alone.
Quick Comparison
Quarter ended March 2026 / Quarter ended March 2026
About ₹19,221 crore / About ₹13,700 crore
Post-merger funding and integration / Return quality and asset discipline
Deposits, NIM, credit costs and capital / NIM, asset quality, fees and capital
Financial Snapshot
| Measure | HDFC Bank | ICICI Bank | Reading note | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Reporting period | Quarter ended March 2026 | Quarter ended March 2026 | Broadly aligned. | 
| Net profit | About ₹19,221 crore | About ₹13,700 crore | HDFC Bank is larger. | 
| Core issue | Post-merger funding and integration | Return quality and asset discipline | Different strategic focus. | 
| Key measures | Deposits, NIM, credit costs and capital | NIM, asset quality, fees and capital | Use standalone basis consistently. | 
Business Models
HDFC Bank
HDFC Bank combines retail, wholesale, payments and a large post-merger mortgage book. Its scale and distribution are major advantages, while replacing higher-cost funding with deposits is a multi-year task.
ICICI Bank
ICICI Bank has strengthened its balance sheet, digital capabilities and risk discipline. Its recent economics depend on maintaining margins and credit quality without taking excessive concentration.
Competitive Battlegrounds
- Low-cost deposits and transaction banking
- Retail, SME and corporate credit
- Digital engagement and cross-selling
The stronger company can change by battleground. Distribution may favour one side, while capital efficiency, regulation or technology transition favours the other. The analysis should therefore avoid declaring a universal winner from one quarter or one headline metric.
Strategic Advantages
HDFC Bank
- Largest private-bank scale
- Broad branch and payments franchise
- Mortgage and retail customer base
ICICI Bank
- Strong recent return metrics
- Improved asset quality
- Efficient digital and risk execution
What Can Break
HDFC Bank
- Post-merger funding pressure
- Net interest margin normalisation
- Integration and balance-sheet complexity
ICICI Bank
- Credit-cycle complacency
- Deposit competition
- Margin pressure as rates change
How to Read It
Use consistent standalone data and compare deposit growth, CASA mix, loan growth, NIM, slippages, credit cost, ROA, ROE and CET1. One quarter can be distorted by recoveries, tax or treasury items.
A sensible investor or strategy team should separate operating quality from market price. An excellent business can be a poor purchase at an excessive valuation, while a weaker business can appear cheap because the market is correctly pricing structural risk. The comparison therefore stops at business analysis and does not create a buy or sell recommendation.
Evidence to Retain
A comparison should be reproducible. Keep the original annual report or results release, the reporting date, the metric definition, the currency and any segment reconciliation used. For HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, record whether the figure is consolidated, standalone, segmental, adjusted or reported under GAAP or another accounting framework.
When management uses an operating measure such as bookings, order value, active clients, subscribers or ARPU, retain its definition and avoid replacing it with a similar term from the other company. That evidence prevents a visually neat table from becoming an economically false comparison.
Practical Example
Decision Checklist
- Use standalone numbers consistently.
- Track deposits against loans.
- Review NIM and credit cost.
- Compare slippages and recoveries.
- Assess capital ratios.
- Separate merger effects.
Common Questions
Which bank is larger?
HDFC Bank is larger by balance-sheet and profit scale.
Why is the merger important?
It changed HDFC Bank’s loan mix, funding structure and historical comparability.
What is the best profitability metric?
ROA and ROE, read with capital and credit cost, are more useful than profit alone.
Can low NPAs guarantee safety?
No. Underwriting quality and the future credit cycle still matter.
Official Sources
Use the latest filing and the same reporting basis before reproducing any number. Market conditions, company disclosures and segment definitions can change.

title: HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank (2026)
snippet: Aug 25, 2026 · HDFC Bank has the bigger balance sheet and distribution machine, but ICICI Bank currently earns a substantially wider net interest margin and is growing loans and profit faster.
content:
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank (2026): Deposits, NIM, NPAs, Growth & Which Bank Is Stronger?
Private-bank comparison · Q1 FY2027 results · Market snapshot 25 August 2026
HDFC Bank is still the bigger banking franchise. ICICI Bank is currently the faster one. HDFC leads on deposits, advances, branch network, market capitalisation and capital adequacy. ICICI leads on net interest margin, recent loan growth, profit growth and net NPA ratio. That makes HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank less about finding a universally "better bank" and more about deciding whether scale or present operating momentum deserves the higher weight.
Do not compare banks using the same ratios used for cement, IT or FMCG companies
For banks, debt-to-equity, current ratio and conventional ROCE are not the right starting points because deposits are part of the operating model rather than simply corporate debt.
The important comparison is built around net interest margin, deposit franchise, CASA, loan growth, asset quality, credit costs, capital adequacy, profitability and the quality of the loan book.
This is why this HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank page deliberately does not force generic industrial-company ratios into the analysis.
The short version: HDFC wins scale, ICICI wins current operating momentum
HDFC Bank has the bigger balance sheet and distribution machine, but ICICI Bank currently earns a substantially wider net interest margin and is growing loans and profit faster.
HDFC Bank ended June 2026 with gross advances of approximately ₹30.61 lakh crore and period-end deposits of about ₹31.71 lakh crore.
ICICI Bank ended the same quarter with total loans of approximately ₹16.31 lakh crore and deposits of around ₹18.34 lakh crore.
HDFC is therefore much larger.
Yet ICICI Bank's Q1 FY2027 net interest margin was 4.36%. HDFC Bank's reported NIM was 3.26% on total assets and 3.40% based on interest-earning assets.
ICICI also delivered 19.6% year-on-year loan growth and 15.9% PAT growth. HDFC's gross advances grew 15.4%, while reported PAT grew 5%, or about 9.8% after adjusting for the prior-year HDB Financial Services transaction gain and other one-offs.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: Q1 FY2027 comparison
| Metric | HDFC Bank | ICICI Bank | Current Edge | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Market capitalisation | ₹12.56 lakh Cr | ₹10.16 lakh Cr | HDFC Bank | 
| Q1 FY27 PAT | ₹19,060 Cr | ₹14,805 Cr | HDFC on absolute profit | 
| Reported PAT growth YoY | 5.0% | 15.9% | ICICI Bank | 
| Adjusted HDFC PAT growth | ~9.8% | 15.9% reported | ICICI Bank | 
| Net interest income | ₹33,535 Cr | ₹24,384 Cr | HDFC on scale | 
| NII growth YoY | 6.7% | 12.7% | ICICI Bank | 
| Net interest margin | 3.26% total assets; 3.40% interest-earning assets | 4.36% | ICICI Bank | 
| Gross advances / loan portfolio | ₹30.61 lakh Cr | ₹16.31 lakh Cr | HDFC Bank on scale | 
| Loan growth YoY | 15.4% gross advances | 19.6% | ICICI Bank | 
| Period-end deposits | ₹31.71 lakh Cr | ₹18.34 lakh Cr | HDFC Bank on scale | 
| Deposit growth YoY | 14.7% | 14.0% | HDFC Bank slightly | 
| CASA ratio | 32.3% period-end | 38.1% average | Not perfectly like-for-like | 
| Gross NPA ratio | 1.17% | 1.38% | HDFC Bank | 
| Net NPA ratio | 0.41% | 0.35% | ICICI Bank | 
| Capital adequacy | 19.6% | 16.84% | HDFC Bank | 
| CET-1 | 17.4% | 16.19% | HDFC Bank | 
| Branches | 9,694 | 7,608 | HDFC Bank | 
| ATMs / cash recyclers | 20,958 ATMs | 12,190 ATMs & cash recyclers | HDFC Bank on physical reach | 
Why HDFC Bank is still India's bigger private-bank franchise
HDFC Bank's biggest advantage is not one quarterly ratio. It is the sheer depth of its deposit, lending and distribution network.
At 30 June 2026, HDFC Bank reported period-end deposits of roughly ₹31.71 lakh crore. ICICI Bank reported approximately ₹18.34 lakh crore.
HDFC Bank's gross advances stood at approximately ₹30.61 lakh crore, compared with ICICI's ₹16.31 lakh crore loan portfolio.
HDFC also operated 9,694 branches and 20,958 ATMs across 4,175 cities and towns. Half of its branches were in semi-urban and rural locations.
ICICI Bank had 7,608 branches and 12,190 ATMs and cash recycling machines.
This difference matters because a broad deposit franchise can become a funding advantage when loan demand strengthens and deposit competition becomes intense.
ICICI Bank's biggest advantage today is margin
ICICI Bank's 4.36% Q1 FY2027 NIM is materially above HDFC Bank's current margin.
ICICI's margin was also slightly higher than its 4.32% Q4 FY2026 reading and close to its 4.34% margin in Q1 FY2026.
HDFC Bank's NIM was 3.26% on total assets and 3.40% based on interest-earning assets.
That difference is not cosmetic. For banks, NIM is one of the clearest measures of the spread earned between interest-bearing assets and funding costs.
HDFC Bank's post-merger balance sheet remains unusually large and its funding mix continues to normalise. ICICI's cleaner margin profile is one reason its recent earnings growth looks stronger.
Which bank is growing loans faster?
ICICI Bank currently has the faster loan-growth rate.
ICICI's total advances grew 19.6% year on year to ₹16.31 lakh crore at 30 June 2026.
Its business banking portfolio grew 28.2%, rural loans grew 35.4%, domestic corporate loans grew 18.5% and retail loans grew 12%.
HDFC Bank's gross advances grew 15.4% year on year to approximately ₹30.61 lakh crore.
Within HDFC's book, retail loans grew 7.2%, small and mid-market enterprise loans grew 18.7%, and corporate and other wholesale loans grew 18.6%.
HDFC is adding a much larger absolute amount of lending because its base is larger. ICICI is growing faster in percentage terms.
Which has the stronger deposit franchise?
HDFC Bank has the larger deposit franchise; ICICI currently has the higher reported CASA ratio, although the disclosed ratios use different averaging conventions.
HDFC's period-end deposits grew 14.7% year on year to ₹31.71 lakh crore.
ICICI's period-end deposits grew 14% to ₹18.34 lakh crore.
HDFC's period-end CASA ratio was 32.3%.
ICICI reported an average CASA ratio of 38.1% for Q1 FY2027.
Because one is a period-end figure and the other an average figure, they should not be treated as a perfectly like-for-like comparison. The direction is still useful: ICICI currently has a richer low-cost deposit mix, while HDFC has the much larger absolute deposit pool.
Which bank has better asset quality?
Neither wins every asset-quality measure.
HDFC Bank's gross NPA ratio was 1.17% at 30 June 2026. ICICI Bank's was 1.38%.
On gross NPAs, HDFC is better.
HDFC's net NPA ratio was 0.41%. ICICI's was 0.35%.
On net NPAs, ICICI is better.
The distinction matters because gross NPAs show the overall stock of problem loans, while net NPAs reflect the residual after provisions.
ICICI also reported a 74.7% provisioning coverage ratio on non-performing loans.
Both private banks are operating with asset-quality ratios that are dramatically cleaner than the stressed-bank conditions Indian investors saw in earlier credit cycles.
Profit growth currently favours ICICI Bank
ICICI Bank delivered the stronger headline earnings growth in Q1 FY2027.
ICICI's standalone PAT increased 15.9% year on year to ₹14,805 crore.
Its core operating profit rose 15.6% to ₹20,235 crore. Excluding dividends from subsidiaries, core operating profit grew 18.3%.
HDFC Bank reported PAT of ₹19,060 crore, up 5% year on year.
That headline comparison is distorted by the prior-year period, when HDFC Bank booked a large transaction gain from the partial divestment of HDB Financial Services through its IPO.
HDFC stated that PAT growth was approximately 9.8% after adjusting for prior-year transaction gains, one-off provisions and tax credits.
Even after that adjustment, ICICI's reported 15.9% growth remains stronger.
HDFC Bank still produces much more absolute profit
ICICI is growing faster, but HDFC remains the larger earnings machine.
Q1 FY2027 standalone PAT was ₹19,060 crore for HDFC Bank compared with ₹14,805 crore for ICICI Bank.
HDFC's net interest income was ₹33,535 crore. ICICI's was ₹24,384 crore.
For investors, this is the classic scale versus growth-rate distinction.
A smaller bank can grow faster for longer. A larger bank can create more absolute profit while growing at a lower percentage rate.
Which bank has the stronger capital buffer?
HDFC Bank currently has the stronger capital ratios.
HDFC's total capital adequacy ratio stood at 19.6% at 30 June 2026, with Tier 1 at 17.8% and CET-1 at 17.4%.
ICICI Bank reported total capital adequacy of 16.84% and CET-1 of 16.19%.
Both are comfortably above minimum regulatory requirements.
HDFC's larger buffer provides more room to absorb credit losses or support balance-sheet growth without immediate capital raising.
What does Bull Run's market data say?
ICICI Bank has been far stronger in market performance over the latest year.
| Market Metric | HDFC Bank | ICICI Bank | 
|---|---|---|
| Current price | ₹727.50 | ₹1,422.70 | 
| Market capitalisation | ₹12.56 lakh Cr | ₹10.16 lakh Cr | 
| 1-month return | -2.06% | -0.71% | 
| 3-month return | -4.11% | +11.79% | 
| 6-month return | -19.04% | +1.27% | 
| 1-year return | -25.92% | -0.73% | 
| Distance from 52-week high | -28.71% | -3.87% | 
| Dividend yield | 1.59% | 0.78% | 
| FII holding | 41.82% | 34.48% | 
| DII holding | 41.75% | 39.94% | 
| Bull Run Score | 38.4/100 | 42.3/100 | 
HDFC's current price is close to its 52-week low in Bull Run's snapshot, while ICICI is trading within roughly 4% of its 52-week high.
This does not mean ICICI must continue outperforming. It shows where market expectations currently sit.
Why HDFC Bank's current share-price weakness cannot be interpreted like a normal "cheap stock" signal
A large drawdown is not enough to establish bank valuation.
HDFC Bank's price is approximately 28.7% below its 52-week high in the current Bull Run data, while ICICI Bank is only around 3.9% below its high.
The market is clearly assigning more confidence to ICICI's current earnings trajectory.
For HDFC, investors need to ask whether post-merger deposit growth, loan growth and margins are normalising quickly enough to restore the bank's historical earnings profile.
Simply arguing that HDFC is "down more" is not a banking thesis.
The HDFC Bank case in one sentence
HDFC Bank offers extraordinary scale, a huge distribution franchise, strong capitalisation and the larger absolute profit pool, but current margins and earnings growth are less impressive than ICICI Bank's.
What works
- ₹31.71 lakh crore deposit base.
- ₹30.61 lakh crore gross advances.
- 19.6% capital adequacy.
- 17.4% CET-1.
- Lower gross NPA ratio than ICICI.
- 9,694-branch distribution network.
- Higher absolute PAT and NII.
What needs improvement
- NIM at 3.26% on total assets.
- Reported PAT growth only 5%.
- Retail loan growth only 7.2%.
- Net NPA ratio rose sequentially to 0.41%.
- Share-price performance remains weak.
What to monitor
- Deposit growth versus loan growth.
- CASA mix.
- Post-merger NIM normalisation.
- Retail credit acceleration.
- Asset-quality stability.
The ICICI Bank case in one sentence
ICICI Bank currently combines faster loan growth, stronger PAT growth, a 4.36% NIM and low net NPAs, but operates from a smaller balance sheet and has a lower capital buffer than HDFC Bank.
What works
- 19.6% loan growth.
- 15.9% PAT growth.
- 12.7% NII growth.
- 4.36% NIM.
- 0.35% net NPA ratio.
- Strong growth in business banking and rural loans.
- Recent share-price resilience.
What deserves attention
- Gross NPA ratio of 1.38% is above HDFC's.
- Capital adequacy below HDFC's, though still strong.
- Deposit base is significantly smaller.
- Strong valuation expectations can reduce room for disappointment.
What to monitor
- Whether NIM stays above 4%.
- Credit costs as loan growth stays high.
- Rural and business banking asset quality.
- Deposit growth relative to advances.
- Provisioning coverage and NPA additions.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank: which wins each banking metric?
Absolute scale: HDFC Bank.
Deposit franchise size: HDFC Bank.
Loan-book size: HDFC Bank.
Branch network: HDFC Bank.
Capital adequacy: HDFC Bank.
Gross NPA ratio: HDFC Bank.
Net NPA ratio: ICICI Bank.
Net interest margin: ICICI Bank.
Current loan-growth rate: ICICI Bank.
Current PAT-growth rate: ICICI Bank.
Current NII-growth rate: ICICI Bank.
Recent share-price momentum: ICICI Bank.
Dividend yield in Bull Run's current snapshot: HDFC Bank.
Which bank looks stronger for growth?
ICICI Bank currently has the stronger growth profile.
Loan growth is 19.6% versus HDFC's 15.4% gross-advance growth.
NII growth is 12.7% versus HDFC's 6.7%.
PAT growth is 15.9% versus HDFC's reported 5%, or approximately 9.8% on HDFC's adjusted comparison.
ICICI therefore wins the current growth comparison.
The caveat is that HDFC is growing from a much larger base, so even a lower growth rate can add enormous absolute assets and earnings.
Which bank looks safer?
Both are strongly capitalised and have low bad-loan ratios, so "safer" depends on which measure receives more weight.
HDFC Bank has the higher total capital adequacy and CET-1 ratios.
HDFC also has the lower gross NPA ratio.
ICICI has the lower net NPA ratio and a strong provisioning coverage ratio.
Neither current dataset suggests the kind of balance-sheet distress associated with weaker banking cycles.
Why the next few quarters matter more for HDFC Bank
HDFC Bank's investment debate remains centred on post-merger balance-sheet normalisation.
The bank already has scale. It does not need to prove that it can build a national franchise.
It needs to prove that the enlarged franchise can restore stronger margins, improve deposit composition and accelerate profitable credit growth without weakening asset quality.
That is a different problem from ICICI's. ICICI's challenge is sustaining an already strong operating trajectory without letting rapid credit growth create future stress.
Why ICICI Bank's current momentum is not just a stock-price story
ICICI's relative market performance is supported by operating numbers rather than technical momentum alone.
Its NIM is stronger. Loan growth is faster. PAT growth is faster. NII growth is faster. Net NPAs are lower.
That does not guarantee future outperformance, but it explains why the stock is much closer to its 52-week high than HDFC Bank.
The market is currently rewarding operating momentum.
Final verdict: HDFC Bank or ICICI Bank?
HDFC Bank is the stronger scale franchise. ICICI Bank is the stronger current operating story.
If the comparison is based on deposits, advances, physical distribution, total capital and absolute profit, HDFC wins.
If the comparison is based on NIM, loan growth, NII growth, PAT growth and net NPAs, ICICI wins.
The important question for an investor is not which bank has the more famous brand. It is which set of economics is more likely to improve from today's level.
HDFC's upside case depends on normalisation. ICICI's depends on durability.
That distinction is more useful than calling one bank permanently superior to the other.
HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank FAQs
Which bank is bigger?
HDFC Bank. It has the larger market capitalisation, deposit base, loan book and branch network.
Which bank has better NIM?
ICICI Bank. Q1 FY2027 NIM was 4.36%, while HDFC reported 3.26% on total assets and 3.40% based on interest-earning assets.
Which bank has lower gross NPAs?
HDFC Bank. Gross NPAs were 1.17% versus 1.38% for ICICI Bank.
Which bank has lower net NPAs?
ICICI Bank. Net NPAs were 0.35% versus 0.41% for HDFC Bank.
Which bank is growing loans faster?
ICICI Bank. Its total loan portfolio grew 19.6% year on year, versus 15.4% growth in HDFC Bank's gross advances.
Which bank has better capital adequacy?
HDFC Bank. Its total CAR was 19.6% compared with ICICI Bank at 16.84%.
Which bank has performed better in the stock market over the last year?
ICICI Bank. Bull Run's 25 August 2026 snapshot shows ICICI down only about 0.7% over one year, while HDFC Bank is down about 25.9%.
Does HDFC Bank have promoter holding?
No identified promoter is reported following the HDFC Limited merger. HDFC Bank describes itself as a professionally managed organisation without an identified promoter.

Disclaimer
This comparison is educational and informational only. Banking metrics are based primarily on HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank disclosures for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with market and ownership data from Bull Run's available 25 August 2026 snapshot. Bank ratios require different interpretation from industrial-company ratios. Financial performance, margins, NPAs, capital ratios and market prices change over time. Nothing in this article recommends buying, selling or holding HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank or any other security. Bull Run is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser.

title: The Cloud Titans: Microsoft’s Copilot Backlog Challenges Amazon’s Data Center Re-Acceleration
snippet: Azure is accelerating, Copilot adoption is surging, and Microsoft's commercial backlog sits at $677 billion, yet the stock trails the S&P 500 by a wide margin. Something has to give, and the answer ...
content:
The Cloud Titans: Microsoft’s Copilot Backlog Challenges Amazon’s Data Center Re-Acceleration
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT | MSFT Price Prediction) trades at $531.01, and its latest quarter showed a large signed backlog changing into accelerating Azure revenue just as investors compare it with Amazon’s cloud revival.
Microsoft sells Azure cloud infrastructure, Microsoft 365 and Copilot software, plus Windows and Xbox. It just reported revenue of $92.28 billion, up 18.8%, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.89 against a $4.72 estimate. Azure grew 48%, and commercial remaining performance obligation reached $677 billion.
The competition story belongs to Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN). AWS revenue grew 37% to $42.23 billion, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, on a backlog of $496 billion.
Azure Acceleration and Copilot Usage Point to More Upside
Azure growth has climbed every quarter, from 39% to 48%, and management guided to 49% to 50% in constant currency next quarter. Copilot daily users rose nearly 50% quarter over quarter, and customers with more than 50,000 seats increased over 8x year over year.
The CFO put the constraint simply: “We still have demand that exceeds supply.” At a forward P/E of 27, investors pay a reasonable multiple for a 46.78% operating margin. Jefferies’ Brent Thill said the stock is going higher from here.
A $170 Billion Spending Plan Could Squeeze Returns
Microsoft expects calendar-year capex of about $170 billion, with next quarter exceeding $50 billion. Fiscal 2026 free cash flow fell 6.5%, and roughly three-quarters of spending goes to short-lived CPUs and GPUs (the power, cooling, and networking vendors on the receiving end of that spend are the subject of a free report on seven AI infrastructure stocks that aren’t chipmakers). Microsoft Cloud gross margin slipped to 66%, with about 65% expected next quarter.
Backlog growth is cooling, slowing from 110% to 73%, with the total edging down from $678 billion. Windows OEM and Devices revenue fell 22%, while AWS posted a 39.4% operating margin.
Supply Delays Leave Room for Patience
Some third-party GPU contracts slipped into the second half of the fiscal year, and Microsoft gave no updated Copilot seat total. Management expects consumption billing outside coding to increase more slowly. Key questions are whether Azure hits its guidance and whether operating cash flow keeps pace with capex over the next two quarters.
Wall Street Sees 14% Upside as Shares Trail the S&P 500
Microsoft trades at $531.01 against an average target of $605.12, meaning about 14% upside. Targets are estimates and can change. Among 55 analysts:
- Strong Buy: 14
- Buy: 39
- Hold: 2
- Sell: 0
Shares are up 10.5% year to date versus 13.27% for the S&P 500, and down 1.23% over one year while the index gained 12.42%. Amazon trades at $254.60, with a $332.24 target meaning about 30% upside.
Backlog Conversion Puts Azure at the Center of Microsoft’s Outlook
At $531.01, Microsoft’s outlook rests on Azure.
The path higher runs through Azure. If growth reaches the guided 49% to 50% while new capacity comes online, the backlog keeps turning into reported sales. About 30% of that backlog should become revenue within 12 months.
The one-year lag versus the S&P 500 may reflect investor concern over capex. CNBC reported capex came in below expectations, which eases the spending concern. Amazon’s 2026 cash capex estimate of about $220 billion is larger, and its trailing free cash flow is negative at -$7.6 billion.
Azure missing guidance or cloud margins falling below the 65% target would weaken the outlook. Microsoft’s $677 billion commercial backlog gives investors a concrete measure of AI demand.

title: Amazon Climbs 5% as Upgrade Fuels Post-Earnings Rebound on AWS Strength; Walmart Rises 2%, Alphabet Edges Higher
snippet: Amazon just bounced hard off earnings that missed estimates, but the debate tearing Wall Street apart has nothing to do with the quarter itself. The real question is whether AWS profits can keep pace ...
content:
Amazon Climbs 5% as Upgrade Fuels Post-Earnings Rebound on AWS Strength; Walmart Rises 2%, Alphabet Edges Higher
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Wall Street is warming back up to the cloud story at Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN | AMZN Price Prediction) after a rocky first reaction to its latest quarter. Amazon stock is at $251.77, up 5% in morning trading. That rebound follows the initial reaction to quarterly results that missed expectations. The gain also lifts Amazon stock to a 9% advance year to date.
Phillip Securities upgraded Amazon to Buy from Accumulate on November 2 and raised its price target to $330 from $320. The bulls see the bounce as dip-buying on accelerating Amazon Web Services (AWS) growth and a reassuring outlook, while skeptics keep returning to heavy AI spending and negative free cash flow.
AWS Strength Powers Amazon’s Rebound
Amazon reported Q3 2026 results on October 29, with earnings of $1.89 per share missing the $1.96 consensus estimate. AWS revenue reached $46 billion, and the unit’s operating income came in at $17.8 billion. Against Amazon’s total revenue of $201.9 billion and total operating income of $28.1 billion, AWS delivered the majority of group profit on a much smaller share of sales.
On the earnings call, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy spoke. He said AWS demand remains “exceptionally strong” and pointed to “projected revenue growth rates of over 40% both in 2027 and in 2028.” That outlook came after AWS growth accelerated for the sixth straight quarter to its fastest pace in nearly five years.
Amazon’s Cash Burn Keeps the AI Spending Debate Alive
Amazon’s trailing 12-month free cash flow swung to an outflow of $42.4 billion from an inflow of $14.8 billion a year earlier. A $94.8 billion year-over-year jump in Amazon’s purchases of property and equipment drove most of that swing. The company said the increase primarily reflects AI investments. For 2026, Amazon estimated its capital expenditures (capex) at $220 billion.
Jassy noted on October 29 that the company would spend “meaningfully more” in 2027, without giving a number. JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) analyst Doug Anmuth now projects Amazon capex of $395 billion in 2027 and $476 billion in 2028. Anmuth argued that management’s demand visibility gives Amazon the confidence to “invest even more aggressively in AI compute infrastructure.”
That tension lies at the heart of the Amazon debate. Strong cloud profits are funding an expansion that’s consuming cash faster than the business generates it, and all of that AI buildout has to be powered, cooled, and connected by somebody. We rounded up seven of those suppliers in a free AI infrastructure report.
Walmart and Google Take Different Paths Than Amazon
Amazon’s main retail rival is moving higher as well. Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) stock is up 2% to $126.29. The overlap between the two companies stops at retail and e-commerce, since Walmart doesn’t have a cloud business tied to the AWS story.
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) is posting a smaller gain amid concerns about its own AI spending following its October 28 report. Alphabet stock is up 1% to $283.10. Revenue at Google Cloud grew 103%, but the company’s capex rose 114% and its free cash flow turned negative. The market is rewarding Amazon’s AWS profits even as it keeps ignoring Google’s spending.
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), the closest hyperscaler comparison to AWS, reported 48% Azure revenue growth on October 28. Capex at Microsoft more than doubled in the quarter, and management said “Customer demand continues to exceed available supply.”
How Amazon’s Business Model Sets It Apart
Amazon combines e-commerce, advertising, subscriptions and the AWS cloud, and the current catalyst sits directly in AWS AI infrastructure, whereas Walmart runs a discount-store and grocery operation that leans on its stores as fulfillment hubs.
Google makes most of its money from search and YouTube ads, with Google Cloud as a fast-growing second engine. The closest match to AWS is Microsoft, which pairs enterprise software with Azure and carries no retail exposure.
Amazon’s 2027 Spending Plan Is the Next Big Test
Amazon now must show whether AWS demand keeps pace with a capex budget headed much higher in 2027. Accelerating cloud growth and an AWS backlog of $578 billion that management called well-diversified give bulls reason for confidence. The bear case is that negative free cash flow and rising debt leave Amazon less room for error if AI demand cools.
Beyond Amazon, the week brings the midterm elections and key economic data that could shift risk appetite across mega-cap tech. More clarity on Amazon’s 2027 spending plan may be needed before the AI spending debate settles.
